# Tempo Flow — Backlog v2 (ticket standard v2)

Written 1 Nov 2026 · Branch `docs/source-2026-11-01` · Draft PR #1352 into `integration`.

This is the **v2** backlog: every Tempo Flow ticket written to
[`docs/backlog/TICKET-STANDARD.md`](./TICKET-STANDARD.md) (v2, 1 Nov 2026). It supersedes the earlier
thin-format rewrite (`docs/backlog/BACKLOG.md`, tickets TRW-1001…TRW-1232) and the plan
`docs/backlog/REWRITE-PLAN.md`, both marked superseded and kept for history.

The plan, inventory, chunk layout, conflict list and fold-in map live in
[`docs/backlog/REWRITE-PLAN-v2.md`](./REWRITE-PLAN-v2.md). This file holds the ticket text only.

## How to read a ticket
Every ticket carries: `ID`, `Title`, `Stage`, `Pass`, `Depends`, `Folds-in`, then the 11 `AGENTS.md`
fields (`FOR`, `WHEN`, `WHY`, `GOAL`, `SCOPE`, `MUTATES`, `STEPS`, `DONE`, `EVIDENCE`, `DO NOT`,
`REPORT`) plus `SPEC`, `TESTS` (Given/When/Then), `NUMBERS` (range + source, or `UNKNOWN`),
`GATES`, and `OPEN`. The authority for what each field must contain is `TICKET-STANDARD.md`.

Ticket IDs are `TFV2-0001` upward, one per screen / component / backend function-table-endpoint, in
build order; a unit split in the Opus rewrite keeps its number with a letter (`TFV2-0065a`, `TFV2-0065b`).
Config-lane tickets are `CFG-NNN` (schema, dependencies, test config, CI; built by Amit, CONVENTIONS §18)
and sit in the Groundwork section, before Chunk 1, with TFV2-0000a…d. `Pass` 1 = clunky (every state works); `Pass` 2 = matches v3 tokens/motion exactly.

- **DONE:** `CI=1 bunx playwright test tests/e2e/helpers.spec.ts --reporter=line` → `8 passed`, no failures.
- **EVIDENCE:** the Playwright summary pasted into the PR.

- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0000b / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts, tests/e2e/helpers.spec.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`.
- **SPEC:** Test-only module. Exact API:
  ```ts
  import type { Page } from "@playwright/test";
  export const VIEWPORTS: { readonly mobile: { readonly width: 390; readonly height: 844 }; readonly desktop: { readonly width: 1280; readonly height: 800 } };
  export type HarnessLang = "en" | "he";
  export function harnessUrl(id: string, opts?: { lang?: HarnessLang; theme?: "light" | "dark" }): string; // "/e2e/components/<id>?lang=…&theme=…"
  export function screenUrl(route: string, opts: { state: string; lang?: HarnessLang }): string;     // "<route>?state=…&lang=…"
  /** Opens harnessUrl(id, opts), then waits until the first `section[data-testid^="<id>-"]` is visible (the state sections of CONVENTIONS §13; never the `<output data-testid="<id>-log">`). */
  export function openHarness(page: Page, id: string, opts?: { lang?: HarnessLang; theme?: "light" | "dark" }): Promise<void>;
  export function openScreen(page: Page, route: string, opts: { state: string; lang?: HarnessLang }): Promise<void>;
  export function expectDir(page: Page, lang: HarnessLang): Promise<void>;        // <html dir="rtl" lang="he"> or <html dir="ltr" lang="en">
  /** Collects the text of every `console` message of type "error" and every `pageerror`, except messages matching CONSOLE_NOISE. */
  export const CONSOLE_NOISE = /example\.convex\.cloud|WebSocket/i; // the root layout's ConvexReactClient (apps/web/components/providers/providers.tsx line 9) points at the placeholder https://example.convex.cloud under the Playwright webServer and cannot connect
  export function trackConsoleErrors(page: Page): string[];
  export function expectTargetSize(page: Page, selector: string): Promise<void>; // every visible button, a[href], input, select, textarea, [role=switch|checkbox|radio|tab|option|button] under selector ≥ 24×24
  export function expectMotionBudget(page: Page, selector: string): Promise<void>; // max transition/animation duration ≤ 0.25 s; ≤ 0.001 s under reduced motion (tempo.css sets 0.01ms)
  /** Two page.goto(url) calls; lcpMs = startTime of the LAST largest-contentful-paint entry (throws Error("no LCP entry") when there is none); cls = sum of `value` over layout-shift entries whose hadRecentInput === false. */
  export function measureVitals(page: Page, url: string): Promise<{ lcpMs: number; cls: number }>;
  ```
  `measureVitals` body (write exactly this):
  ```ts
  export async function measureVitals(page: Page, url: string): Promise<{ lcpMs: number; cls: number }> {
    await page.goto(url); // warm-up
    await page.goto(url); // measured
    const result = await page.evaluate(
      () =>
        new Promise<{ lcp: number | null; cls: number }>((resolve) => {
          let lcp: number | null = null;
          let cls = 0;
          new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
            const entries = list.getEntries();
            lcp = entries[entries.length - 1].startTime; // the last largest-contentful-paint entry wins
          }).observe({ type: "largest-contentful-paint", buffered: true });
          new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
            for (const entry of list.getEntries() as Array<PerformanceEntry & { value: number; hadRecentInput: boolean }>) {
              if (entry.hadRecentInput === false) cls += entry.value; // shifts right after input do not count (web.dev CLS)
            }
          }).observe({ type: "layout-shift", buffered: true });
          setTimeout(() => resolve({ lcp, cls }), 1000);
        }),
    );
    if (result.lcp === null) throw new Error("no LCP entry");
    return { lcpMs: result.lcp, cls: result.cls };
  }
  ```
  Failure messages (Playwright `expect` with a message): target size → `"target smaller than 24x24: <tag>#<index> <w>x<h>"`; motion → `"motion over 250ms: <tag> <duration>s"`; reduced motion → `"motion not removed under reduced motion: <tag>"`. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  - Given `harnessUrl("scheduled-job-row", { lang: "he", theme: "dark" })` / Then it equals `"/e2e/components/scheduled-job-row?lang=he&theme=dark"`; and `harnessUrl("x")` equals `"/e2e/components/x"`.
  - Given `screenUrl("/modules", { state: "empty", lang: "en" })` / Then it equals `"/modules?state=empty&lang=en"`.
  - Given `page.setContent('<html dir="rtl" lang="he"><body></body></html>')` / When `expectDir(page, "he")` runs / Then it passes; and `expectDir(page, "en")` throws.
  - Given content with a `<button style="width:40px;height:40px">` / When `expectTargetSize(page, "body")` runs / Then it passes; given a `<button style="width:20px;height:20px;padding:0;border:0">` it throws with a message starting `"target smaller than 24x24"`.
  - Given `page.setContent('<style>div { transition: opacity 120ms; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { div { transition-duration: 0.01ms; } }</style><div>a</div>')` (a stylesheet rule, not an inline `style`, so the reduced-motion rule can override it) / When `expectMotionBudget(page, "body")` runs / Then it passes; given `page.setContent('<style>div { transition: opacity 400ms; }</style><div>a</div>')` / Then it throws with a message starting `"motion over 250ms"`.
  - Given `trackConsoleErrors(page)` then `page.evaluate(() => console.error("boom"))` / Then the returned array equals `["boom"]`; and after `page.evaluate(() => console.error("WebSocket connection to 'wss://example.convex.cloud/api/1.32.0/sync' failed"))` the array still equals `["boom"]` (CONSOLE_NOISE dropped).
  - Given `await page.route("http://helpers.test/", (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: "text/html", body: "<html><body><h1>Hi</h1></body></html>" }))` (no `setContent`; the page is served by the route) / When `const v = await measureVitals(page, "http://helpers.test/")` runs / Then `expect(Number.isFinite(v.lcpMs) && v.lcpMs > 0).toBe(true)` (the `<h1>` is the LCP element) and `expect(v.cls).toBe(0)` (nothing on the page moves).
  - Given `await page.route("http://helpers-empty.test/", (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, contentType: "text/html", body: "<html><body></body></html>" }))` (no content, so no largest-contentful-paint entry) / When and Then, in one line: `await expect(measureVitals(page, "http://helpers-empty.test/")).rejects.toThrow("no LCP entry")`.
- **NUMBERS:** 8 of 8 cases pass. The helper thresholds are the catalogue numbers: target ≥ 24×24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#target-size-minimum); motion ≤ 250 ms (DESIGN.md motion rule; CONVENTIONS §5).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.

  ```ts
  // apps/web/lib/e2e/e2eState.ts
  export const E2E_STATE_PATTERN = /^[a-z][a-z-]{0,23}$/;
  export function parseE2EState(raw: string | null, bypass: boolean): string | null {
    return bypass && raw !== null && E2E_STATE_PATTERN.test(raw) ? raw : null;
  }
  export function isE2EBypass(env: { NODE_ENV?: string; NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS?: string }): boolean {
    return env.NODE_ENV !== "production" && env.NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS === "1";
  }
  // apps/web/lib/e2e/useE2EState.ts ("use client")
  export function useE2EState(): string | null {
    return parseE2EState(useSearchParams().get("state"), isE2EBypass({ NODE_ENV: process.env.NODE_ENV, NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS }));
  }
  ```
  No user-facing copy, no errors thrown.

  - Given `parseE2EState("empty", false)` / Then `null`.
  - Given `parseE2EState(null, true)` / Then `null`.
  - Given `parseE2EState("Empty", true)` and `parseE2EState("<script>", true)` / Then each is `null`.
  - Given `parseE2EState("a".repeat(24), true)` / Then it equals `"a".repeat(24)` (24 characters, the cap, accepted); and `parseE2EState("a".repeat(25), true)` / Then `null` (one over the cap; CONVENTIONS §23.6).
  - Given `isE2EBypass({ NODE_ENV: "development", NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS: "1" })` / Then `true`.
  - Given `isE2EBypass({ NODE_ENV: "production", NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS: "1" })` and `isE2EBypass({ NODE_ENV: "development" })` / Then both `false`.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // apps/mobile/lib/e2e/e2eState.ts
  const STATE_PATTERN = /^[a-z][a-z-]{0,23}$/;
  export function parseE2EMobileState(raw: string | null, enabled: boolean): string | null {
    return enabled && raw !== null && STATE_PATTERN.test(raw) ? raw : null;
  }
  export type TempoGate = "sign-in" | "onboarding" | "render";
  export function tempoGate(input: { isLoading: boolean; isAuthenticated: boolean; hasProfile: boolean; onboardedAt: number | undefined; e2e: boolean }): TempoGate {
    if (input.e2e) return "render";
    if (!input.isLoading && !input.isAuthenticated) return "sign-in";
    if (input.hasProfile && input.onboardedAt === undefined) return "onboarding";
    return "render";
  }
  // apps/mobile/lib/e2e/useE2EMobile.ts
  export function useE2EMobile(): string | null {
    const { state } = useLocalSearchParams<{ state?: string }>();
    return parseE2EMobileState(state ?? null, process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E === "1");
  }
  ```
  No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  - Given `parseE2EMobileState("offline", true)` / Then `"offline"`; and `parseE2EMobileState("offline", false)` / Then `null`.
  - Given `parseE2EMobileState("Bad!", true)` / Then `null`.
  - Given `parseE2EMobileState("a".repeat(24), true)` / Then it equals `"a".repeat(24)` (24 characters, the cap, accepted); and `parseE2EMobileState("a".repeat(25), true)` / Then `null` (one over the cap; CONVENTIONS §23.6).
  - Given `tempoGate({ isLoading: false, isAuthenticated: false, hasProfile: false, onboardedAt: undefined, e2e: false })` / Then `"sign-in"`.
  - Given the same input with `e2e: true` / Then `"render"`.
  - Given `{ isLoading: false, isAuthenticated: true, hasProfile: true, onboardedAt: undefined, e2e: false }` / Then `"onboarding"`.
  - Given `{ isLoading: true, isAuthenticated: false, hasProfile: false, onboardedAt: undefined, e2e: false }` / Then `"render"` (matches today's layout: no redirect while loading).
- **NUMBERS:** 7 of 7 cases pass (exact). State cap: 24 characters (`STATE_PATTERN`), tested at 24 (accepted) and 25 (null) in case 3. No UI number applies (no visible UI).

```ts
  jobs: defineTable({
    userId: v.id("users"),
    cron: v.string(),
    timeZone: v.string(),
    task: v.string(),
    targetPageType: v.union(v.literal("daily"), v.literal("weekly"), v.literal("project"), v.literal("plain")),

    approvedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
    lastRunAt: v.optional(v.number()),
    lastRunResult: v.optional(v.union(v.literal("ok"), v.literal("didnt_finish"))),
    lastRunNoteId: v.optional(v.id("notes")),
    createdAt: v.number(),
    updatedAt: v.number(),
    deletedAt: v.optional(v.number()),
  })
    .index("by_userId", ["userId"])
    .index("by_userId_deletedAt", ["userId", "deletedAt"])
    .index("by_enabled", ["enabled"]),
```

  Readers/writers (tickets that depend on this one): TFV2-0161, TFV2-0250b. `cron` is a 5-field cron string in UTC; `timeZone` is the IANA zone used to show it (TFV2-0250 STEP 3). A job runs only when `enabled === true` and `approvedAt` is set. `targetPageType` uses the `notes.pageType` values a job may write to. No data migration: the table starts empty.

  - Given the schema / When `schema.tables.jobs[" indexes"]()` is read / Then it contains `{ indexDescriptor: "by_enabled", fields: ["enabled"] }`.

- **SPEC:** **Relies on** (existing code, checked in STEP 1 with these greps; a mismatch is `blocked: PATH_DRIFT — <what differs>`): signed out, `useTempoSession()` (`apps/mobile/components/v3/session.ts`) returns `ready: false`, so `OnboardingScreen` (`apps/mobile/app/(auth)/onboarding.tsx` line 86, `if (session.isLoading || !session.ready) {`) renders `<StateLoading label={t("load.label")} rows={3} />`; `StateLoading` (`apps/mobile/components/v3/states.tsx` line 13) renders `<View accessible accessibilityRole="progressbar" accessibilityLabel={label} …>`, which React Native Web outputs as `role="progressbar" aria-label="<label>"`; the onboarding `load.label` is `["Getting things ready", "מכינים הכול"]` (`apps/mobile/lib/v3/strings.ts` line 283); the sign-in screen's heading is the literal Hebrew text `התחבר לחשבון` (`apps/mobile/app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx` line 131). STEP 1 greps: `grep -n 'if (session.isLoading || !session.ready) {' 'apps/mobile/app/(auth)/onboarding.tsx'` → line 86; `grep -n 'accessibilityRole="progressbar" accessibilityLabel={label}' apps/mobile/components/v3/states.tsx` → line 13; `grep -n '"load.label": \["Getting things ready", "מכינים הכול"\]' apps/mobile/lib/v3/strings.ts` → line 283; `grep -n 'התחבר לחשבון' 'apps/mobile/app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx'` → line 131; `grep -n 'export function trackConsoleErrors' tests/e2e/helpers/harness.ts` → 1 line (TFV2-0000b). Behaviour table: signed out on `/onboarding` → today: redirect to `/(auth)/sign-in`; after this ticket: still that redirect, except when `__DEV__ && process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E === "1"`, where the route renders (`<Slot />`). Signed in → unchanged (onboarding, paywall and preview stay reachable; other `(auth)` routes redirect to onboarding or Today). `isLoading` → unchanged (`null`). No new copy. Readers: TFV2-0334.
  Spec code (write exactly this):
  ```ts
  import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
  import { VIEWPORTS, trackConsoleErrors } from "../helpers/harness";

  test.skip(!!process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, "local webServer only");
  const NOISE = /example\.convex\.cloud|WebSocket/i;

  test("signed out /onboarding renders the onboarding screen · mobile · en", async ({ page }) => {
    const errors = trackConsoleErrors(page);
    await page.setViewportSize(VIEWPORTS.mobile);
    await page.goto("/onboarding");
    await page.waitForLoadState("networkidle");
    await expect(page.getByRole("progressbar", { name: "Getting things ready" })).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByText("התחבר לחשבון", { exact: true })).toHaveCount(0);
    expect(new URL(page.url()).pathname).toBe("/onboarding");
    expect(errors.filter((m) => !NOISE.test(m))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("signed out /sign-in still renders sign-in · mobile · en", async ({ page }) => {
    const errors = trackConsoleErrors(page);
    await page.setViewportSize(VIEWPORTS.mobile);
    await page.goto("/sign-in");
    await page.waitForLoadState("networkidle");
    await expect(page.getByText("התחבר לחשבון", { exact: true })).toBeVisible();
    expect(new URL(page.url()).pathname).toBe("/sign-in");
    expect(errors.filter((m) => !NOISE.test(m))).toEqual([]);
  });
  ```
  The URL is read only after a rendered screen has been asserted (a web-first `expect` that waits), so a client-side redirect cannot pass unseen. (once · en · mobile) Given the mobile config (flag on, dev server, signed out) / When `/onboarding` is opened and the network is idle / Then the onboarding screen's `role="progressbar"` named "Getting things ready" is visible, the sign-in heading "התחבר לחשבון" has count 0, the pathname is `/onboarding`, and there are no console errors besides NOISE.
  2. (once · en · mobile) Given the same / When `/sign-in` is opened and the network is idle / Then the sign-in heading "התחבר לחשבון" is visible and the pathname is `/sign-in` (other signed-out `(auth)` routes are unchanged), with no console errors besides NOISE.

  ```rust
  // apps/desktop/src-tauri/build.rs
  fn main() {
      tauri_build::try_build(tauri_build::Attributes::new().app_manifest(tauri_build::AppManifest::new().commands(&[
          "desktop_settings_get", "desktop_settings_set", "desktop_page_cache_put", "desktop_page_cache_list",
          "desktop_page_cache_get", "desktop_page_cache_clear", "desktop_update_status", "desktop_update_restart",
      ]))).expect("failed to run tauri-build");
  }
  // apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs
  #![cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), windows_subsystem = "windows")]
  fn main() { tempo_desktop_lib::run() }
  // apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs
  #[cfg_attr(mobile, tauri::mobile_entry_point)]
  pub fn run() {
      tauri::Builder::default()
          .plugin(tauri_plugin_single_instance::init(|_app, _argv, _cwd| {}))
          .plugin(tauri_plugin_deep_link::init())
          .plugin(tauri_plugin_store::Builder::new().build())
          .plugin(tauri_plugin_autostart::init(tauri_plugin_autostart::MacosLauncher::LaunchAgent, None))
          .plugin(tauri_plugin_updater::Builder::new().build())
          .plugin(tauri_plugin_opener::init())
          .invoke_handler(tauri::generate_handler![])
          .setup(|app| {
              tauri::WebviewWindowBuilder::new(app, "main", tauri::WebviewUrl::App("index.html".into()))
                  .title("Tempo Flow").inner_size(1200.0, 800.0).min_inner_size(800.0, 600.0)
                  .build()?;
              Ok(())
          })
          .run(tauri::generate_context!())
          .expect("error while running Tempo Flow desktop");
  }
  ```

  ```yaml
        - name: cargo clippy
  ```

### CFG-056 — Config: iOS privacy manifest in `apps/mobile/app.json` — config lane: Amit — OPEN
- **STATUS:** open — new: Ship this privacy manifest (four categories with Expo's documented reasons), or first upload a build and declare only what App Store Connect's ITMS-91053 report lists for React Native 0.81 / Expo 54?

- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** PRD §4.11 F-122 (App Store). Apple requires apps and SDKs that call "required reason" APIs to declare them in a privacy manifest, or App Store Connect warns (ITMS-91053) and rejects (Apple docs, "Describing use of required reason API"). Expo writes `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` from `expo.ios.privacyManifests` (Expo docs, "Privacy manifests"). React Native apps commonly use UserDefaults (AsyncStorage), file timestamps, system boot time and disk space; Expo's docs show these four with reasons `CA92.1`, `C617.1`, `35F9.1`, `E174.1`. `app.json` has no `privacyManifests` today.
- **GOAL:** `apps/mobile/app.json` declares the four required-reason API categories with their reasons, proven by its own test.
- **SCOPE:** `apps/mobile/app.json` · test: `tests/unit/mobile_config_cfg056_privacy_manifest.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `apps/mobile/app.json` (edit: `ios.privacyManifests`) · `tests/unit/mobile_config_cfg056_privacy_manifest.test.ts` (new) · iOS build's `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy`.
- **STEPS:** 1) Code-map check: `grep -n "privacyManifests" apps/mobile/app.json` → nothing. 2) Add the SPEC object as `expo.ios.privacyManifests`. 3) Create the test with the 2 TESTS cases. 4) Run DONE.

- **EVIDENCE:** the output of `bun test tests/unit/mobile_config_cfg056_privacy_manifest.test.ts` (DONE); the `bun test` summary lines and the typecheck exit code, pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** declare tracking or tracking domains; declare collected data types here (the App Store privacy answers are TFV2-0434b); change other `ios` keys.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: CFG-056 / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: apps/mobile/app.json, tests/unit/mobile_config_cfg056_privacy_manifest.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync` (AGENTS.md format).
- **SPEC:**
  ```json
  "privacyManifests": {
    "NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes": [
      { "NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType": "NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults", "NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons": ["CA92.1"] },
      { "NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType": "NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp", "NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons": ["C617.1"] },
      { "NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType": "NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategorySystemBootTime", "NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons": ["35F9.1"] },
      { "NSPrivacyAccessedAPIType": "NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryDiskSpace", "NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypeReasons": ["E174.1"] }
    ]
  }
  ```

### TFV2-0001 — Bounded list helper `convex/lib/bounded.ts`
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent
- **Stage:** A · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** #1348 (TM-0032)
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); pure-helper lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** PRD §4.11 F-130 (per-user isolation, bounded reads); REWRITE-PLAN-v2 §6 chunk 1 "bounded queries + resource quotas"; CONVENTIONS §16 "Limits: every list read is bounded (… or `boundedQuery` from TFV2-0001)", §7 H ("Bytes" = UTF-8 length).
- **GOAL:** `convex/lib/bounded.ts` exports `boundedQuery`, a pure function that keeps rows in order until a row-count or UTF-8 byte budget would be exceeded and reports `truncated`, proven by its own test file.
- **SCOPE:** `convex/lib/bounded.ts` · test: `convex/lib/bounded.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `convex/lib/bounded.ts` (new) · `convex/lib/bounded.test.ts` (new). No table, route, env or schema change.
- **STEPS:**
  1. Code-map: `ls convex/lib | grep -i bounded` → no output (the helper does not exist today); `grep -rn "boundedQuery" convex apps packages` → no output (no caller to keep working).
  2. Create `convex/lib/bounded.ts` with exactly the SPEC exports and algorithm. No imports.
  3. Create `convex/lib/bounded.test.ts` (`import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";`) with exactly the 9 TESTS cases.
  4. Run DONE, then `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck`.
- **DONE:** `bun test convex/lib/bounded.test.ts` → `9 pass`, `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** the summary of `bun test convex/lib/bounded.test.ts` pasted into the PR, plus the `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck` exit codes.
- **DO NOT:** change any existing query to call the helper (later tickets do); measure bytes with `string.length` or `JSON.stringify(x).length` alone; sort or skip rows; use `ConvexError` (new modules throw plain `Error`, CONVENTIONS §8); touch `convex/schema.ts`, `convex/auth*`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** AGENTS.md format — `status / ticket: TFV2-0001 / evidence: <DONE command> -> <summary> / changed: convex/lib/bounded.ts, convex/lib/bounded.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 each with its evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export type BoundedOptions = { maxRows: number; maxBytes: number };
  export type BoundedResult<T> = { rows: T[]; truncated: boolean };
  /** UTF-8 byte length of the row's JSON form: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(row)).length. */
  export function rowUtf8Bytes(row: unknown): number;
  export function boundedQuery<T>(rows: readonly T[], opts: BoundedOptions): BoundedResult<T>;
  ```
  - Validation first: `opts.maxRows` must satisfy `Number.isSafeInteger(x) && x >= 0`, else `throw new Error("maxRows must be a non-negative integer")`; then the same for `opts.maxBytes` with `"maxBytes must be a non-negative integer"`.
  - Algorithm: walk `rows` in input order with `kept: T[] = []` and `used = 0`. For each row: if `kept.length === opts.maxRows` → stop with `truncated: true`; let `b = rowUtf8Bytes(row)`; if `used + b > opts.maxBytes` → stop with `truncated: true`; else push the row (same reference) and add `b`. Reaching the end of `rows` returns `truncated: false`. A row that does not fit ends the walk; later smaller rows are never taken.
  - `rowUtf8Bytes(undefined)` treats `JSON.stringify(undefined)` (which is `undefined`) as `"null"` → 4 bytes.
  - The input array is never mutated. No user-facing copy (callers own copy). No database access.
- **TESTS:** (`convex/lib/bounded.test.ts`; `const row = (n: number) => ({ s: "a".repeat(n - 8) })` is a row whose JSON is exactly `n` UTF-8 bytes, because `{"s":""}` is 8 bytes)
  1. Given `rows = []`, `{ maxRows: 10, maxBytes: 1_000 }` / When `boundedQuery` runs / Then it returns `{ rows: [], truncated: false }`.
  2. Given 10 rows `row(100)` and `{ maxRows: 5, maxBytes: 1_000_000 }` / Then `rows.length === 5`, `truncated === true`, and `rows[0]` is the same object as the input's first row (`toBe`).
  3. Given 3 rows `row(100)` and `{ maxRows: 10, maxBytes: 250 }` / Then `rows.length === 2` and `truncated === true`.
  4. Given 2 rows `row(100)` and `{ maxRows: 10, maxBytes: 200 }` / Then `rows.length === 2` and `truncated === false` (an exact fit is not truncated).
  5. Given `[{ s: "שלום" }]` (UTF-16 JSON length 14, UTF-8 length 16) / When `maxBytes` is 15 / Then `{ rows: [], truncated: true }`; when `maxBytes` is 16 / Then one row and `truncated === false`; and `rowUtf8Bytes({ s: "שלום" }) === 16`.
  6. Given `{ maxRows: 0, maxBytes: 100 }` / When rows are `[row(10)]` / Then `{ rows: [], truncated: true }`; when rows are `[]` / Then `{ rows: [], truncated: false }`.
  7. Given `maxRows: -1` and, separately, `maxRows: 1.5` / Then each call throws `"maxRows must be a non-negative integer"`.
  8. Given `maxBytes: Number.NaN` and, separately, `maxBytes: Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` / Then each call throws `"maxBytes must be a non-negative integer"`.
  9. Given `rows = [3, 1, 2]` and `{ maxRows: 10, maxBytes: 100 }` / Then `rows` returned equals `[3, 1, 2]` (input order) and the input array still equals `[3, 1, 2]`.
- **NUMBERS:** 9 of 9 cases pass (exact). Byte counts are exact UTF-8 lengths (TESTS 5; CONVENTIONS §7 H). The helper holds no default budget: each caller names its own exported constant (CONVENTIONS §16). Latency: n/a (pure, in-memory, O(n)).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  import type { AiCallOptions, AiResult } from "./ai_router";
  export const MOCK_MODEL_ID = "mock-model";
  export const MOCK_FALLBACK_REPLY = "Done.";
  export type MockModel = ((opts: AiCallOptions) => Promise<AiResult>) & { readonly calls: readonly AiCallOptions[] };
  export function mockModel(queue: readonly string[]): MockModel;
  ```
  - `mockModel` copies `queue` when called (later changes to the caller's array have no effect).
  - Each call validates `opts.messages`: it must be an array with length ≥ 1 whose every item is an object with `role` in `"system" | "user" | "assistant"` and `typeof content === "string"`. Otherwise the returned promise rejects with `new Error("Bad messages for the mock model")` and the call is not recorded.
  - A valid call is pushed to `calls` (the same `opts` object), then resolves to `{ tier: opts.tier, requestedTier: opts.tier, model: MOCK_MODEL_ID, content, usage: { promptTokens: 0, completionTokens: 0, totalTokens: 0 }, escalated: false }`, where `content` is the next queued reply in order, or `MOCK_FALLBACK_REPLY` once the queue is empty.
  - No user-facing copy; no network, env or database access.
- **TESTS:** (`convex/lib/mockModel.test.ts`; `const msgs = [{ role: "user" as const, content: "hi" }]`)
  1. Given `mockModel(["First", "Second"])` / When called twice with `{ tier: "balanced", messages: msgs }` / Then the results' `content` are `"First"` then `"Second"`.
  2. Given `mockModel([])` / When called once / Then `content === "Done."` and `calls.length === 1`.
  3. Given three queued replies and four calls / Then the fourth `content` is `"Done."`.
  4. Given one call with `opts = { tier: "fast", messages: msgs, maxTokens: 50 }` / Then `calls[0]` is that same object (`toBe`).
  5. Given `mockModel(["x"])` called with tier `"deep"` / Then the result `toEqual`s `{ tier: "deep", requestedTier: "deep", model: "mock-model", content: "x", usage: { promptTokens: 0, completionTokens: 0, totalTokens: 0 }, escalated: false }`.
  6. Given `messages: [{ role: "tool", content: "x" }]` (cast through `unknown`) / Then the promise rejects with `"Bad messages for the mock model"` and `calls.length === 0`.
  7. Given `messages: []` / Then it rejects with `"Bad messages for the mock model"`.
  8. Given `messages: [{ role: "user", content: 5 }]` (cast) / Then it rejects with `"Bad messages for the mock model"`.
  9. Given `const fetchMock = mock(() => { throw new Error("network"); }); globalThis.fetch = fetchMock as unknown as typeof fetch;` (the original saved in `const originalFetch = globalThis.fetch;` at the top of the file and restored in `afterEach(() => { globalThis.fetch = originalFetch; })`) / When the mock model is called / Then `fetchMock` was called 0 times (`expect(fetchMock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(0)`).
  10. Given `const q = ["a"]; const m = mockModel(q); q.push("b");` / When `m` is called twice / Then the contents are `"a"` then `"Done."`; and inside this test `const asSeam: typeof callLLM = mockModel([]);` (with `import type { callLLM } from "./ai_router"` at the top of the file) is followed by `expect(typeof asSeam).toBe("function");`.

### TFV2-0003 — Anti-shaming word check `convex/lib/shameWords.ts`
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent

- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); pure-helper lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.

- **GOAL:** `convex/lib/shameWords.ts` exports the canonical EN and HE shaming terms and `containsShame(text)`, which reports every canonical term found, proven by its own test file.
- **SCOPE:** `convex/lib/shameWords.ts` · test: `convex/lib/shameWords.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `convex/lib/shameWords.ts` (new) · `convex/lib/shameWords.test.ts` (new). No table, route, env or schema change.
- **STEPS:**
  1. Code-map: `ls convex/lib | grep -i shame` → no output (CONVENTIONS §12 names the file; it does not exist yet); `grep -n "CRISIS_PHRASES" convex/lib/crisisWords.ts` (style reference only; do not edit).
  2. Create `convex/lib/shameWords.ts` as in SPEC. No imports.
  3. Create `convex/lib/shameWords.test.ts` with exactly the 12 TESTS cases.
  4. Run DONE, then `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck`.
- **DONE:** `bun test convex/lib/shameWords.test.ts` → `12 pass`, `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** the summary of `bun test convex/lib/shameWords.test.ts` pasted into the PR, plus the `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck` exit codes.
- **DO NOT:** add, remove or reword a term (the list is CONVENTIONS §12's, exactly); return or log the input text; wire the check into any caller (later tickets); touch `convex/schema.ts`, `convex/auth*`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** AGENTS.md format — `status / ticket: TFV2-0003 / evidence / changed: convex/lib/shameWords.ts, convex/lib/shameWords.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 each with its evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const SHAME_TERMS_EN: readonly string[] = ["failed", "overdue", "lazy", "must", "should have", "streak lost", "you never"];
  export const SHAME_TERMS_HE: readonly string[] = ["נכשל", "איחרת", "עצלן", "חייב", "היית צריך"];
  export type ShameCheck = { found: boolean; matches: string[] };
  export function containsShame(text: string): ShameCheck;
  ```
  - Both arrays are `Object.freeze`d.
  - EN matching: for each term build once, at module load, `new RegExp(\`(?<![\\p{L}\\p{N}])${term.split(" ").join("\\s+")}(?![\\p{L}\\p{N}])\`, "iu")` — case-insensitive, whole word (no letter or digit on either side), any run of whitespace between the words of a phrase.
  - HE matching: plain substring (`text.includes(term)`), so prefixed and inflected forms ("ונכשלתי") are flagged; over-flagging is allowed, under-flagging is not.
  - `matches` lists the canonical terms that matched (never the input text), each once, in order: every EN term in `SHAME_TERMS_EN` order, then every HE term in `SHAME_TERMS_HE` order. `found === matches.length > 0`. The input is not modified. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `"You failed to finish it."` / Then `{ found: true, matches: ["failed"] }`.
  2. Given `"The task is overdue by a day."` / Then `matches` equals `["overdue"]`.
  3. Given `"Must do the dishes"` / Then `matches` equals `["must"]` (case-insensitive).
  4. Given `"Pass the mustard"` / Then `{ found: false, matches: [] }` (whole word).
  5. Given `"I should   have called"` (three spaces) / Then `matches` equals `["should have"]`.
  6. Given `"You never call"` / Then `matches` equals `["you never"]`.
  7. Given `"איחרת עם המשימה."` / Then `matches` equals `["איחרת"]`.
  8. Given `"ונכשלתי שוב"` / Then `matches` equals `["נכשל"]` (substring for Hebrew).
  9. Given `"Write the plan for Monday."` / Then `{ found: false, matches: [] }`.
  10. Given `"failed and failed again"` / Then `matches` equals `["failed"]` (deduplicated).
  11. Given `"You must, it is overdue"` / Then `matches` equals `["overdue", "must"]` (canonical order, not text order).
  12. Given each term `t` of `SHAME_TERMS_EN` and `SHAME_TERMS_HE` in a loop / When `containsShame(t)` runs / Then `matches` contains `t` (recall 100%); and `containsShame("")` is `{ found: false, matches: [] }`.
- **NUMBERS:** recall on the canonical list = 100% (TESTS 12; source: PRD §13 + CONVENTIONS §12). Precision: not a gate (over-flagging allowed by design). 12 of 12 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

  ```ts
  export const undo = mutation({
    args: { noteId: v.id("notes"), targetOperationId: v.id("pageOperations"), requestId: v.string() },
    returns: pageWriteResult,
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { noteId: Id<"notes">; targetOperationId: Id<"pageOperations">; requestId: string }): Promise<PageWriteResult> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Handler order:
  1. `user = await requireUser(ctx)`; `note = await loadOwnedLiveNote(ctx, user._id, args.noteId)`.
  2. `target = await ctx.db.get(args.targetOperationId)`; if `!target || target.userId !== user._id || target.noteId !== args.noteId || target.deletedAt !== undefined` → `throw new Error("Change not found")`.
  3. `requestDigest = unwrap(await computePageRequestDigest({ kind: "undo", noteId: args.noteId, targetOperationId: args.targetOperationId }))`; `nowMs = Date.now()`; `replay = await admitPageRequest(…)` → return `toWriteResult(replay)`.
  4. `decision = unwrap(decideUndoRequest({ nowMs, target }))`; if `decision.decision === "already_undone"` → return `toWriteResult((await ctx.db.get(decision.undoOperationId as Id<"pageOperations">))!)` (no write).
  5. `payload = await ctx.db.query("pageOperationPayloads").withIndex("by_userId_operationId", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).eq("operationId", target._id)).first()`.
  6. `intervening = await ctx.db.query("pageOperations").withIndex("by_userId_noteId_affectsBody_resultRevision", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).eq("noteId", args.noteId).eq("affectsBody", true).gte("resultRevision", target.resultRevision + 1)).take(PAGE_LEDGER_LIMITS.maxInterveningRevisions + 1)`.
  7. `plan = unwrap(await planUndo({ nowMs, userId: user._id, noteId: args.noteId, noteRevision: note.revision, currentBody: note.body, target: { operation: target, payload: payload ?? undefined }, intervening }))` (`planUndo` types `target` as `{ operation: unknown; payload: unknown }` and drops an `undefined` payload).
  8. `facts = unwrap(buildOperationFacts({ userId: user._id, noteId: args.noteId, requestId: args.requestId, requestDigest, kind: "undo", source: "ui", change: plan.facts, nowMs, undoOfOperationId: target._id }))`; `undoId = await ctx.db.insert("pageOperations", facts)`.
  9. `marked = unwrap(markOperationUndone({ target, undoOperationId: undoId, nowMs }))`; `await ctx.db.patch(target._id, { undoneAtMs: marked.undoneAtMs, undoneByOperationId: marked.undoneByOperationId, updatedAt: marked.updatedAt })`.
  10. `await ctx.db.patch(args.noteId, { body: plan.candidateBody, revision: plan.facts.resultRevision, updatedAt: nowMs })`; `await rebuildNoteBlocks(ctx, user._id, args.noteId, plan.candidateBody, nowMs)`.
  11. Return `toWriteResult` of the undo row (an `undo` receipt has no window of its own, so `undoUntilMs: null`).
  Errors (exact message · trigger · test):
  | message | trigger | TESTS |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Not authenticated` | no identity | 7 |
  | `Note not found` | note owned by another user | 8 |
  | `Change not found` | target belongs to another note of the same user | 9 |
  | `Undo window has passed` | `now >= undoUntilMs` | 4 |
  | `Undo conflicts with a later edit` | a later edit overlaps the target's inserted text | 3 |
  | `Page write rejected: undo_not_undoable` | target is a `noop` receipt | 10 |

  ```ts

  const task = (n: number) => fence(JSON.stringify({ id: id(n), v: 1, type: "task", data: { title: `t${n}`, durationMin: 5, status: "later", order: n, inelastic: false } }));
  ```
   `const saveAs = (body: string, expectedRevision: number, tail: string) => runHandler(notes.save, ctx, { noteId, expectedRevision, body, requestId: reqId(Date.now(), tail) })`)
  1. Given a save `"Hello"` → `"Hello world"` (operation T) / When `undo({ noteId, targetOperationId: T, requestId: reqId(Date.now(), "0000000000000009") })` runs / Then the note body is `"Hello"` and `revision 2`; the result has `revision 2`, `result "applied"`, `undoUntilMs null`; the new `pageOperations` row has `kind "undo"` and `undoOfOperationId T`; row T has `undoneByOperationId` equal to the new id and a numeric `undoneAtMs`.
  2. Given saves `"A\nB"` (seeded body) → `"A\nB\nC"` (T) → `"Z\nB\nC"` / When T is undone / Then the body is `"Z\nB"` (the later edit survives) and `revision 3`.
  3. Given saves `"Hello"` → `"Hello world"` (T) → `"Hello there"` / When T is undone / Then it rejects with `"Undo conflicts with a later edit"` and the body is still `"Hello there"`.
  4. Given a save at time `t0` (T) and `setSystemTime(new Date(t0 + 300_000))` / When T is undone / Then it rejects with `"Undo window has passed"`.
  5. Given T undone once / When `undo` runs again with a different `requestId` / Then it returns the first undo's `operationId`, the body and `revision` are unchanged, and there is exactly one `kind "undo"` row.
  6. Given `undo` run twice with the same `requestId` / Then both results are deep-equal and there is exactly one `kind "undo"` row.
  7. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / Then `undo` rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  8. Given a note of `"users:2"` / When user 1 calls `undo` on it / Then it rejects with `"Note not found"`.
  9. Given T on note 1 and a second note 2 of the same user / When `undo({ noteId: note2, targetOperationId: T, … })` runs / Then it rejects with `"Change not found"`.
  10. Given a `noop` save receipt N (body unchanged) / When N is undone / Then it rejects with `"Page write rejected: undo_not_undoable"`.
  11. Given `saveAs("Hello\n" + task(1), 0, "0000000000000000")` (T) / Then the page has 1 `noteBlocks` row (`ctx.db.query("noteBlocks").withIndex("by_userId_noteId_deletedAt_position", (q) => q.eq("userId", "users:1").eq("noteId", noteId).eq("deletedAt", undefined)).take(1000)`); When T is undone / Then the body is `"Hello"` and the same read returns 0 rows.
- **NUMBERS:** Undo window 300,000 ms, half-open (`PAGE_LEDGER_TIMING.undoWindowMs`, PRD F-131; TESTS 4); intervening revisions read ≤ 257 (`PAGE_LEDGER_LIMITS.maxInterveningRevisions` 256 + 1; bounded read). Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline; not a gate).

### TFV2-0020a — Hebrew voice detector `apps/web/lib/heVoice.ts`
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent

- **GOAL:** `apps/web/lib/heVoice.ts` exports `GENDERED_HE_FORMS` and `findGenderedHebrew(text)`, which returns every listed gendered second-person form found as a whole Hebrew word, proven by its own test file.

- **MUTATES:** `apps/web/lib/heVoice.ts` (new) · `apps/web/lib/heVoice.test.ts` (new). No copy, route or data change.
- **STEPS:**
  1. Code-map: `ls apps/web/lib | grep -i voice` → no `heVoice*` file today.
  2. Create `apps/web/lib/heVoice.ts` as in SPEC (no imports).
  3. Create `apps/web/lib/heVoice.test.ts` with exactly the 8 TESTS cases.
  4. Run DONE, then `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck`.
- **DONE:** `bun test apps/web/lib/heVoice.test.ts` → `8 pass`, `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** the summary of `bun test apps/web/lib/heVoice.test.ts` pasted into the PR, plus the exit codes of `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck`.
- **DO NOT:** edit any copy file (`apps/web/lib/i18n.ts`, `apps/web/lib/i18n-groups/*` — that is TFV2-0020b); run the detector over `MESSAGES` in a test (it would fail until the sweep lands); add or remove a form from the SPEC list; touch `convex/**`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** AGENTS.md format — `status / ticket: TFV2-0020a / evidence / changed: apps/web/lib/heVoice.ts, apps/web/lib/heVoice.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 each with its evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  /** Gendered second-person forms CONVENTIONS §12 forbids in Hebrew UI copy (feminine, then masculine). */
  export const GENDERED_HE_FORMS: readonly string[] = Object.freeze([
    "לחצי", "תלחצי", "בחרי", "תבחרי", "הקלידי", "כתבי", "תכתבי", "נסי", "תנסי", "שמרי", "הוסיפי", "תוסיפי",
    "בקשי", "העתיקי", "תרשמי", "תחזרי", "כשתחזרי", "תוכלי", "תרצי", "מוכנה", "את צריכה",
    "תלחץ", "תבחר", "תכתוב", "תנסה", "תוסיף", "תחזור", "כשתחזור", "תוכל", "תרצה", "אתה", "מוכן/ה",
  ]);
  /** Every listed form found as a whole word (no Hebrew letter immediately before or after), deduplicated, in list order. */
  export function findGenderedHebrew(text: string): string[];
  ```
  Matching: for each form `f`, `new RegExp(\`(?<![\\u05D0-\\u05EA])${escapeRegExp(f)}(?![\\u05D0-\\u05EA])\`, "u")` where `const escapeRegExp = (s: string): string => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\/]/g, "\\$&");` (a module-private helper; it escapes `/` and every regex syntax character); forms are compiled once at module load. A form glued to a one-letter prefix (ש, כש, ו, ה, ל, ב) is not matched unless the list holds the prefixed form itself (`כשתחזרי`, `כשתחזור`). Pure; no errors thrown; no user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `"נסי שוב"` / Then `["נסי"]`.
  2. Given `"תרשמי מה שקרה"` / Then `["תרשמי"]`.
  3. Given `"מנסים שוב"` (contains the letters נסי inside a word) / Then `[]`.
  4. Given `"לנסות שוב"` / Then `[]` (the §12 infinitive voice passes).
  5. Given `"אם אתה מוכן/ה"` / Then `["אתה", "מוכן/ה"]` (list order).
  6. Given `"נסי, נסי"` / Then `["נסי"]` (deduplicated).
  7. Given `"Try again"` and `""` / Then each returns `[]`.
  8. Given each form `f` of `GENDERED_HE_FORMS` in a loop / When `findGenderedHebrew(\`(${f})\`)` runs / Then the result contains `f` (recall 100%).
- **NUMBERS:** recall on the listed forms = 100% (TESTS 8); 8 of 8 pass. Latency: n/a (pure).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.

- **SPEC:** Behaviour under test (existing code):

  - Desktop 1280×800: rail width 264 px (`--tp-rail-w`) ±1, docked (not `inert`); top bar height ≥ 56 px (`--tp-topbar-h`); tab bar not visible (`.tp-tabbar { display: none }` above 767 px); `data-rail="closed"`, `data-coach="closed"`.
  - Mobile 390×844: rail has the `inert` attribute and lies fully outside the viewport (EN: its right edge ≤ 0; HE: its left edge ≥ 390, because `[dir="rtl"] .tp-rail { transform: translateX(100%) }`); tab bar visible with height ≥ 64 px (`--tp-tabbar-h`); `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390` (no sideways scroll).
  - Direction: in HE the docked rail's box is to the right of `main` (logical properties); in EN to the left.
  - Drawer (mobile): clicking the opener sets `data-rail="open"`, the opener's `aria-expanded="true"`, removes `inert` from the rail and moves focus inside the rail; Escape sets `data-rail="closed"` and returns focus to the opener.
  - Motion: below 1024 px `.tp-rail` has `transition: transform var(--tp-dur-slow) var(--tp-ease-out)` (240 ms) ≤ 250 ms; reduced motion collapses it (tempo.css `0.01ms` rule). The motion check is scoped to `.tp-rail`.
  - **Relies on** (checked in STEP 1): `html, body { margin: 0; padding: 0; }` (`apps/web/app/tempo.css` line 57), so the shell spans the full viewport; `.tp-tabbar { display: none; }` (line 460); inside `@media (max-width: 1023px)` (line 497): `.tp-rail { position: fixed; inset-block: 0; inset-inline-start: 0; z-index: 40; width: min(var(--tp-rail-w), 86vw); transform: translateX(-100%); transition: transform var(--tp-dur-slow) var(--tp-ease-out); box-shadow: var(--tp-shadow-modal); }` (line 500; at 390 px the width is 264 px), `[dir="rtl"] .tp-rail { transform: translateX(100%); }` (line 501), `.tp-topbar__menu { display: inline-flex; }` (line 504); `TempoShell.tsx` passes `inert={(narrow && !railOpen) || coachModal}` to `Sidebar` (line 305) and on drawer open focuses `[data-component="Sidebar"] [data-component="CommandTrigger"]` (line 124); the opener is `header[data-component="Topbar"] .tp-topbar__menu` with `aria-expanded={railOpen}` (`Topbar.tsx` lines 41–44); i18n keys `skip` (EN "Skip to page" / HE "דלגו לדף"), `top.menu` ("Open pages" / "פתיחת הדפים"), `rail.label` ("Pages" / "דפים"), `tab.label` ("Main" / "ראשי") in `apps/web/lib/i18n.ts`.
  - States: `default` (docked), `drawer-closed`, `drawer-open`, RTL. `loading`, `empty`, `error`, `offline`, `success`, `disabled`: n/a for the shell — each slot's content owns them.
- **TESTS:** (numbered; §22 spec skeleton as STEP 2 states)
  1. (loop) Given the viewport and `lang` / Then `expectDir(page, lang)` passes, `a.tp-skip` has the SPEC text for `lang`, and the viewport's SPEC geometry holds (desktop: rail 264±1 px wide, not inert, top bar ≥ 56 px tall, tab bar hidden, rail box left of `main#main` in EN / right of it in HE; mobile: rail has `inert` and lies off-screen on the leading side (EN right edge ≤ 0, HE left edge ≥ 390), tab bar visible and ≥ 64 px tall, `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= 390`).
  2. (once · en · mobile) Given the page / When the opener (`aria-label` "Open pages") is clicked / Then the shell has `data-rail="open"`, the opener `aria-expanded="true"`, the rail has no `inert`, and `document.activeElement` is inside the rail; When Escape is pressed / Then `data-rail="closed"` and the opener is focused.
  3. (once · he · mobile) Given the page / When the opener (`aria-label` "פתיחת הדפים") is clicked / Then the shell has `data-rail="open"`, the opener `aria-expanded="true"`, the rail has no `inert`, and `document.activeElement` is inside the rail; When Escape is pressed / Then `data-rail="closed"` and the opener is focused.
  4. (once · en · mobile) When `expectMotionBudget(page, ".tp-rail")` runs / Then it passes (240 ms ≤ 250 ms; ≤ 0.001 s under reduced motion).
- **NUMBERS:** rail 264 px ±1 (`--tp-rail-w`); top bar ≥ 56 px (`--tp-topbar-h`); tab bar ≥ 64 px (`--tp-tabbar-h`) — tokens, CONVENTIONS §5; no horizontal overflow at 390 px; motion ≤ 250 ms and collapsed under reduced motion (DESIGN.md motion rule; `expectMotionBudget`). - **REPORT:** AGENTS.md format — `status / ticket: TFV2-0023b / evidence / changed: apps/web/app/e2e/components/layout.tsx, apps/web/lib/e2e/HarnessFrame.tsx, tests/e2e/screens/components-frame.spec.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 each with its evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```tsx
  // apps/web/app/e2e/components/layout.tsx (server component)
  import type React from "react";
  import { type ReactNode, Suspense } from "react";
  import { HarnessFrame } from "@/lib/e2e/HarnessFrame";
  export default function ComponentHarnessLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }): React.JSX.Element {
    return <Suspense fallback={null}><HarnessFrame>{children}</HarnessFrame></Suspense>;
  }

  // apps/web/lib/e2e/HarnessFrame.tsx
  "use client";
  import { notFound, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation";
  import type React from "react";
  import type { ReactNode } from "react";
  import { LocaleProvider } from "@/components/providers/LocaleProvider";
  import { dirFor, resolveLang } from "@/lib/i18n";
  import { isE2EBypass } from "./e2eState";
  export type HarnessTheme = "light" | "dark";
  export function HarnessFrame({ children }: { children: ReactNode }): React.JSX.Element {
    const params = useSearchParams(); // the hook runs first, unconditionally (rules of hooks)
    if (!isE2EBypass({ NODE_ENV: process.env.NODE_ENV, NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_TEMPO_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS })) notFound();
    const lang = resolveLang(params.get("lang"), null);
    const theme: HarnessTheme = params.get("theme") === "dark" ? "dark" : "light";
    return (
      <LocaleProvider>
        <div data-testid="component-harness" lang={lang} dir={dirFor(lang)} data-theme={theme}>{children}</div>
      </LocaleProvider>
    );
  }
  ```
  `LocaleProvider` also sets `<html lang dir>` from `?lang=` on mount, so `expectDir` (which reads `<html>`) agrees with the frame.

  ```tsx
  // apps/web/components/auth/EmailField.tsx
  "use client";
  import type React from "react";
  import { useLocale } from "@/components/providers/LocaleProvider";
  import { TpIcon } from "@/components/tempo/TpIcon";
  import type { Lang } from "@/lib/i18n";
  export const EMAIL_PATTERN = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;
  export const EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER = "name@example.com";
  export function isValidEmail(value: string): boolean { return EMAIL_PATTERN.test(value.trim()); }
  export type EmailFieldProps = {
    id: string;                          // input id; help id = `${id}-help`, error id = `${id}-error`
    value: string;
    onChange: (value: string) => void;   // called with event.target.value on every input event
    help?: string;                       // screen-specific helper line (EN/HE given by the screen)
    invalid?: boolean;                   // true → aria-invalid="true" + error line
    disabled?: boolean;
  };
  export function EmailField(props: EmailFieldProps): React.JSX.Element; // body starts `const { lang } = useLocale(); const copy = COPY[lang];`
  ```
  Markup (Case A: `Field` + `TextInput` classes): `<div className="tp-field" data-component="EmailField">`; `<label className="tp-label" htmlFor={id}>{copy.label}</label>`; `<input className="tp-input" id={id} name="email" type="email" autoComplete="email" inputMode="email" dir="ltr" spellCheck={false} required placeholder={EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER} value={value} disabled={disabled === true} aria-invalid={invalid === true ? "true" : undefined} aria-describedby={describedBy} onChange={(e) => onChange(e.target.value)} />` where `describedBy` joins, in order, `${id}-help` (when `help`) and `${id}-error` (when `invalid`) with one space, or is `undefined` when both are absent; `{help && <p className="tp-help" id={`${id}-help`}>{help}</p>}`; `{invalid && <p className="tp-error-text" id={`${id}-error`}><TpIcon name="alert" size="sm" /><span>{before}<span className="tp-ltr">{EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER}</span>{after}</span></p>}` where `before`/`after` are `copy.error` split on `{example}`.
  Copy (`COPY: Record<Lang, Record<"label" | "error", string>>`):
  - `label` EN: "Email" / HE: "מייל"
  - `error` EN: "Enter your email, like {example}" / HE: "לכתוב כתובת מייל, כמו {example}"
  - placeholder (not translated, `EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER`): "name@example.com"
  States (harness order): `default` (empty, with help), `filled`, `invalid` (value kept, error shown), `disabled`, `no-help`, `interactive`, `validation`.
  Tokens (tempo.css, unchanged): input `min-height: var(--tp-touch)` (44 px), padding-inline `--tp-space-3`, `--tp-paper`, 1px `--tp-line-control`, radius `--tp-radius-md` (10 px), `--tp-text-md`; invalid border and 1px ring `--tp-danger`; disabled `--tp-sunken` + `--tp-ink-muted`; label `--tp-text-sm` 600; help `--tp-text-sm` `--tp-ink-muted`; error `--tp-text-sm` 600 `--tp-danger`; border transition `--tp-dur-fast` `--tp-ease-out`. RTL: label, help and error follow the page direction; the input stays `dir="ltr"` (an email address is LTR in Hebrew). Keyboard: label click and Tab focus the input; focus ring is the global `:focus-visible` outline. Screen reader: label via `for`; help and error via `aria-describedby`; invalid via `aria-invalid`. Breakpoints: full width of its container at 390 and 1280. Motion: border-colour transition 120 ms.

  Behaviour of `SignInScreen`: `const view = forced === null ? null : FIXTURES[forced in FIXTURES ? (forced as keyof typeof FIXTURES) : "default"]`; `const { isAuthenticated, isLoading } = useConvexAuth()`; `const liveOnline = useOnline()` (`@/lib/useOnline`); `online = view ? view.online : liveOnline`; `checkingAuth = view ? view.checkingAuth : isLoading`; state `email`, `errors`, `notice`, `sending` start from `view` (or `""`, `"none"`, `"none"`, `false`). The redirect effect `if (!isLoading && isAuthenticated) router.replace(nextPath)` runs only when `view === null`, and when `view === null && isAuthenticated` the screen renders `null` (as today). Submit (`onSubmit`, `event.preventDefault()`): if `!online || sending` return; if `!isValidEmail(email)` (from `@/components/auth/EmailField`) set `errors` to `"empty"` when `email.trim() === ""` else `"invalid"`, then focus the summary (`summaryRef.current?.focus()` after render) and return; else set `errors "none"`, `notice "none"`, `sending true` and run `send()`: live = `await signIn("resend", { email: email.trim(), redirectTo: nextPath })`; forced = the fixture `send` outcome. On success `router.push("/link-sent?" + new URLSearchParams({ email: email.trim(), next: nextPath }).toString())`. On a thrown error whose `message` contains `TooManyRequests` set `notice "rate-limited"`, else `notice "error"`; both set `sending false` and keep `email`. Typing in the field clears `errors` back to `"none"`.

"true" : undefined} onClick={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setLang("en"); }}>English</a><a href="?lang=he" hrefLang="he" lang="he" aria-current={lang === "he" ? No test asserts an icon by its drawing; a test that checks an icon asserts its `use[href="#i-<name>"]`.

"true" : undefined} onClick={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setLang("en"); }}>English</a><a href="?lang=he" hrefLang="he" lang="he" aria-current={lang === "he" ? "true" : undefined} onClick={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setLang("he"); }}>עברית</a></div>`. `setLang` stores the choice in `localStorage` (`LANG_STORAGE_KEY`) and sets `<html lang dir>` at once; a plain link would not, because `LocaleProvider` reads `?lang=` only on first mount. "English" and "עברית" are never translated.

  Module constants (not exported): `const RESEND_WAIT_SECONDS = 30;` and `safeNext(raw: string | null): string` — the rules of the module-private `getPostAuthDestination` (`apps/web/app/sign-in/page.tsx` lines 8–28), written out: `const trimmed = raw?.trim();` return `"/today"` when `!trimmed || !trimmed.startsWith("/") || trimmed.startsWith("//") || trimmed === "/dashboard" || trimmed.startsWith("/dashboard?") || trimmed.startsWith("/dashboard/") || trimmed === "/sign-in" || trimmed.startsWith("/sign-in?") || trimmed === "/sign-up" || trimmed.startsWith("/sign-up?")`, else `trimmed`.

State `left` (seconds, starts at `waitSeconds`) ticks down once per second with `setInterval` in an effect while `left > 0` (cleared on unmount). Resend (only when `email !== null && online && left === 0 && phase !== "resending"`): set `phase "resending"`; live `await signIn("resend", { email, redirectTo: next })`, forced = the fixture outcome; success → `phase "resent"`, `left = RESEND_WAIT_SECONDS`; error with `TooManyRequests` in the message → `phase "rate-limited"`; other error → `phase "error"` (both keep `left` at 0).

When `forced !== null` the page passes `"skip"` to every `useQuery`, never calls a mutation, an action or `signIn`, and renders `FIXTURES[forced in FIXTURES ? (forced as keyof typeof FIXTURES) : "default"]` (an unknown `?state=` value falls back to `default`). Each fixture also fixes what a user action does in forced mode: `"ok"` resolves, `"fail"` rejects with `new Error("fixture")`, `"rate-limit"` rejects with `new Error("TooManyRequests")`, `"hang"` returns `new Promise(() => {})` and never settles, so the spec clicks through without Convex. `forced === "offline"` (any fixture with `online: false`) behaves exactly as `useOnline()` (`@/lib/useOnline`) returning `false`. Here the `resend` field uses all four outcomes; this page has no `useQuery`.
  Next.js page exports: an App Router `page.tsx` may export only `default` (plus Next.js route-config names such as `metadata` or `dynamic`; none is used here). A type export is erased at build time, so it is allowed. This page exports exactly `default` and the type `LinkSentView`; `COPY`, `RESEND_WAIT_SECONDS`, `safeNext` and `LinkSentScreen` and every other constant, helper and sub-component stay module-private. The fixtures file imports the type with `import type` and exports only `FIXTURES`.

"true" : undefined} onClick={(e) => { e.preventDefault(); setLang("he"); }}>עברית</a></div>`. `setLang` stores the choice in `localStorage` (`LANG_STORAGE_KEY`) and sets `<html lang dir>` at once; a plain link would not, because `LocaleProvider` reads `?lang=` only on first mount. "English" and "עברית" are never translated.

### TFV2-0062a — PageEditorView takes backlinks as a prop; NotePage loads them and shows the v3 loading state
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent
- **Stage:** A · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** TFV2-0000b, TFV2-0023b, TFV2-0044 · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** after TFV2-0000b, TFV2-0023b, TFV2-0044.
- **WHY:** CONVENTIONS §13 (components take their data through props) and §14 (the page-editor screen must render "Linked here" and its loading state from fixtures). Code truth: `apps/web/components/notes/PageEditorView.tsx` reads `useQuery(api.notes.backlinks, …)` inside the component, so a fixture can never show backlinks; its one caller is `NotePage` in `apps/web/components/notes/NotesScreen.tsx` (also mounted by Today's `DailyPage.tsx`), whose loading branch is a plain text line, not the v3 skeleton (`page-editor.html` StateLoading). This ticket moves the backlinks read up into `NotePage` (prop down), draws "Linked here" with the range-1 `Backlinks` block (TFV2-0044, `apps/web/components/blocks/Backlinks.tsx`, props `{ links: readonly BacklinkRow[] | undefined }`, its own loading and empty lines) instead of the inline section, and gives `NotePage` an exported `NoteLoading` view that the screen (TFV2-0062b) reuses, so forced and live loading are the same markup. File set: the component, its single caller (the prop becomes required, so the caller must pass it in the same commit for typecheck to stay green; this takes the slot a Case B stylesheet would use, and no stylesheet is needed: Case A, existing Stage 1 classes), and the harness page. The wiki-link picker (`notes.searchTitles` while the `[[` menu is open; `notes.searchTitles` + `notes.create` when a link is followed) stays inside `PageEditorView`: it runs only on user input, never during a forced render, and moving it would add `useConvex` to `NotePage`, which `NotesScreen.test.tsx` mocks without (Cross-range notes).
- **GOAL:** `PageEditorView` renders "Linked here" with `<Backlinks links={backlinks} />` from a `backlinks` prop and makes no backlinks query, `NotePage` passes `notes.backlinks` to it and shows `NoteLoading` while the page loads, proven by a harness spec of every `PageEditorView` state with the existing notes and Today tests still green.
- **SCOPE:** `apps/web/components/notes/PageEditorView.tsx` · `apps/web/components/notes/NotesScreen.tsx` · `apps/web/app/e2e/components/page-editor-view/page.tsx` · test: `tests/e2e/screens/page-editor-view.spec.ts`.

No data, no route registration (TFV2-0023a registers `/e2e/components/(.*)`).

- **STATUS:** approved-unsent

Decision on the old OPEN (Q-07 block-model authority): the screen as wired today leaves nothing undecided. `notes.body` is the single authority in code: the page loads with `notes.getSafe({ noteId: string })`, saves the whole title/body with `notes.update({ noteId, title?, body? })` (500 ms debounce in `NotePage`), "Linked here" is computed from bodies (`notes.backlinks`, "bodies are the only truth"), and blocks are parsed from the body (`parseTempoBlocks`). This ticket keeps that path; moving the editor to `notes.save` / `notes.patchBlock` / `notes.undo` (TFV2-0007a/0007b/0010) is a separate change and not needed here. The live data path stays in `NotePage` (shared with Today's `DailyPage`, autosave races covered by `NotesScreen.test.tsx`); `page.tsx` adds forced states, the offline notice, an error boundary and route registration, and makes no Convex call itself. The old dependencies on range-1 TFV2-0021/0027/0035/0036 are dropped: the screen uses the existing `TempoShell` (layout), `PageEditorView`, `LivePreviewEditor` and `components/editor/SlashMenu`, all on `integration` today; TFV2-0044 Backlinks comes in through TFV2-0062a.

Live → `<>{online ? null : <OfflineNotice />}<NoteBoundary key={id}><NotePage noteId={id} /></NoteBoundary></>` (`NotePage` from `@/components/notes/NotesScreen`).

### TFV2-0063b — Notes list screen (`/notes`)
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent
- **Stage:** A · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** TFV2-0000b, TFV2-0000c, TFV2-0062b, TFV2-0063a · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** after TFV2-0000b, TFV2-0000c, TFV2-0062b, TFV2-0063a.
- **WHY:** PRD §4.1 (notes/pages list); `docs/design/v3/screens/web/notes.html` (`@states default | empty | loading | error | offline`; pinned first; status line counts pages); CONVENTIONS §9, §11, §14, §17. The design's folder tree, `pages.tree`/`pages.list` and "Sort: Recently edited / Title" are not built: no folder data or sort argument exists (`notes.list` takes `{ search?, pinnedOnly? }` and returns newest first); the screen keeps today's period filter (`?type=`) instead. The design's "New page → /notes/new" is not wired here because the new-page screen (TFV2-0064) comes later; the inline "New note" form stays (Cross-range notes). Old dependencies TFV2-0021/0022 are dropped: `TempoShell` and the rail are already in `apps/web/app/(tempo)/layout.tsx`.

### TFV2-0064 — New-page screen (`/notes/new`)
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent
- **Stage:** A · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** TFV2-0000b, TFV2-0000c, TFV2-0047, TFV2-0062b · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** after TFV2-0000b, TFV2-0000c, TFV2-0047, TFV2-0062b.
- **WHY:** PRD §4.1 F-06 (the app proposes one template; one tap accepts); `docs/design/v3/screens/web/new-page.html` (`@states default | empty | loading | error | offline`; one proposed template, a picker of built-in + own templates, "Start a plain note"); CONVENTIONS §9, §11, §14, §17. Code truth (`convex/templates.ts`): `templates.list({ scope?: "all" | "starter" | "mine" })` returns `{ templateId, source: "starter" | "user", name, description?, periodType, sections, body, updatedAt? }[]` (9 starters with English names, then the person's own); `templates.proposeForPage({ periodType, title? })` returns `{ templateId, name, reason } | null` (null for `"none"`); `templates.applyToNote({ templateId, title? })` creates a NEW note from the template and returns its `Id<"notes">`; `notes.create({ title, body, pinned?, periodType? })` makes a blank page. There is no `templates.apply` to an existing page, no `templates.dismissOffer`, no `templates.createFromPage`. So this screen creates the page only when a choice is made, then opens `/notes/<id>`; "Not now" is local (the offer returns on the next visit); "Make this page a template" is left out (the page does not exist yet; templates are made in the Template builder at `/templates/builder`); no Undo toast (the new page has its own Delete with a 5-minute undo). TemplateBlock (TFV2-0047) shows the offer. The route is covered by `"/notes/(.*)"` from TFV2-0062b, and Next.js serves the static `notes/new` segment before `notes/[id]`. The old dependency on TFV2-0062 (unsplit) now points at TFV2-0062b. The state components (TFV2-0120…0123) come later, so the screen writes their tempo.css markup directly.
- **GOAL:** `/notes/new` lets a person name a page, accept the one proposed template (for `?type=daily|weekly|monthly`), pick any built-in or own template, or start a plain note, then lands on `/notes/<id>`, with loading, error (plain note still possible), offline, no-own-templates and create-error states forceable with `?state=`, in EN and HE at 390 and 1280.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const EVENT_END_BEFORE_START = "Pick an end time after the start time.";
  export const update = mutation({
    args: {
      eventId: v.id("calendarEvents"),
      title: v.optional(v.string()),
      startsAtMs: v.optional(v.number()),
      endsAtMs: v.optional(v.union(v.number(), v.null())),
    },
    returns: v.id("calendarEvents"),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { eventId: Id<"calendarEvents">; title?: string; startsAtMs?: number; endsAtMs?: number | null }): Promise<Id<"calendarEvents">> => {
      const user = await requireUser(ctx);
      return updateEventForUser(ctx, user._id, args);
    },
  });
  export async function updateEventForUser(
    ctx: MutationCtx,
    userId: Id<"users">,
    args: { eventId: Id<"calendarEvents">; title?: string; startsAtMs?: number; endsAtMs?: number | null },
  ): Promise<Id<"calendarEvents">> {
    const event = await ctx.db.get(args.eventId);
    if (!event || event.userId !== userId || event.deletedAt !== undefined) {
      throw new Error("Event not found");
    }
    const patch: { title?: string; startsAtMs?: number; endsAtMs?: number; updatedAt: number } = { updatedAt: Date.now() };
    if (args.title !== undefined) {
      const title = args.title.trim();
      if (!title) {
        throw new Error("Give the event a gentle label first.");
      }
      patch.title = title;
    }
    if (args.startsAtMs !== undefined) patch.startsAtMs = args.startsAtMs;
    const nextStart = args.startsAtMs ?? event.startsAtMs;
    const nextEnd = args.endsAtMs === undefined ? event.endsAtMs : (args.endsAtMs ?? undefined);
    if (nextEnd !== undefined && nextEnd <= nextStart) {
      throw new Error(EVENT_END_BEFORE_START);
    }
    if (args.endsAtMs !== undefined) patch.endsAtMs = nextEnd;
    await ctx.db.patch(args.eventId, patch);
    return args.eventId;
  }
  ```
  `calendarEventValidator` gains `endsAtMs: v.optional(v.number())`. Auth: `requireUser`; owner only. `endsAtMs: null` clears the end (patching `undefined` removes the field), leaving a point-in-time event; omitting `endsAtMs` keeps the stored end, which is still checked against a new `startsAtMs`. Errors (plain `Error`, checked in this order): `"Not authenticated"` — no identity; `"Event not found"` — no row, foreign row, or row with `deletedAt`; `"Give the event a gentle label first."` — `title` passed and blank after trim; `"Pick an end time after the start time."` — the resulting end is set and `<=` the resulting start. A throw writes nothing. No other user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  - Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / When `run(calendarEvents.update, ctx, { eventId: "calendarEvents:1", title: "y" })` / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  - Given no row `"calendarEvents:999"` / When A calls `update({ title: "y" })` / Then it rejects with `"Event not found"`.
  - Given B's event titled `"x"` / When A calls `update({ title: "y" })` / Then it rejects with `"Event not found"` and the title is still `"x"`.
  - Given A's event with `deletedAt: 5` / When `update({ title: "y" })` / Then it rejects with `"Event not found"`.
  - Given A's event / When `update({ title: "   " })` / Then it rejects with `"Give the event a gentle label first."` and the title is still `"x"`.
  - Given A's event with `startsAtMs: 1000` / When `update({ endsAtMs: 1000 })` / Then it rejects with `"Pick an end time after the start time."` and the row has no `endsAtMs`.
  - Given A's event with `startsAtMs: 1000`, `endsAtMs: 2000` / When `update({ startsAtMs: 2500 })` / Then it rejects with `"Pick an end time after the start time."` and `startsAtMs` is still `1000`.
  - Given A's event with `startsAtMs: 1000` / When `update({ title: "  Lunch ", endsAtMs: 5000 })` / Then it returns the event id and the row has `title: "Lunch"`, `startsAtMs: 1000`, `endsAtMs: 5000`.
  - Given A's event with `endsAtMs: 2000` / When `update({ endsAtMs: null })` / Then the row's `endsAtMs` is `undefined`.
  - Given A's event with `startsAtMs: 1000`, `endsAtMs: 2000` / When `update({ title: "B" })` / Then the row has `title: "B"`, `startsAtMs: 1000`, `endsAtMs: 2000`.
- **NUMBERS:** test cases 10 of 10 pass (exact); end-after-start rule from CFG-005 (cases 6–7); Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline measured in this repo; not a gate) — CONVENTIONS §20. Reads: one `ctx.db.get`.

  ```ts
  export const create = mutation({
    args: { title: v.string(), startsAtMs: v.number(), endsAtMs: v.optional(v.number()) },
    returns: v.id("calendarEvents"),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { title: string; startsAtMs: number; endsAtMs?: number }): Promise<Id<"calendarEvents">> => {
      const user = await requireUser(ctx);
      return createEventForUser(ctx, user._id, args);
    },
  });
  export async function createEventForUser(
    ctx: MutationCtx,
    userId: Id<"users">,
    args: { title: string; startsAtMs: number; endsAtMs?: number },
  ): Promise<Id<"calendarEvents">> {
    const title = args.title.trim();
    if (!title) {
      throw new Error("Give the event a gentle label first.");
    }
    if (args.endsAtMs !== undefined && args.endsAtMs <= args.startsAtMs) {
      throw new Error(EVENT_END_BEFORE_START);
    }
    const now = Date.now();
    return await ctx.db.insert("calendarEvents", {
      userId,
      title,
      startsAtMs: args.startsAtMs,
      ...(args.endsAtMs !== undefined ? { endsAtMs: args.endsAtMs } : {}),
      createdAt: now,
      updatedAt: now,
    });
  }
  ```

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const MAX_HABIT_CHECKINS_READ = 3660;
  async function liveCheckInsForHabit(ctx: MutationCtx, habitId: Id<"habits">) {
  	return ctx.db
  		.query("habitCheckIns")
  		.withIndex("by_habitId_deletedAt_localDate", (q) => q.eq("habitId", habitId).eq("deletedAt", undefined))
  		.order("desc")
  		.take(MAX_HABIT_CHECKINS_READ);
  }
  async function findLiveCheckIn(ctx: MutationCtx, habitId: Id<"habits">, localDate: string): Promise<Doc<"habitCheckIns"> | null> {
  	return ctx.db
  		.query("habitCheckIns")
  		.withIndex("by_habitId_deletedAt_localDate", (q) =>
  			q.eq("habitId", habitId).eq("deletedAt", undefined).eq("localDate", localDate),
  		)
  		.first();
  }
  export const check = mutation({
  	args: {
  		habitId: v.id("habits"),
  		localDate: v.string(),
  		source: v.union(v.literal("habits"), v.literal("today"), v.literal("suggestion")),
  		note: v.optional(v.string()),
  		asOfLocalDate: v.optional(v.string()),
  	},
  	returns: v.object({ checkInId: v.id("habitCheckIns"), alreadyChecked: v.boolean(), currentStreak: v.number(), longestStreak: v.number() }),
  	handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { habitId: Id<"habits">; localDate: string; source: "habits" | "today" | "suggestion"; note?: string; asOfLocalDate?: string }): Promise<{ checkInId: Id<"habitCheckIns">; alreadyChecked: boolean; currentStreak: number; longestStreak: number }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Auth: `requireUser`; the habit's owner only (`getOwnedHabit`). Behaviour: one live row per habit per `localDate`. Already checked → returns `{ checkInId: existing._id, alreadyChecked: true, currentStreak: habit.currentStreak, longestStreak: habit.longestStreak }` with no write. Otherwise inserts `{ userId, habitId, localDate, checkedAt: now, source, note?, createdAt: now, updatedAt: now }` (`note` trimmed; blank → no `note` key), then patches the habit cache (`currentStreak`, `longestStreak = max(computed, stored)`, `lastCompletedAt`, `updatedAt`) from the newest `MAX_HABIT_CHECKINS_READ` live rows, evaluated as of `asOfLocalDate` (UTC today when omitted). Errors (plain `Error`, in this order): `"Not authenticated"` — no identity; `"localDate must be YYYY-MM-DD"` — `localDate` is not a real `YYYY-MM-DD` date (`isLocalDate`); `"asOfLocalDate must be YYYY-MM-DD"` — `asOfLocalDate` passed and not a real date; `"asOfLocalDate must be within one day of UTC today"` — outside UTC today −1…+1 days; `"Habit not found"` — habit missing, foreign or soft-deleted. A throw writes nothing. No user-facing copy (the screen never shows the streak, PRD F-10).
- **TESTS:**
  - Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / When `run(habitCheckIns.check, ctx, { habitId: "habits:1", localDate: "2026-10-07", source: "habits" })` / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  - Given USER's habit / When `check(ctx, habitId, "2026-13-01", "2026-10-07")` / Then it rejects with `"localDate must be YYYY-MM-DD"` and `habitCheckIns` has no rows.
  - Given USER's habit / When `check(ctx, habitId, "2026-10-07", "2026/10/07")` / Then it rejects with `"asOfLocalDate must be YYYY-MM-DD"`.
  - Given USER's habit / When `check(ctx, habitId, "2026-10-07", "2026-10-09")` / Then it rejects with `"asOfLocalDate must be within one day of UTC today"`.
  - Given no habit `"habits:999"` / When `check(ctx, "habits:999", "2026-10-07", "2026-10-07")` / Then it rejects with `"Habit not found"`.
  - Given a habit with `userId: "users:b"` / When USER calls `check` / Then it rejects with `"Habit not found"` and `habitCheckIns` has no rows.
  - Given USER's habit with `deletedAt: 5` / When `check` / Then it rejects with `"Habit not found"`.
  - Given USER's habit with no check-ins / When `run(habitCheckIns.check, ctx, { habitId, localDate: "2026-10-07", source: "today", note: "  ok  ", asOfLocalDate: "2026-10-07" })` / Then it returns `alreadyChecked: false`, `currentStreak: 1`, the inserted row has `localDate: "2026-10-07"`, `source: "today"`, `note: "ok"`, and the habit row has `currentStreak: 1`.
  - Given that check-in already exists / When `check(ctx, habitId, "2026-10-07", "2026-10-07")` runs again / Then it returns `alreadyChecked: true` with the same `checkInId`, and exactly one live row exists for that date.
  - Given USER's habit / When `run(habitCheckIns.check, ctx, { habitId, localDate: "2026-10-07", source: "habits", note: "   ", asOfLocalDate: "2026-10-07" })` / Then the inserted row has no `note` key (`"note" in row` is `false`).
  - Given USER's habit and `MAX_HABIT_CHECKINS_READ - 1` (3659) live check-ins on consecutive days ending `"2026-10-06"`, inserted newest first / When `check(ctx, habitId, "2026-10-07", "2026-10-07")` (now exactly 3660 live rows) / Then it returns `currentStreak: 3660` (every row read); and, with a fresh `makeFakeCtx(USER)` and habit, given `MAX_HABIT_CHECKINS_READ + 1` (3661) live check-ins ending `"2026-10-06"`, inserted newest first / When the same `check` runs / Then it returns `currentStreak: MAX_HABIT_CHECKINS_READ` (3660), not 3662.
- **NUMBERS:** test cases 11 of 11 pass (exact); bounded read ≤ `MAX_HABIT_CHECKINS_READ` = 3660 rows (code constant; the cap case reaches exactly 3660 rows, then seeds 3661); Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline measured in this repo; not a gate) — CONVENTIONS §20.
