  ```ts
  import type React from "react";
  import type { ReactNode } from "react";
  export type PrefsTheme = "light" | "dark" | "system";
  export type PrefsLang = "en" | "he";
  export type PrefsTextSize = "s" | "m" | "l";
  export type PrefsWeekStart = 0 | 1 | 6;
  export type PrefsData = {
    theme: PrefsTheme; lang: PrefsLang; textSize: PrefsTextSize; readingFont: boolean;
    dial: number;                 // 0–10, what the slider shows now (the route debounces the save)
    weekStartsOn: PrefsWeekStart; timeZone: string; timeZones: string[];  // timeZones includes timeZone
    emailReminders: boolean; inAppNotifications: boolean;
  };
  export type PrefsChange =
    | { key: "theme"; value: PrefsTheme } | { key: "lang"; value: PrefsLang }
    | { key: "textSize"; value: PrefsTextSize } | { key: "readingFont"; value: boolean }
    | { key: "weekStartsOn"; value: PrefsWeekStart } | { key: "timeZone"; value: string }
    | { key: "emailReminders"; value: boolean } | { key: "inAppNotifications"; value: boolean };
  export type PrefsState = "default" | "loading" | "error" | "signed-out";
  export type PreferencesViewProps = {
    state: PrefsState;
    online: boolean;
    data: PrefsData;
    status: string;               // the header status line ("Saved." or ""); spoken politely
    saveError: boolean;           // the last change did not save
    extra?: ReactNode;            // more sections after the View's own (rendered in "default" and "loading")
    onChange: (change: PrefsChange) => void;
    onDial: (value: number) => void;   // every slider move
    onRetry: () => void;
  };
  export function PreferencesView(props: PreferencesViewProps): React.JSX.Element;
  ```

### TFV2-0312 — PWA: web app manifest + icons (`apps/web/app/manifest.ts`)
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent

Code truth (checked on `integration`): no `apps/web/app/manifest*`, no `apps/web/public/icons/` and no `apps/web/public/sw*` exist; `apps/web/app/layout.tsx` sets `metadata.title` "Tempo Flow — your brain's operating system" and `viewport.themeColor` light `#F3EEE4` / dark `#161412` (the `--tp-ground` values of `docs/design/v3/tokens.css` lines 25 and 125). Next.js 16 serves `app/manifest.ts` (a `MetadataRoute.Manifest` default export) at `/manifest.webmanifest` and adds `<link rel="manifest">` to every page by itself, so **no dependency and no `next.config.ts` change is needed** (no config lane). `apps/web/proxy.ts`'s matcher skips paths ending in `.webmanifest`, `.svg`, `.js` and `.html`, so the manifest and the icons are reachable signed out. `bun run scan:design-tokens` counts raw 6-digit hex literals in `apps/web/app/**/*.ts`, so the manifest writes its colours as `rgb()`; `.svg` files are not scanned. The old ticket's DONE (`bun run typecheck` only) proved nothing; this one checks what the server actually serves.

### TFV2-0313a — PWA: service worker with an offline fallback (`apps/web/public/sw.js`)
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent
- **Stage:** D · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); web lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** PRD F-120 (web PWA: never a dead page offline); the old TFV2-0313 (service worker + offline page + registration in one ticket, `apps/web/app/sw.ts`, OPEN on a cache budget) was more than one unit and could not work as written: Next.js does not compile `app/sw.ts` into a worker, and a precache of the app shell needs the build's hashed asset list (a `next-pwa` / `workbox` dependency = config lane). Decision: a dependency-free, hand-written worker in `apps/web/public/` (served as-is at `/sw.js`; `apps/web/proxy.ts`'s matcher skips `.js` paths) that precaches **only** the static offline page and answers a failed page navigation with it. It never caches pages, API responses or Convex traffic: Tempo's HTML embeds the signed-in session state from `ConvexAuthNextjsServerProvider` (`apps/web/app/layout.tsx`), so caching pages would store credentials. Split: this ticket = the worker; TFV2-0313b = the offline page; TFV2-0313c = registration. Because no asset list is precached, the old OPEN "shell cache size budget" no longer applies (the cache holds one small HTML file).
- **GOAL:** `apps/web/public/sw.js` installs a cache `tempo-offline-v1` holding `/offline.html`, drops older `tempo-offline-*` caches on activate, passes every page navigation to the network and falls back to the cached `/offline.html` only when the network fails, proven by a unit test that runs the real file against fakes.
- **SCOPE:** `apps/web/public/sw.js` · test: `apps/web/lib/pwa/serviceWorker.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `apps/web/public/sw.js` (new) · `apps/web/lib/pwa/serviceWorker.test.ts` (new; creates `apps/web/lib/pwa/`) · new public URL `/sw.js` (not registered by anything until TFV2-0313c). No dependency, config, schema or env change.

- **SPEC:**
  ```js
  // apps/web/public/sw.js
  /* Tempo service worker (TFV2-0313a): offline fallback page only. It never caches pages or data. */
  const CACHE = "tempo-offline-v1";
  const OFFLINE_URL = "/offline.html";

  self.addEventListener("install", (event) => {
    event.waitUntil(
      caches
        .open(CACHE)
        .then((cache) => cache.add(new Request(OFFLINE_URL, { cache: "reload" })))
        .then(() => self.skipWaiting()),
    );
  });

  self.addEventListener("activate", (event) => {
    event.waitUntil(
      caches
        .keys()
        .then((keys) => Promise.all(keys.filter((key) => key.startsWith("tempo-offline-") && key !== CACHE).map((key) => caches.delete(key)))),
    );
  });

  self.addEventListener("fetch", (event) => {
    if (event.request.mode !== "navigate") return;
    event.respondWith(fetch(event.request).catch(() => caches.match(OFFLINE_URL).then((cached) => cached || Response.error())));
  });
  ```

A fake event is `{ request?: { mode: string }, waitUntil(p) { this.p = p; }, respondWith(p) { this.r = p; } }`; tests `await` `event.p` / `event.r`. Auth: none (static asset). Errors: a failed navigation never throws to the page; with no cached page it answers `Response.error()`. Limits: one cached file, one cache name.

Given the loaded worker / When the `install` handler runs with a fake event / Then `caches.open` was called with `"tempo-offline-v1"`, the opened cache's `add` received one `FakeRequest` whose `url` is `"/offline.html"` and `init.cache` is `"reload"`, and `self.skipWaiting` was called once after `add` resolved.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // apps/web/lib/pwa/registerServiceWorker.ts — pure (no React, no Next)
  export type SwRegistrationResult = "registered" | "skipped" | "failed";
  export type SwContainerLike = { register: (scriptUrl: string, options: { scope: string }) => Promise<unknown> };
  export const SERVICE_WORKER_URL = "/sw.js";
  /** Registers /sw.js (scope "/") only in production and only when the browser has service workers. Never throws. */
  export async function registerServiceWorker(env: { NODE_ENV?: string }, container: SwContainerLike | undefined): Promise<SwRegistrationResult> {
    if (env.NODE_ENV !== "production" || container === undefined) return "skipped";
    try {
      await container.register(SERVICE_WORKER_URL, { scope: "/" });
      return "registered";
    } catch {
      return "failed";
    }
  }
  ```
  ```tsx
  // apps/web/components/pwa/ServiceWorkerRegister.tsx
  "use client";
  import { useEffect } from "react";
  import { registerServiceWorker } from "@/lib/pwa/registerServiceWorker";

  /** Mounted once in the root layout; renders nothing. */
  export function ServiceWorkerRegister(): null {
    useEffect(() => {
      const container = typeof navigator !== "undefined" && "serviceWorker" in navigator ? navigator.serviceWorker : undefined;
      void registerServiceWorker({ NODE_ENV: process.env.NODE_ENV }, container);
    }, []);
    return null;
  }
  ```
  `layout.tsx` additions (exact):
  ```diff
   import { ThemeProvider } from "@/components/providers/ThemeProvider";
  +import { ServiceWorkerRegister } from "@/components/pwa/ServiceWorkerRegister";
  …
           <body className="antialiased" suppressHydrationWarning>
  +          <ServiceWorkerRegister />
             <ThemeProvider>
  ```
  Copy: none (renders nothing). States: registered / skipped / failed (returned, never shown; a failed registration leaves the app working online). Auth: none. Errors: none thrown (a rejected `register` returns `"failed"`).
- **TESTS:** (bun:test; the fake container is `{ register: mock(async () => ({})) }`)
  1. Given `env = { NODE_ENV: "development" }` and a fake container / When `registerServiceWorker` runs / Then it returns `"skipped"` and `register` was not called.
  2. Given `env = { NODE_ENV: "test" }` / When it runs / Then it returns `"skipped"` and `register` was not called.
  3. Given `env = { NODE_ENV: "production" }` and a fake container / When it runs / Then it returns `"registered"` and `register` was called once with `("/sw.js", { scope: "/" })`.
  4. Given `env = { NODE_ENV: "production" }` and `container = undefined` / When it runs / Then it returns `"skipped"`.
  5. Given `env = { NODE_ENV: "production" }` and `register` rejecting `new Error("SecurityError")` / When it runs / Then it resolves `"failed"` (no throw).

### TFV2-0314b — PWA install store `createInstallPromptStore` (`apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.ts`)
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent
- **Stage:** D · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); web lib lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** PRD F-120; old TFV2-0314 ("show a quiet install button on `beforeinstallprompt`"; DO NOT "auto-install", "nag repeatedly"). Code truth: `grep -rn beforeinstallprompt apps/web` finds nothing. A framework-free store makes the install rules testable with `bun test` (CONVENTIONS §9 pure helper kind); the component (TFV2-0314c) and the mount (TFV2-0314d) use it.
- **GOAL:** `apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.ts` exports `createInstallPromptStore`, which captures the browser's install event, offers it once, and remembers a "Not now" forever, proven by its own test file.
- **SCOPE:** `apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.ts` · test: `apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.ts` (new) · `apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.test.ts` (new) · browser `localStorage["tempo-install-dismissed"]` (written only by `dismiss()` or a declined prompt, at runtime).
- **STEPS:**
  1. Code-map: `ls apps/web/lib/pwa` (absent); `grep -rn "beforeinstallprompt" apps/web` (no hits).
  2. Create `installPrompt.ts` exactly as SPEC: no imports, no React, no `window` access at module scope.
  3. Create `installPrompt.test.ts` (`import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";`) with exactly the 11 TESTS cases, using `new EventTarget()` and the fake storage and fake event in SPEC.
  4. Run DONE, then `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck`.
- **DONE:** `bun test apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.test.ts` → `11 pass`, `0 fail`.
- **EVIDENCE:** the summary of `bun test apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.test.ts`, plus lint/typecheck exit codes, pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** call `event.prompt()` anywhere except inside `prompt()`; show anything (no DOM); read or write any storage key other than `tempo-install-dismissed`; add a dependency; touch `convex/**`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** AGENTS.md format — `status / ticket: TFV2-0314b / evidence / changed: apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.ts, apps/web/lib/pwa/installPrompt.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 each with its evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const INSTALL_DISMISSED_KEY = "tempo-install-dismissed";
  export type InstallState = "unavailable" | "available" | "prompting" | "installed" | "dismissed";
  export type InstallOutcome = "accepted" | "dismissed" | "unavailable";
  /** The non-standard `beforeinstallprompt` event (Chromium). */
  export interface BeforeInstallPromptEventLike extends Event {
    prompt(): Promise<void>;
    readonly userChoice: Promise<{ outcome: "accepted" | "dismissed"; platform: string }>;
  }
  export type InstallStorage = Pick<Storage, "getItem" | "setItem">;
  export interface InstallPromptStore {
    getState(): InstallState;
    /** Calls `listener` after every state change; returns the unsubscribe function. */
    subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void;
    prompt(): Promise<InstallOutcome>;
    dismiss(): void;
  }
  export function createInstallPromptStore(target: EventTarget, storage: InstallStorage | null): InstallPromptStore;
  ```
  Rules (each is one TESTS case):
  - Start state: `"dismissed"` when `storage?.getItem(INSTALL_DISMISSED_KEY) === "1"`, else `"unavailable"`. A `getItem` that throws counts as `null`.
  - `target` gets two listeners at creation: `"beforeinstallprompt"` and `"appinstalled"`.
  - On `"beforeinstallprompt"`: always `event.preventDefault()` (the browser's own mini-infobar never shows). If the state is `"dismissed"` or `"installed"`, keep the state and drop the event (no nag). Otherwise keep the event and set `"available"`.
  - On `"appinstalled"`: drop any kept event, set `"installed"`.
  - `prompt()`: when the state is not `"available"` (or no event is kept) → resolve `"unavailable"`, state unchanged. Otherwise set `"prompting"`, `await event.prompt()`, `const { outcome } = await event.userChoice`, drop the event; `"accepted"` → state `"installed"`; `"dismissed"` → `storage?.setItem(INSTALL_DISMISSED_KEY, "1")` and state `"dismissed"`; resolve `outcome`. If `event.prompt()` or `userChoice` rejects → drop the event, state `"unavailable"`, resolve `"unavailable"` (never rejects).
  - `dismiss()`: `storage?.setItem(INSTALL_DISMISSED_KEY, "1")` (a throwing `setItem` is ignored), drop the event, set `"dismissed"`.
  - Every state change calls each subscribed listener once; setting the same state again calls none.
  - Test doubles: `const storage = new Map<string, string>(); const fake = { getItem: (k: string) => storage.get(k) ?? null, setItem: (k: string, v: string) => void storage.set(k, v) };` and `function installEvent(outcome: "accepted" | "dismissed") { const e = new Event("beforeinstallprompt", { cancelable: true }) as BeforeInstallPromptEventLike; Object.assign(e, { prompt: async () => {}, userChoice: Promise.resolve({ outcome, platform: "web" }) }); return e; }`.
  - No user-facing copy; no errors thrown.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given a fresh store on `new EventTarget()` with empty storage / Then `getState()` is `"unavailable"`.
  2. Given a subscribed listener / When `installEvent("accepted")` is dispatched / Then `getState()` is `"available"`, the event's `defaultPrevented` is `true`, and the listener ran exactly once.
  3. Given `"available"` from an `"accepted"` event / When `await prompt()` / Then it resolves `"accepted"`, `getState()` is `"installed"`, and storage has no `tempo-install-dismissed` entry.
  4. Given `"available"` from a `"dismissed"` event / When `await prompt()` / Then it resolves `"dismissed"`, `getState()` is `"dismissed"`, and storage `tempo-install-dismissed` is `"1"`.
  5. Given `"available"` / When `dismiss()` runs and then a second `installEvent("accepted")` is dispatched / Then `getState()` stays `"dismissed"`, storage holds `"1"`, and the second event's `defaultPrevented` is `true`.
  6. Given storage already holding `tempo-install-dismissed = "1"` / When the store is created and an install event is dispatched / Then `getState()` is `"dismissed"` both before and after.
  7. Given a fresh store / When `await prompt()` / Then it resolves `"unavailable"` and the state stays `"unavailable"`.
  8. Given `"available"` / When `new Event("appinstalled")` is dispatched / Then `getState()` is `"installed"` and a later `await prompt()` resolves `"unavailable"`.
  9. Given `storage = null`, and separately a storage whose `getItem` and `setItem` throw / When each store is created and `dismiss()` runs / Then neither throws, both start `"unavailable"`, and both end `"dismissed"`.
  10. Given an install event whose `prompt` is `async () => { throw new Error("blocked"); }` / When `await prompt()` / Then it resolves `"unavailable"` and `getState()` is `"unavailable"`.
  11. Given a listener whose unsubscribe function was called / When an install event is dispatched / Then the listener did not run.
- **NUMBERS:** 11 of 11 cases pass (exact). Install offers per browser after "Not now" = 0 (cases 4–6; old ticket "do not nag repeatedly"). Latency: n/a (pure, synchronous apart from the browser prompt).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

- **SPEC:**
  ```tsx
  "use client";
  import type React from "react";
  import { useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
  import { InstallPrompt } from "@/components/pwa/InstallPrompt";
  import { createInstallPromptStore, type InstallPromptStore, type InstallState } from "@/lib/pwa/installPrompt";

  function browserStorage(): Storage | null {
    try {
      return window.localStorage;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }
  // Created at module load in the browser, so an install event fired before hydration is still caught.
  const store: InstallPromptStore | null = typeof window === "undefined" ? null : createInstallPromptStore(window, browserStorage());
  const subscribe = (listener: () => void): (() => void) => store?.subscribe(listener) ?? (() => undefined);
  const getSnapshot = (): InstallState => store?.getState() ?? "unavailable";
  const getServerSnapshot = (): InstallState => "unavailable";

  export function InstallPromptMount(): React.JSX.Element | null {
    const state = useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot);
    if (state !== "available" && state !== "prompting") return null;
    return <InstallPrompt busy={state === "prompting"} onInstall={() => void store?.prompt()} onDismiss={() => store?.dismiss()} />;
  }
  ```
  - Placement: `InstallPrompt` default `placement="floating"` (fixed; below 768 px above the mobile tab bar, from 768 px a 400 px card in the inline-end bottom corner — TFV2-0314c SPEC).
  - States: hidden (`unavailable`, `installed`, `dismissed`), shown (`available`), shown busy (`prompting`). Copy: none new; every visible string is `InstallPrompt`'s own `COPY` (created by TFV2-0314c, in Depends). RTL, keyboard, screen reader, motion: this component renders only `<InstallPrompt />` (props above) or `null`, so all four come from `InstallPrompt` (TFV2-0314c).
  - Synthetic event the spec dispatches (after `await page.waitForLoadState("networkidle")`): `await page.evaluate((outcome) => { const w = window as unknown as { __promptCalls: number }; w.__promptCalls = 0; const e = new Event("beforeinstallprompt", { cancelable: true }); Object.assign(e, { prompt: async () => { w.__promptCalls += 1; }, userChoice: Promise.resolve({ outcome, platform: "web" }) }); window.dispatchEvent(e); }, outcome)`.
- **TESTS:** (spec starts `test.skip(!!process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, "local webServer only");`; every case runs at both `VIEWPORTS` × `["en", "he"]` after `await page.goto(\`/?lang=${lang}\`)`, = 16; console errors are collected with `trackConsoleErrors`, messages matching `/example\.convex\.cloud|WebSocket/i` dropped, then asserted `[]`)
  1. Given `/` loaded / Then `[data-component="InstallPrompt"]` has count 0; When the synthetic event (`"accepted"`) is dispatched / Then it is visible with `data-placement="floating"`, computed `position` `fixed`, and the title "Install Tempo" (en) or "התקנת Tempo" (he).
  2. Given the notice shown from an `"accepted"` event / When Install is clicked / Then `window.__promptCalls` is `1` and `[data-component="InstallPrompt"]` has count 0 within 2 s.
  3. Given the notice shown / When Not now is clicked / Then the notice has count 0, `localStorage.getItem("tempo-install-dismissed")` is `"1"`; When the page is reloaded and the synthetic event dispatched again / Then the notice still has count 0 (no second offer).

  ```tsx
  type CopyKey = "version" | "new" | "better" | "fixed";
  const COPY: Record<Lang, Record<CopyKey, string>> = {
    en: { version: "Version", new: "New", better: "Better", fixed: "Fixed" },
    he: { version: "גרסה", new: "חדש", better: "שיפור", fixed: "תוקן" },
  };
  const KIND: Record<ChangeKind, { icon: TpIconName; tone?: "info" | "done" }> = {
    new: { icon: "sparkle", tone: "info" },
    better: { icon: "arrow" },
    fixed: { icon: "check", tone: "done" },
  };
  export type ChangelogEntryProps = {
    /** "major.minor", shown in `.tp-num`. */
    version: string;
    /** YYYY-MM-DD; formatted with `changelogDate(date, lang)`. */
    date: string;
    /** Already-translated change lines, in display order. */
    changes: readonly { kind: ChangeKind; text: string }[];
  };
  export function ChangelogEntry({ version, date, changes }: ChangelogEntryProps): React.JSX.Element;
  ```

    ```ts
    export type TodayView = {

      plan: FunctionReturnType<typeof api.dayPlans.getForDate> | undefined;
      blocks: FunctionReturnType<typeof api.timeBlocks.listForDate> | undefined;
      events: FunctionReturnType<typeof api.calendar_events.listInRange> | undefined;
      habits: FunctionReturnType<typeof api.habits.list> | undefined;
      checkIns: FunctionReturnType<typeof api.habitCheckIns.listForDate> | undefined;

    const USER = "users:e2e" as Id<"users">;

    const DONE_TASK = { _id: "tasks:e2e-done" as Id<"tasks">, _creationTime: NOON - 7_200_000, userId: USER, title: "Water the plants", status: "done" as const, priority: "low" as const, dueAt: NOON, completedAt: NOON - 3_600_000, createdAt: NOON - 7_200_000, updatedAt: NOON - 3_600_000 };
    const DEFAULT: TodayView = { tasks: [OPEN_TASK, DONE_TASK], plan: null, blocks: [], events: [], habits: [], checkIns: [] };

    };
    ```

  **Fixtures** (`apps/mobile/lib/e2e/fixtures/tasks.ts`, the whole file):
  ```ts
  import type { TaskLike } from "@/lib/v3/tasks";

  export type TasksState = "default" | "empty" | "loading" | "error" | "offline";
  export type TasksView = { tasks: readonly TaskLike[] | undefined };

  const HOUR_MS = 3_600_000;
  const DAY_MS = 86_400_000;
  /** Local midnight today, so "today" rows land in Today whatever time the spec runs. */
  const START = (() => {
    const d = new Date();
    d.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
    return d.getTime();
  })();

  const TASKS: readonly TaskLike[] = [
    { _id: "tasks:fx-1", title: "Call the dentist", status: "todo", priority: "high", timeEstimate: 900_000, dueAt: START + 17 * HOUR_MS, createdAt: START - DAY_MS, updatedAt: START - DAY_MS },
    { _id: "tasks:fx-2", title: "Pay the electricity bill", status: "todo", priority: "medium", dueAt: START + 3 * DAY_MS + 12 * HOUR_MS, createdAt: START - DAY_MS, updatedAt: START - DAY_MS },
    { _id: "tasks:fx-3", title: "Buy a birthday card", status: "todo", priority: "low", createdAt: START - 2 * DAY_MS, updatedAt: START - 2 * DAY_MS },
    { _id: "tasks:fx-4", title: "Water the plants", status: "done", priority: "low", completedAt: START + 8 * HOUR_MS, createdAt: START - 3 * DAY_MS, updatedAt: START + 8 * HOUR_MS },
  ];

  export const FIXTURES: Record<TasksState, TasksView> = {
    default: { tasks: TASKS },
    empty: { tasks: [] },
    loading: { tasks: undefined },
    error: { tasks: undefined },
    offline: { tasks: TASKS },
  };
  ```
  With `groupTasks`, `default` gives Today = "Call the dentist", Coming up = "Pay the electricity bill", Inbox = "Buy a birthday card", Done today = "Water the plants".
  **Edit** (`tasks.tsx`; every other line stays byte for byte):
  1. Imports: add `import { FIXTURES, type TasksState, type TasksView } from "@/lib/e2e/fixtures/tasks";` and `import { useE2EMobile } from "@/lib/e2e/useE2EMobile";` after the `@/convex/_generated/dataModel` import.
  2. In `TasksScreen`, replace `  const offline = useOffline();` with:
     ```ts
     const forced = useE2EMobile();
     const key: TasksState = forced !== null && forced in FIXTURES ? (forced as TasksState) : "loading";
     const fixture = forced === null ? null : FIXTURES[key];
     const liveOffline = useOffline();
     const offline = forced ? forced === "offline" : liveOffline;
     ```
  3. In `TasksScreen`, move the `QueryBoundary` fallback into a constant declared before `return`, unchanged in content:

  - `error`: `role="alert"` holding heading `err.title` EN "Couldn't load your tasks." / HE "לא הצלחנו לטעון את המשימות שלך.", the text `state.safe` EN "Your data is safe." / HE "הנתונים שלך בטוחים." followed by `err.body`, and button `state.retry` EN "Try again" / HE "לנסות שוב" (no-op while forced).

  ```ts
  import type { Id } from "@/convex/_generated/dataModel";

  export type HabitsState = "default" | "empty" | "loading" | "error" | "offline" | "welcome-back";
  export type HabitsFixtureHabit = { _id: Id<"habits">; name: string; createdAt: number; deletedAt?: number };
  export type HabitsView = {
    habits: readonly HabitsFixtureHabit[] | undefined;
    checkIns: readonly { habitId: Id<"habits"> }[] | undefined;
    /** Check-ins of the last 7 local days, per habit id. */
    days: Readonly<Record<string, readonly { localDate: string }[]>>;
  };

  const DAY_MS = 86_400_000;
  const START = (() => {
    const d = new Date();
    d.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
    return d.getTime();
  })();
  /** The phone's local date `n` days ago as YYYY-MM-DD. */
  function isoDaysAgo(n: number): string {
    const d = new Date();
    d.setDate(d.getDate() - n);
    return `${d.getFullYear()}-${String(d.getMonth() + 1).padStart(2, "0")}-${String(d.getDate()).padStart(2, "0")}`;
  }

  const WALK = "habits:fx-1" as Id<"habits">;
  const WATER = "habits:fx-2" as Id<"habits">;
  const STRETCH = "habits:fx-3" as Id<"habits">;

  const DEFAULT: HabitsView = {
    habits: [

      { _id: WATER, name: "Drink water", createdAt: START - 3 * DAY_MS },
    ],
    checkIns: [{ habitId: WALK }],
    days: { [WALK]: [{ localDate: isoDaysAgo(3) }, { localDate: isoDaysAgo(1) }, { localDate: isoDaysAgo(0) }], [WATER]: [{ localDate: isoDaysAgo(1) }] },
  };

  export const FIXTURES: Record<HabitsState, HabitsView> = {
    default: DEFAULT,
    empty: { habits: [], checkIns: [], days: {} },
    loading: { habits: undefined, checkIns: undefined, days: {} },
    error: { habits: undefined, checkIns: undefined, days: {} },
    offline: DEFAULT,
    "welcome-back": { habits: [{ _id: STRETCH, name: "Stretch", createdAt: START - 30 * DAY_MS }], checkIns: [], days: { [STRETCH]: [] } },
  };
  ```

  ```ts
  import type { Id } from "@/convex/_generated/dataModel";

  export type CalendarState = "default" | "empty" | "loading" | "error" | "offline" | "free-day";
  export type CalendarFixtureEvent = { _id: Id<"calendarEvents">; title: string; startsAtMs: number };
  export type CalendarView = { events: readonly CalendarFixtureEvent[] | undefined };

  /** Local time `hours:minutes` on the day `dayDelta` days from today. */
  function at(dayDelta: number, hours: number, minutes: number): number {
    const d = new Date();
    d.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
    d.setDate(d.getDate() + dayDelta);
    d.setHours(hours, minutes, 0, 0);
    return d.getTime();
  }
  /** Another day in the same Monday-to-Sunday week as today. */
  const OTHER_DAY = new Date().getDay() === 1 ? 1 : -1;
  ```

     ```ts
     /** The first day of the week holding `iso`, for a week that starts on `weekStartsOn` (0 Sunday, 1 Monday, 6 Saturday). */
     function weekStartOf(iso: string, weekStartsOn: 0 | 1 | 6): string {
       return addDays(iso, -((weekdayOf(iso) - weekStartsOn + 7) % 7));
     }
     ```

  ```ts
  import type { RoutineRun } from "@/lib/v3/routine-run";

  export type RoutinesState = "default" | "empty" | "loading" | "offline" | "resume";
  export type RoutinesView = {
    /** Saved runs by routine id; null while the phone's copy is still being read. */
    runs: Readonly<Record<string, RoutineRun | null>> | null;
    /** false shows the empty state (no bundled routines). */
    hasRoutines: boolean;
  };

  const PAUSED_AT = (() => {
    const d = new Date();
    d.setHours(8, 30, 0, 0);
    return d.getTime();
  })();

  export const FIXTURES: Record<RoutinesState, RoutinesView> = {
    default: { runs: {}, hasRoutines: true },
    empty: { runs: {}, hasRoutines: false },
    loading: { runs: null, hasRoutines: true },
    offline: { runs: {}, hasRoutines: true },
    resume: {
      runs: { "desk-unlock": { routineId: "desk-unlock", index: 2, marks: ["done", "done", "open", "open"], paused: true, pausedAt: PAUSED_AT, finished: false, updatedAt: PAUSED_AT } },
      hasRoutines: true,
    },
  };
  ```

### TFV2-0335 — Study track: SM-2 scheduling helper `scheduleSm2` (`convex/lib/sm2.ts`)
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent
- **Stage:** E · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); area `backend`; lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** PRD F-90 ("Record → notes → flashcards → test; SM-2; recall quiz; Anki export; scoped RAG. It is a separate mode, never mixed into Today."); the SM-2 algorithm as published by SuperMemo (https://super-memory.com/english/ol/sm2.htm). `convex/lib/sm2.ts` does not exist on `integration`. `study.createCard` (TFV2-0337a) and `study.reviewCard` (TFV2-0337c) use it. CONVENTIONS §9 "Pure helper".
- **GOAL:** `convex/lib/sm2.ts` exports the pure function `scheduleSm2(prev, quality)` and its constants, mapping a card's SM-2 state and an answer quality 0–5 to the next state, proven by its own test file.
- **SCOPE:** `convex/lib/sm2.ts` · test: `convex/lib/sm2.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `convex/lib/sm2.ts` (new) · `convex/lib/sm2.test.ts` (new). No table, no data.
- **STEPS:**
  1. Code-map check: `ls convex/lib/sm2.ts convex/lib/sm2.test.ts` → both missing (if either exists, stop and report `blocked: file exists`).
  2. Create `convex/lib/sm2.ts` with exactly the SPEC exports. It imports nothing (no Convex, no `_generated`).
  3. Create `convex/lib/sm2.test.ts` (`import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";`) with the 8 TESTS cases inside `describe("scheduleSm2 (TFV2-0335)", …)`; compare `easeFactor` with `toBeCloseTo(value, 10)`.
  4. Run DONE.
- **DONE:** `bun test convex/lib/sm2.test.ts` → `8 pass`, `0 fail`; `bun run typecheck` → exit 0.
- **EVIDENCE:** the summary of `bun test convex/lib/sm2.test.ts` and the summary of `bun run typecheck`, plus the typecheck exit code pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** read or write the database; import anything; round `easeFactor`; change the formulas to another algorithm (SM-5, FSRS); touch `convex/schema.ts`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0335 / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: convex/lib/sm2.ts, convex/lib/sm2.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 with evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // convex/lib/sm2.ts — pure, no imports
  export const SM2_INITIAL_EASE = 2.5;
  export const SM2_MIN_EASE = 1.3;
  export const SM2_DAY_MS = 86_400_000;
  export type Sm2Quality = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
  export type Sm2State = { repetitions: number; easeFactor: number; intervalDays: number };
  export function scheduleSm2(prev: Sm2State, quality: number): Sm2State;
  ```
  Validation, in this order:
  1. `!Number.isInteger(quality) || quality < 0 || quality > 5` → `throw new RangeError("quality must be an integer from 0 to 5")`.
  2. `!Number.isInteger(prev.repetitions) || prev.repetitions < 0 || !Number.isFinite(prev.easeFactor) || prev.easeFactor < SM2_MIN_EASE || !Number.isFinite(prev.intervalDays) || prev.intervalDays < 0` → `throw new RangeError("invalid SM-2 state")`. (A new card has `intervalDays: 0`, which is valid.)

  Rules (SM-2 steps 4–6):
  - `quality < 3` → return `{ repetitions: 0, easeFactor: prev.easeFactor, intervalDays: 1 }` (repetitions restart; the E-Factor is not changed, per the published text "start repetitions for the item from the beginning without changing the E-Factor").
  - `quality >= 3` → `n = prev.repetitions + 1`; `intervalDays = n === 1 ? 1 : n === 2 ? 6 : Math.round(prev.intervalDays * prev.easeFactor)`; `easeFactor = Math.max(SM2_MIN_EASE, prev.easeFactor + (0.1 - (5 - quality) * (0.08 + (5 - quality) * 0.02)))`; return `{ repetitions: n, easeFactor, intervalDays }`.
  - The returned `intervalDays` is always an integer ≥ 1. `easeFactor` is never below 1.3 and is not rounded.
  Errors (exact → trigger): `RangeError("quality must be an integer from 0 to 5")` → quality not an integer in 0–5; `RangeError("invalid SM-2 state")` → a non-integer or negative `repetitions`, a non-finite or < 1.3 `easeFactor`, or a non-finite or negative `intervalDays`. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `{ repetitions: 0, easeFactor: 2.5, intervalDays: 0 }` and quality 5 / When `scheduleSm2` runs / Then it returns `repetitions: 1`, `intervalDays: 1`, `easeFactor` ≈ 2.6.
  2. Given `{ repetitions: 1, easeFactor: 2.6, intervalDays: 1 }` and quality 4 / Then `repetitions: 2`, `intervalDays: 6`, `easeFactor` ≈ 2.6 (quality 4 leaves it unchanged).
  3. Given `{ repetitions: 2, easeFactor: 2.5, intervalDays: 6 }` and quality 5 / Then `repetitions: 3`, `intervalDays: 15` (`Math.round(6 × 2.5)`), `easeFactor` ≈ 2.6.
  4. Given `{ repetitions: 4, easeFactor: 2.0, intervalDays: 10 }` and quality 3 / Then `repetitions: 5`, `intervalDays: 20`, `easeFactor` ≈ 1.86.
  5. Given `{ repetitions: 5, easeFactor: 2.2, intervalDays: 30 }` and quality 2 / Then it returns exactly `{ repetitions: 0, easeFactor: 2.2, intervalDays: 1 }`.
  6. Given `{ repetitions: 3, easeFactor: 1.3, intervalDays: 8 }` and quality 3 / Then `easeFactor` is exactly `1.3` (clamped) and `intervalDays` is `10` (`Math.round(8 × 1.3)`).
  7. Given quality `6`, then `-1`, then `2.5` / Then each throws a `RangeError` with message `"quality must be an integer from 0 to 5"`.
  8. Given `{ repetitions: -1, easeFactor: 2.5, intervalDays: 0 }`, then `{ repetitions: 0, easeFactor: 1.2, intervalDays: 0 }`, then `{ repetitions: 0, easeFactor: 2.5, intervalDays: Number.NaN }` with quality 4 / Then each throws a `RangeError` with message `"invalid SM-2 state"`.
- **NUMBERS:** SM-2 constants: E-Factor floor 1.3, starting E-Factor 2.5, I(1) = 1 day, I(2) = 6 days, I(n) = round(I(n−1) × EF) (https://super-memory.com/english/ol/sm2.htm); one day = 86,400,000 ms (`SM2_DAY_MS`); 8 of 8 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure function).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

  ```ts
  export const studyCardValidator = v.object({
    _id: v.id("studyCards"),
    front: v.string(),
    back: v.string(),
    sourceNoteId: v.union(v.id("notes"), v.null()),
    repetitions: v.number(),
    easeFactor: v.number(),
    intervalDays: v.number(),
    dueAtMs: v.number(),
    status: v.union(v.literal("new"), v.literal("learning"), v.literal("reviewing")),
  });
  export type StudyCardView = {
    _id: Id<"studyCards">; front: string; back: string; sourceNoteId: Id<"notes"> | null;
    repetitions: number; easeFactor: number; intervalDays: number; dueAtMs: number;
    status: "new" | "learning" | "reviewing";
  };
  /** Maps a row to StudyCardView; a missing sourceNoteId becomes null. */
  export function toStudyCard(doc: Doc<"studyCards">): StudyCardView;
  export const LIST_DUE_DEFAULT = 50;
  export const LIST_DUE_MAX = 100;
  export const LIST_DUE_SCAN_MAX = 500;
  export const listDue = query({
    args: { nowMs: v.number(), sourceNoteId: v.optional(v.union(v.id("notes"), v.null())), limit: v.optional(v.number()) },
    returns: v.array(studyCardValidator),
    handler: async (
      ctx: QueryCtx,
      args: { nowMs: number; sourceNoteId?: Id<"notes"> | null; limit?: number },
    ): Promise<StudyCardView[]> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Steps: `const user = await requireUser(ctx);` → `limit` = `LIST_DUE_DEFAULT` when `args.limit` is missing or not finite, else `Math.min(LIST_DUE_MAX, Math.max(1, Math.floor(args.limit)))` → `rows = await ctx.db.query("studyCards").withIndex("by_userId_dueAtMs", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).lt("dueAtMs", args.nowMs + 1)).take(LIST_DUE_SCAN_MAX)` (ascending `dueAtMs`) → keep rows with `deletedAt === undefined` and, by `args.sourceNoteId`: `undefined` → every deck; `null` → only rows without `sourceNoteId`; an id → only rows whose `sourceNoteId` equals it → `slice(0, limit)` → `map(toStudyCard)`.
  The deck filter runs after the bounded read, so a deck's cards that sort after the caller's first 500 due cards are not returned in this call (they come back once earlier cards are reviewed). Errors: `"Not authenticated"` (from `requireUser`; also `"User not found"`, `"This account is not active"`). No user-facing copy.

  4. Given 120 due cards / When it runs with no `limit`, with `limit: 500`, with `limit: 0` and with `limit: 2.7` / Then it returns 50, 100, 1 and 2 cards.
  5. Given 500 due cards without a note (`dueAtMs` 1…500) and one deck-A card with `dueAtMs` 501, `nowMs: 1000` / When it runs with `sourceNoteId: noteA` / Then it returns `[]` (the read stops at `LIST_DUE_SCAN_MAX` = 500 rows); and with only 499 note-less cards (deck-A card at `dueAtMs` 500) it returns that one deck-A card.
  6. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / When `listDue({ nowMs: 1 })` runs / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const NOTE_CARDS_MAX = 100;
  export const NOTE_CARD_FRONT_MAX = 200;
  export const NOTE_CARD_BACK_MAX = 500;
  export const NOTE_PASSAGES_MAX = 200;
  export const PASSAGE_MAX = 500;
  export type CardSuggestion = { front: string; back: string };
  /** The body's Markdown with every json tempo block (valid or broken) removed: the "markdown" segments' source joined with "\n". */
  export function markdownOnly(body: string): string;
  export function cardsFromMarkdown(body: string): CardSuggestion[];
  export function notePassages(body: string): string[];
  ```
  `clip(text, max)` (not exported): `text.length <= max ? text : text.slice(0, max - 1) + "…"`.
  `cardsFromMarkdown`: lines = `markdownOnly(body).split(/\r?\n/)`. A line whose trimmed text starts with `` ``` `` or `~~~` toggles "in code"; fence lines and lines in code count as blank and never make a card. Walk lines top to bottom:
  - **Heading card:** a line matching `/^#{2,3}\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$/` (levels 2–3; a level-1 `# ` title is ignored) → front = the captured text trimmed. Skip following blank lines; then the paragraph = the consecutive non-blank lines that do not match `/^#{1,6}\s/`, the Q pattern or the A pattern, each trimmed, joined with `" "`. Non-empty paragraph → card `{ front: clip(front, 200), back: clip(paragraph, 500) }`; empty → no card. Continue after the paragraph.
  - **Q/A card:** a line matching `/^\s*[-*]\s+Q:\s*(.+)$/i` whose next non-blank line matches `/^\s*[-*]\s+A:\s*(.+)$/i` → card `{ front: clip(q.trim(), 200), back: clip(a.trim(), 500) }`; continue after the A line. A Q line without that A line makes no card.
  - Cards keep the order they appear; stop at 100 cards.
  `notePassages`: `markdownOnly(body)` split on `/\n\s*\n/`, each part trimmed, empty parts dropped, each `clip(part, 500)`, at most 200 parts in order.
  No errors are thrown. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `"# Page\n\n## Mitochondria\nThe powerhouse of the cell."` / When `cardsFromMarkdown` runs / Then it returns `[{ front: "Mitochondria", back: "The powerhouse of the cell." }]`.
  2. Given `"### Osmosis\nWater moves\nacross a membrane.\n\nUnrelated line"` / Then it returns `[{ front: "Osmosis", back: "Water moves across a membrane." }]`.
  3. Given `"- Q: Capital of France?\n- A: Paris\n* q: 2 + 2?\n\n* a: 4"` / Then it returns `[{ front: "Capital of France?", back: "Paris" }, { front: "2 + 2?", back: "4" }]`.
  4. Given `"- Q: Lonely question\nplain text\n## Empty\n## Next\nBody"` / Then it returns only `[{ front: "Next", back: "Body" }]` (the Q has no A; `Empty` has no paragraph).
  5. Given ``"## Term\n```json tempo\n{}\n```\nDefinition."`` / Then it returns `[{ front: "Term", back: "Definition." }]`; and given ``"## Code\n```js\nconst a = 1;\n```"`` / Then it returns `[]`.
  6. Given a heading of 250 `"h"` characters followed by a paragraph of 600 `"p"` characters / Then the card's `front.length` is 200, `back.length` is 500, and both end with `"…"`; and a 200-character heading with a 500-character paragraph gives a card with both unchanged (no `"…"`).
  7. Given 150 `- Q:` / `- A:` pairs / Then it returns 100 cards, the first being the first pair; and exactly 100 pairs return 100 cards.
  8. Given `""` / Then `cardsFromMarkdown("")` and `notePassages("")` both return `[]`.
  9. Given ``"Para one.\n\nPara two\nline two.\n\n\n```json tempo\n{}\n```"`` / When `notePassages` runs / Then it returns `["Para one.", "Para two\nline two."]`; and a single 600-character paragraph returns one passage of length 500 ending `"…"`, a 500-character paragraph is returned unchanged; and 201 one-word paragraphs return 200 passages while exactly 200 return 200.
- **NUMBERS:** at most 100 card suggestions (`NOTE_CARDS_MAX`, tested with 150), front ≤ 200 and back ≤ 500 characters (tested at 250 / 600), at most 200 passages of ≤ 500 characters; all well under `STUDY_FIELD_MAX` 2,000 (TFV2-0337a); 9 of 9 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.

  ```ts
  export const ANKI_EXPORT_MAX = 1000;
  export const ANKI_HEADER = "#separator:tab\n#html:false\n";
  export const exportAnki = query({
    args: { sourceNoteId: v.optional(v.union(v.id("notes"), v.null())) },
    returns: v.object({ text: v.string(), count: v.number(), truncated: v.boolean() }),
    handler: async (
      ctx: QueryCtx,
      args: { sourceNoteId?: Id<"notes"> | null },
    ): Promise<{ text: string; count: number; truncated: boolean }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Steps: `const user = await requireUser(ctx);` → `rows = await ctx.db.query("studyCards").withIndex("by_userId_deletedAt", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).eq("deletedAt", undefined)).take(ANKI_EXPORT_MAX + 1)` → `truncated = rows.length > ANKI_EXPORT_MAX`; use `rows.slice(0, ANKI_EXPORT_MAX)` → filter by `args.sourceNoteId` (`undefined` → every deck; `null` → rows without `sourceNoteId`; an id → rows with that `sourceNoteId`) → each card becomes the line `clean(front) + "\t" + clean(back)` where `clean(s) = s.replace(/[\t\r\n]+/g, " ").trim()` → `count` = number of lines → `text` = `count === 0 ? "" : ANKI_HEADER + lines.join("\n") + "\n"`. Order: index order (creation order).
  Errors: `"Not authenticated"` (from `requireUser`; also `"User not found"`, `"This account is not active"`). No user-facing copy.

  3. Given a deck-A card (`"QA"`, `"AA"`) and a card without a note (`"QN"`, `"AN"`) / When it runs with `sourceNoteId: noteA`, then with `sourceNoteId: null` / Then the first text holds only the `QA` line and the second only the `QN` line, each with `count: 1`.
  4. Given a card of `users:1` with `deletedAt: 5` and a card of `users:2` / When `users:1` runs it / Then it returns `{ text: "", count: 0, truncated: false }`.
  5. Given no cards / Then it returns `{ text: "", count: 0, truncated: false }`.
  6. Given 1,001 live cards / Then `count` is 1000 and `truncated` is `true`; and with exactly 1,000 cards `count` is 1000 and `truncated` is `false`.
  7. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / When `exportAnki({})` runs / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.

  |---|---|---|

  Render, top to bottom inside `<View style={{ gap: 16 }}>`:

  States (harness sections, in order): `unanswered` (interactive), `selected` (choice b chosen, not checked), `correct` (choice a chosen, checked), `wrong` (choice c chosen, checked), `disabled` (nothing chosen, `disabled: true`).

- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0345a / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: apps/mobile/lib/v3/studyQuiz.ts, tests/unit/mobile_study_quiz.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 with evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // apps/mobile/lib/v3/studyQuiz.ts — pure, no imports
  export const TEST_QUESTIONS_MAX = 10;
  export const TEST_CHOICES_MAX = 4;
  export type QuizSourceCard = { id: string; front: string; back: string };
  export type TestChoice = { id: string; label: string };
  export type TestQuestion = { id: string; question: string; choices: TestChoice[]; correctId: string };
  /** null when the cards have fewer than 2 different answers. */
  export function buildQuiz(cards: readonly QuizSourceCard[]): TestQuestion[] | null;
  ```
  Rules:
  1. `pool` = one `TestChoice` per different answer, in card order: for each card, `label = card.back.trim()`; skip `""`; keep the first card per label (`{ id: card.id, label }`).
  2. `pool.length < 2` → return `null`.
  3. For each of the first `TEST_QUESTIONS_MAX` cards with a non-empty trimmed back, at question position `i` (0-based): `correct` = the pool entry whose `label` equals the card's trimmed back; `n = Math.min(TEST_CHOICES_MAX, pool.length)`; distractors = the next `n - 1` pool entries after `correct`, walking forward and wrapping to the start (`pool[(p + 1) % pool.length]`, `pool[(p + 2) % pool.length]`, … where `p` is `correct`'s pool index); `choices = [correct, ...distractors]`; rotate so `correct` lands at index `i % n`: `k = (n - (i % n)) % n; choices = [...choices.slice(k), ...choices.slice(0, k)]`.
  4. Question = `{ id: card.id, question: card.front.trim(), choices, correctId: correct.id }`.
  No errors are thrown. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given cards `[{ id: "A", front: "Q1", back: "Paris" }, { id: "B", front: "Q2", back: "4" }, { id: "C", front: "Q3", back: "Blue" }]` / When `buildQuiz` runs / Then it returns 3 questions with ids `A`, `B`, `C`, questions `Q1`, `Q2`, `Q3`, correct ids `A`, `B`, `C`, and every question's `choices` equals `[{ id: "A", label: "Paris" }, { id: "B", label: "4" }, { id: "C", label: "Blue" }]` (so the correct choice is at index 0, 1, 2).
  2. Given cards A (`back: "Paris"`), B (`back: " Paris "`) and C (`back: "Rome"`) / Then question B's `correctId` is `"A"` and every question has exactly 2 choices.
  3. Given one card, and separately two cards both with `back: "Same"` / Then `buildQuiz` returns `null` for each.
  4. Given 12 cards with 12 different backs / Then it returns 10 questions, each with 4 choices whose ids are all different, and question `i` has its correct choice at index `i % 4`.
  5. Given the 12 cards of case 4 / When `buildQuiz` runs twice / Then both results are deeply equal.
  6. Given `[]` / Then it returns `null`.
- **NUMBERS:** at most 10 questions (`TEST_QUESTIONS_MAX`, tested with 12 cards) and at most 4 choices (`TEST_CHOICES_MAX`); 6 of 6 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.

  ```ts
  export const startExecutorConnect = action({
    args: { returnTo: v.optional(v.union(v.literal("settings"), v.literal("coach"))) },
    returns: v.object({ authorizationUrl: v.string() }),
    handler: async (ctx: ActionCtx, args: { returnTo?: "settings" | "coach" }): Promise<{ authorizationUrl: string }> =>
      startExecutorConnectFlow(ctx, args, defaultConnectionDeps()),
  });
  export async function startExecutorConnectFlow(
    ctx: Pick<ActionCtx, "runQuery" | "runMutation">,
    args: { returnTo?: "settings" | "coach" },
    deps: { fetch: FetchLike; env: Record<string, string | undefined>; now: () => number },
  ): Promise<{ authorizationUrl: string }>;
  ```
  Order (code truth): `requireApprovedForAi` (runs `approval.assertApprovedForAi` → `requireApprovedUser` → `requireUser`); then `executorConfig(env)` and `loadConnectionsKey(env)`; then `reserveConnectAttempt` (counts one attempt in the person's `connectionLimits` row: window `HOUR_MS` = 3,600,000 ms, cap `CONNECT_ATTEMPTS_PER_HOUR` = 5; a window older than `HOUR_MS` restarts at count 1); then discovery, client registration (one `oauthClients` row per issuer + redirect URI), PKCE and `createPending` (row `{ userId, provider: "executor", stateHash, codeVerifierCipher, returnTo: args.returnTo ?? "settings", startGeneration: <connectionLimits.disconnectGeneration ?? 0>, expiresAt: now + PENDING_TTL_MS, … }`, `PENDING_TTL_MS` = 600,000 ms). Errors (exact → trigger → test):
  - `Error("Not authenticated")` → no identity → new case 1.
  - `Error("This account is not active")` → the users row has `isActive: false` → new case 2.
  - `Error(PENDING_APPROVAL_MESSAGE)` (`"ACCOUNT_PENDING_APPROVAL: your account is waiting for approval."`) → pending account → existing test "a pending account cannot start, and nothing is fetched".
  - `ConvexError({ code: "unavailable", message: "Executor isn't available right now. Nothing changed." })` → Executor off or misconfigured, or a discovery/registration failure → existing tests "<variant>: status unavailable, enabled false, and nothing is fetched" and "a mismatched issuer or no S256 stops the connect in Tempo's words; the log names the kind only".
  - `ConvexError({ code: "rate_limited", message: "That's a lot of connect attempts. Try again in a bit." })` → sixth attempt inside the hour → existing test "at most five connect attempts an hour; the sixth calls nothing".
  `"User not found"` needs an identity with an email, which this file's fake never sends (its identity is `{ subject }` only); it is not tested here. No user-facing copy beyond the two `ConvexError` messages above (English; the settings screen maps the code).
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `makeWorld()` and `fakeExecutor()` / When `connections.startExecutorConnectFlow(world.actionAs(null), {}, deps(executor))` runs / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"`, `executor.calls` has length 0 and `world.rows("connectionLimits")` has length 0.
  2. Given `await world.db.patch(A, { isActive: false })` / When `startExecutorConnectFlow(world.actionAs(A), {}, deps(executor))` runs / Then it rejects with `"This account is not active"` and `executor.calls` has length 0.
  3. Given a `connectionLimits` row `{ userId: A, connectWindowStartMs: Date.now() - connections.HOUR_MS - 1, connectWindowCount: connections.CONNECT_ATTEMPTS_PER_HOUR, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1 }` / When `startConnect(world, executor)` runs / Then it resolves, the row's `connectWindowCount` is `1` and its `connectWindowStartMs` is at least the `Date.now()` read before the call.
  4. Given a person with no `connectionLimits` row / When `startConnect(world, executor, A, "coach")` runs / Then the one `oauthPending` row has `returnTo: "coach"` and `startGeneration: 0`.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export async function handleExecutorCallback(
    ctx: Pick<ActionCtx, "runQuery" | "runMutation">,
    request: Request,
    deps: { fetch: FetchLike; env: Record<string, string | undefined>; now: () => number },
  ): Promise<Response>;
  export const executorCallback = httpAction(async (ctx, request) => handleExecutorCallback(ctx, request, defaultConnectionDeps())); // convex/connectionsHttp.ts, unchanged
  ```
  Every answer carries `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; redirects go to `<SITE_URL>/settings/integrations?executor=<result>` (or `/coach?executor=<result>` for `returnTo: "coach"`). Guards this ticket proves (trigger → answer):
  - `state` absent or longer than 512 characters → 302 to `…?executor=expired`; `consumePending` is not called, so the attempt stays unspent.
  - attempt spent, then `code` absent or longer than 4,096 characters → 302 to `…?executor=error`; no request to the token endpoint.
  - the attempt's `oauthClients` row has `deletedAt` set → `consumePending` spends the attempt and returns `error` → 302 to `…?executor=error`; no token request.
  No thrown errors (the callback always answers with a redirect or the 503 text, which existing tests cover). No user-facing copy is added.
- **TESTS:**

  ```ts
  export const confirmExecutorConnect = action({
    args: { nonce: v.string() },
    returns: v.object({ status: v.union(v.literal("connected"), v.literal("expired"), v.literal("mismatch"), v.literal("error")) }),
    handler: async (ctx: ActionCtx, args: { nonce: string }): Promise<{ status: "connected" | "expired" | "mismatch" | "error" }> =>
      confirmExecutorConnectFlow(ctx, args, defaultConnectionDeps()),
  });
  ```
  Behaviour: `nonce.trim()` not matching `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,128}$/` → `{ status: "expired" }` with no mutation; else `confirmStaged({ nonceHash: sha256Hex(nonce) })`, then every id in its `revoke` list is revoked at Executor (refresh token first, then access token) and scrubbed. Statuses: `connected` (owner, active, approved, within `CONFIRM_TTL_MS` = 600,000 ms, no later disconnect); `expired`; `mismatch` (another person); `error` (owner inactive — `deletedAt` set or `isActive === false` — or not approved). Thrown error: `Error("Not authenticated")` when nobody is signed in → existing test "a late confirm is expired and revokes; an unknown or malformed nonce is expired; signed out is refused". No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given a staged connect with nonce `n` / When `confirm(world, executor, "  " + n + "  ")` runs / Then it returns `{ status: "connected" }` and the connection row has `status: "connected"`.
  2. Given a staged connect / When `confirm(world, executor, "short-nonce-123")` (15 characters) runs / Then it returns `{ status: "expired" }`, the staged row still has `status: "pending_confirm"` and no `deletedAt`, and `executor.revoked` is `[]`.
  3. Given a staged connect with nonce `n` and then `await world.db.patch(A, { isActive: false })` / When `confirm(world, executor, n)` runs / Then it returns `{ status: "error" }`, `executor.revoked` has length 2, and the staged row has `status: "disconnected"`.
- **NUMBERS:** `85 pass`, `0 fail` for the whole file (82 before + 3 new; exact). Nonce length 16–128 characters (code pattern); confirm life 600,000 ms (`CONFIRM_TTL_MS`). Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline measured in this repo; not a gate) — CONVENTIONS §20.

  ```ts
  export type ExecutorSearchOutcome =

    | { status: "not_connected" | "needs_reauth" | "unavailable" | "rate_limited" | "busy" };
  export async function searchExecutorFor(

    userId: Id<"users">,
    query: string,
    deps: { fetch: FetchLike; env: Record<string, string | undefined>; now: () => number },
  ): Promise<ExecutorSearchOutcome>;
  ```

  Auth: none of its own (the caller `coach.runExecutorLookup` checks approval and the conversation); it reads only `userId`'s usable connection (`secretsForCall`). Order: Executor off or key missing → `unavailable` before any read or fetch; no usable connection → `not_connected` / `needs_reauth`; a changed MCP URL → revoke + `needs_reauth`; `reserveCall` (cap `CALLS_PER_HOUR` = 30 per person per `HOUR_MS`); refresh when the token ends within `REFRESH_EARLY_MS` = 60,000 ms; one MCP session `initialize` → `tools/list` → `tools/call` of `search` only (`SEARCH_TOOL`), timeout 15,000 ms (`MCP_CLIENT_LIMITS.timeoutMs`). - **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const recordCall = internalMutation({
    args: {
      connectionId: v.id("connections"),
      tool: v.string(),
      decision: v.union(v.literal("auto"), v.literal("approved"), v.literal("rejected"), v.literal("blocked")),
      outcome: v.union(v.literal("ok"), v.literal("error"), v.literal("approval_required"), v.literal("timeout"), v.literal("rate_limited"), v.literal("unauthorized")),
      inputDigest: v.optional(v.string()),
      resultBytes: v.optional(v.number()),
      durationMs: v.optional(v.number()),
    },
    returns: v.union(v.null(), v.id("connectionCalls")),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { connectionId: Id<"connections">; tool: string; decision: "auto" | "approved" | "rejected" | "blocked"; outcome: "ok" | "error" | "approval_required" | "timeout" | "rate_limited" | "unauthorized"; inputDigest?: string; resultBytes?: number; durationMs?: number }): Promise<Id<"connectionCalls"> | null> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Internal (no auth; callers are actions that already resolved the person). Missing connection → `null`, nothing written. Otherwise inserts `{ userId: <connection's>, connectionId, kind: "tool_call", tool, decision, outcome, createdAt, updatedAt }` plus `inputDigest`, `resultBytes`, `durationMs` only when passed. `outcome === "ok"` on a connection without `deletedAt` patches `lastUsedAt: now`, and when its status is `unavailable` also `status: "connected"` and removes `lastErrorAt`. No thrown errors; no user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `makeWorld()` / When `recordCall({ connectionId: "connections:999", tool: "search", decision: "auto", outcome: "ok" })` runs / Then it returns `null` and `world.rows("connectionCalls")` has length 0.
  2. Given a connected row / When `recordCall({ connectionId, tool: "search", decision: "auto", outcome: "timeout" })` runs (no digest, bytes or duration) / Then the inserted row's sorted keys equal `["_creationTime", "_id", "connectionId", "createdAt", "decision", "kind", "outcome", "tool", "updatedAt", "userId"]`, `kind` is `"tool_call"`, `userId` is `A`, and the connection has no `lastUsedAt`.
  3. Given a connected row patched to `{ status: "unavailable", lastErrorAt: 5 }` / When `recordCall({ …, outcome: "ok", inputDigest: "a".repeat(64), resultBytes: 10, durationMs: 3 })` runs / Then the connection has `status: "connected"`, no `lastErrorAt`, a numeric `lastUsedAt`, and the audit row has `inputDigest`, `resultBytes: 10`, `durationMs: 3`.
  4. Given a connection after `connections.disconnectFlow(world.actionAs(A), deps(executor))` (status `disconnected`, `deletedAt` set) / When `recordCall({ …, outcome: "ok" })` runs / Then a new audit row with `userId: A` exists and the connection has no `lastUsedAt` and still `status: "disconnected"`.
- **NUMBERS:** `93 pass`, `0 fail` for the whole file (89 before + 4 new; exact). Audit rows carry 0 bytes of input or result text (key set asserted in case 2). Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline measured in this repo; not a gate) — CONVENTIONS §20.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const reserveCall = internalMutation({
    args: { connectionId: v.id("connections") },
    returns: v.union(v.literal("ok"), v.literal("rate_limited"), v.literal("gone")),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { connectionId: Id<"connections"> }): Promise<"ok" | "rate_limited" | "gone"> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Internal. `gone` when the row is missing, has `deletedAt`, or its status is neither `connected` nor `unavailable` (no count written). Otherwise counts one call in the person's `connectionLimits` row (`callWindowStartMs`, `callWindowCount`; window `HOUR_MS` = 3,600,000 ms; cap `CALLS_PER_HOUR` = 30): `ok`, or `rate_limited` when the window already holds 30. No thrown errors; no user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given a connected row (`connectFully`) / When `reserveCall` runs / Then it returns `"ok"` and A's `connectionLimits` row has `callWindowCount: 1`.
  2. Given that row patched to `status: "unavailable"` / When `reserveCall` runs / Then it returns `"ok"`.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  /** Shared by `upsert` and the MCP `today_plan_set` tool. The caller has resolved `userId`. */
  export async function upsertDayPlanForUser(
  	ctx: MutationCtx,
  	userId: Id<"users">,
  	args: { localDate: string; timezone?: string; intention?: string; topTaskIds?: Id<"tasks">[]; energy?: "low" | "medium" | "high" },
  ): Promise<Id<"dayPlans">> {
  	assertLocalDate(args.localDate);
  	if (args.topTaskIds !== undefined) {
  		await assertOwnedTasks(ctx, userId, args.topTaskIds);
  	}
  	const now = Date.now();
  	const fields: Partial<Doc<"dayPlans">> = {};
  	if (args.timezone !== undefined) fields.timezone = args.timezone;
  	if (args.intention !== undefined) fields.intention = args.intention.trim();
  	if (args.topTaskIds !== undefined) fields.topTaskIds = args.topTaskIds;
  	if (args.energy !== undefined) fields.energy = args.energy;
  	const existing = await findLivePlan(ctx, userId, args.localDate);
  	if (existing) {
  		// Patch only: never touches `status`, so a committed plan stays committed.
  		await ctx.db.patch(existing._id, { ...fields, updatedAt: now });
  		return existing._id;
  	}
  	return ctx.db.insert("dayPlans", { userId, localDate: args.localDate, ...fields, status: "draft", createdAt: now, updatedAt: now });
  }
  export const upsert = mutation({ /* args and returns unchanged */
  	handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { localDate: string; timezone?: string; intention?: string; topTaskIds?: Id<"tasks">[]; energy?: "low" | "medium" | "high" }): Promise<Id<"dayPlans">> => {
  		const user = await requireUser(ctx);
  		return upsertDayPlanForUser(ctx, user._id, args);
  	},
  });
  ```
  Helper: no auth. Errors (plain `Error`, in this order): `"localDate must be YYYY-MM-DD"` — not a real date; `"A day plan can have at most 3 top tasks"` — more than `MAX_TOP_TASKS` = 3 ids; `"Task not found"` — an id that is missing, belongs to another `userId`, or is soft-deleted. A throw writes nothing. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given the file's `makeFakeCtx(USER)` and two USER tasks `t1 = await addTask(ctx)`, `t2 = await addTask(ctx)` / When `upsertDayPlanForUser(ctx, USER, { localDate: "2026-10-05", timezone: "UTC", intention: " Rest ", topTaskIds: [t1, t2], energy: "low" })` runs / Then the returned id's row has `userId: USER`, `status: "draft"`, `intention: "Rest"`, `timezone: "UTC"`, `energy: "low"`, `topTaskIds: [t1, t2]`.
  2. Given that plan / When `upsertDayPlanForUser(ctx, USER, { localDate: "2026-10-05", energy: "high" })` runs / Then it returns the same id, the row has `energy: "high"` and `intention: "Rest"`, and exactly one `dayPlans` row exists.
  3. Given a USER task / When `upsertDayPlanForUser(ctx, "users:b", { localDate: "2026-10-05", topTaskIds: [it] })` runs / Then it rejects with `"Task not found"` and no `dayPlans` row exists.
  4. Given `makeFakeCtx(USER)` / When `upsertDayPlanForUser(ctx, USER, { localDate: "2026-02-30" })` runs / Then it rejects with `"localDate must be YYYY-MM-DD"`.
  5. Given four USER tasks / When `upsertDayPlanForUser(ctx, USER, { localDate: "2026-10-05", topTaskIds: [all four] })` runs / Then it rejects with `"A day plan can have at most 3 top tasks"` and no `dayPlans` row exists; and with the first three it resolves and the row's `topTaskIds` has length 3.
- **NUMBERS:** `44 pass` in `convex/dayPlans.test.ts` (39 before + 5 new) and `12 pass` in `convex/mcp.test.ts`, `0 fail` each (exact). Top tasks ≤ 3 (`MAX_TOP_TASKS`, case 5 seeds 4). Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline measured in this repo; not a gate) — CONVENTIONS §20.

  ```ts
  function dayPlanView(p: Doc<"dayPlans">) {
    return {
      id: p._id,
      date: p.localDate,
      timezone: p.timezone ?? null,
      status: p.status,
      intention: p.intention ?? null,
      energy: p.energy ?? null,
      topTaskIds: p.topTaskIds ?? [],
    };
  }
  // inside runWriteTool's switch:
      case "today_plan_set": {
        const timezone = (a.timezone as string | undefined) ?? "UTC";
        if (!isValidTimeZone(timezone)) throw new Error(`Unknown timezone: ${timezone}`);
        const date = (a.date as string | undefined) ?? localDateOf(timezone, Date.now());
        let topTaskIds: Id<"tasks">[] | undefined;
        if (a.topTaskIds !== undefined) {
          topTaskIds = [];
          for (const raw of a.topTaskIds as string[]) {
            const taskId = ctx.db.normalizeId("tasks", raw);
            if (!taskId) throw new Error("Task not found");
            topTaskIds.push(taskId);
          }
        }
        const dayPlanId = await upsertDayPlanForUser(ctx, userId, {
          localDate: date,
          timezone,
          ...(a.intention !== undefined ? { intention: a.intention as string } : {}),
          ...(a.energy !== undefined ? { energy: a.energy as "low" | "medium" | "high" } : {}),
          ...(topTaskIds !== undefined ? { topTaskIds } : {}),
        });
        const plan = await ctx.db.get(dayPlanId);
        return { plan: plan ? dayPlanView(plan) : { id: dayPlanId } };
      }
  ```

  ```ts
  export const mcpPost = httpAction(async (ctx: ActionCtx, request: Request): Promise<Response> => { … }); // unchanged
  // test harness in convex/mcpHttp.test.ts
  import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";
  import { getFunctionName } from "convex/server";
  import { hashToken } from "./lib/mcp/token";
  import { makeFakeCtx, run } from "./lib/testFakeCtx";
  import * as mcp from "./mcp";
  import * as mcpHttp from "./mcpHttp";
  import * as mcpTools from "./mcpTools";
  const A = "users:a";
  const TOKEN = `tmcp_${"A".repeat(43)}`; // token-shaped fake, not a real secret
  const HANDLERS: Record<string, unknown> = {
    "mcp:authorizeCall": mcp.authorizeCall,
    "mcpTools:runReadTool": mcpTools.runReadTool,
    "mcpTools:runWriteTool": mcpTools.runWriteTool,
    "mcpTools:runBrainDump": mcpTools.runBrainDump,
  };
  function httpCtx(ctx: ReturnType<typeof makeFakeCtx>) {
    const dispatch = (ref: unknown, args: unknown) => {
      const handler = HANDLERS[getFunctionName(ref as never)];
      if (!handler) throw new Error(`unexpected call ${getFunctionName(ref as never)}`);
      return run(handler, ctx, args);
    };
    return { runQuery: dispatch, runMutation: dispatch, runAction: dispatch };
  }
  async function seedToken(ctx: ReturnType<typeof makeFakeCtx>, extra: Record<string, unknown> = {}) {
    return ctx.db.insert("mcpTokens", { userId: A, name: "t", tokenHash: await hashToken(TOKEN), prefix: TOKEN.slice(0, 8), createdAt: 1, ...extra });
  }
  function post(body: string, headers: Record<string, string> = {}): Request {
    return new Request("https://tempo.test/mcp", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${TOKEN}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", ...headers }, body });
  }
  const send = (ctx: ReturnType<typeof makeFakeCtx>, request: Request) =>
    (mcpHttp.mcpPost as unknown as { _handler: (c: unknown, r: Request) => Promise<Response> })._handler(httpCtx(ctx), request);
  const PING = JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "ping" });
  ```
  Guard order (code truth) and answers; every answer has header `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18` and, with a body, `Content-Type: application/json`; error bodies are `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: null, error: { code, message } }`:
  1. `Origin` present, not localhost and not in `TEMPO_MCP_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` → 403, `code: -32600`, `message: "Origin not allowed"`.
  2. `Authorization` missing, not `Bearer <x>`, or `<x>` not `/^tmcp_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/` → 401, `-32600`, `"Missing or invalid token"`, header `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="tempo-mcp"`.
  3. `MCP-Protocol-Version` present and not one of `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`, `2024-11-05` → 400, `-32600`, `` `Unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version: ${version}` ``.
  4. `authorizeCall` → `unauthorized` (unknown, revoked or deleted-account token) → the same 401 as 2.
  5. `pending` → 403, `-32600`, `"ACCOUNT_PENDING_APPROVAL"` (`PENDING_APPROVAL_ERROR`).
  6. `rate_limited` → 429, `-32600`, `"Rate limit: 120 calls per minute"`, header `Retry-After: 60`.
  Guards 1–3 run before `authorizeCall`, so they never count a call.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given a seeded token / When `send(ctx, post(PING, { Origin: "https://evil.test" }))` runs / Then the status is 403, the body equals `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: null, error: { code: -32600, message: "Origin not allowed" } }`, the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header is `"2025-06-18"`, and the token row has no `windowCount`.
  2. Given a seeded token / When a request with no `Authorization` header, and one with `Authorization: "Bearer tmcp_short"`, are sent / Then both are 401 with message `"Missing or invalid token"` and header `WWW-Authenticate` = `Bearer realm="tempo-mcp"`.
  3. Given no token row / When `send(ctx, post(PING))` runs / Then the status is 401 with message `"Missing or invalid token"`.
  4. Given a seeded token / When `post(PING, { "MCP-Protocol-Version": "1999-01-01" })` is sent / Then the status is 400 with message `"Unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version: 1999-01-01"` and the token row has no `windowCount`.
  5. Given a seeded token and `ctx.db.patch(A, { approvalStatus: "pending" })` / When `post(PING)` is sent / Then the status is 403 with message `"ACCOUNT_PENDING_APPROVAL"`.
  6. Given a token seeded with `{ windowStartMs: Date.now(), windowCount: 120 }` / When `post(PING)` is sent / Then the status is 429, the message is `"Rate limit: 120 calls per minute"` and the `Retry-After` header is `"60"`; and with `Origin: "https://app.tempo.test"` and a fresh token row the same `PING` answers 200.
- **NUMBERS:** 6 of 6 cases pass (exact). HTTP statuses 400/401/403/429 per RFC 9110 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110) and JSON-RPC 2.0 error code `-32600` (https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification); rate 120 calls per token per 60,000 ms (`RATE_LIMIT_MAX_CALLS`, `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS` in `convex/mcp.ts`). Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline measured in this repo; not a gate) — CONVENTIONS §20.

  Body answers after the guards of TFV2-0358a (error bodies `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: null, error: { code, message } }`): over 262,144 bytes → 413, `-32600`, `"Request too large"`; not JSON → 400, `-32700`, `"Parse error"`; a JSON array → 400, `-32600`, `"JSON-RPC batches are not supported"`; not a request (`parseRequest` → null) → 400, `-32600`, `"Invalid request"`; a notification (no `id`) → 202, empty body, no `Content-Type`; a request → 200 with the `handleRpc` response. `tools/call` routing: kind `query` → `runQuery(internal.mcpTools.runReadTool, { userId, name, args })`; `mutation` → `runMutation(internal.mcpTools.runWriteTool, …)`; `action` → `runAction(internal.mcpTools.runBrainDump, { userId, text, accept })`; `userId` is the token owner from `authorizeCall`. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**

  3. Given a seeded token / When `post("not json")`, `post("[" + PING + "]")` and `post(JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: "2.0", result: 1 }))` are sent / Then each is 400 with, in order, `{ code: -32700, message: "Parse error" }`, `{ code: -32600, message: "JSON-RPC batches are not supported" }`, `{ code: -32600, message: "Invalid request" }`.

  6. Given a seeded token and one A task `await ctx.db.insert("tasks", { userId: A, title: "Seeded", status: "todo", priority: "medium", createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1 })` / When `tools/call` with `{ name: "tasks_list", arguments: {} }` and then `{ name: "task_create", arguments: { title: "From MCP" } }` are sent / Then the first `result.structuredContent.tasks` has length 1, and the second creates a `tasks` row with `userId: A` and `title: "From MCP"`.

  ```ts
  // packages/mcp-cli/src/index.ts
  export const MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2025-06-18";
  export const USAGE = "Usage: tempo-mcp tools | tempo-mcp call <tool> [json-arguments]";
  export type CliIo = {
    fetch: (url: string, init: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>;
    out: (line: string) => void;
    err: (line: string) => void;
  };
  /** Returns the process exit code: 0 ok, 1 runtime failure, 2 usage error. */
  export async function runCli(argv: string[], env: Record<string, string | undefined>, io: CliIo): Promise<number>;
  // packages/mcp-cli/src/cli.ts
  import { runCli } from "./index";
  const code = await runCli(process.argv.slice(2), process.env, { fetch: (url, init) => fetch(url, init), out: (l) => console.log(l), err: (l) => console.error(l) });
  process.exit(code);
  ```
  Behaviour of `runCli`, in this order:
  1. `argv[0]` is `"tools"` with no more items, or `"call"` with a tool name and at most one more item; anything else → `err(USAGE)`, return 2, no request.
  2. `env.TEMPO_MCP_TOKEN` empty or missing → `err("Missing TEMPO_MCP_TOKEN")`, return 1; `env.TEMPO_MCP_URL` empty or missing → `err("Missing TEMPO_MCP_URL")`, return 1.
  3. For `call`, the optional JSON text must parse to a plain object (not an array, not `null`) → else `err("Arguments must be a JSON object")`, return 2. Missing → `{}`.
  4. One request: `io.fetch(env.TEMPO_MCP_URL, { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: "Bearer " + token, "Content-Type": "application/json", Accept: "application/json", "MCP-Protocol-Version": MCP_PROTOCOL_VERSION }, body })` with body `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/list" }` or `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/call", params: { name, arguments } }`. A thrown fetch → `err("Could not reach TEMPO_MCP_URL")`, return 1.
  5. Status not 2xx → `err("Request failed (<status>): <error.message>")` when the body is a JSON-RPC error, else `err("Request failed (<status>)")`; return 1.
  6. A 200 JSON-RPC error → `err("Error <code>: <message>")`, return 1.
  7. `tools` → one `out` line per tool, `<name>\t<description>`, in server order; return 0. `call` with `result.isError === true` → `err("Tool error: " + <first text content>)`, return 1; else `out(JSON.stringify(result.structuredContent ?? result, null, 2))`, return 0.
  Messages are English only: the CLI is a developer tool whose output mirrors the English MCP tool metadata and backend error text (CONVENTIONS §11 keeps backend messages English). Nothing ever prints the token or the `Authorization` header.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `env = { TEMPO_MCP_URL: "https://tempo.test/mcp", TEMPO_MCP_TOKEN: "tmcp_" + "A".repeat(43) }` and a stub answering 200 `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, result: { tools: [{ name: "tasks_list", description: "List tasks" }, { name: "task_create", description: "Create a task." }] } }` / When `runCli(["tools"], env, io)` runs / Then it returns 0 and `out` lines equal `["tasks_list\tList tasks", "task_create\tCreate a task."]`.
  2. Given the same env and a stub answering 200 `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, result: { content: [], structuredContent: { tasks: [] } } }` / When `runCli(["call", "tasks_list", "{\"status\":\"all\"}"], env, io)` runs / Then it returns 0, the recorded body parses to `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/call", params: { name: "tasks_list", arguments: { status: "all" } } }`, the headers include `Authorization: "Bearer " + token` and `MCP-Protocol-Version: "2025-06-18"`, and `out` received `JSON.stringify({ tasks: [] }, null, 2)`.
  3. Given env without `TEMPO_MCP_TOKEN` / When `runCli(["tools"], env, io)` runs / Then it returns 1, `err` received `"Missing TEMPO_MCP_TOKEN"`, and the stub was not called; and without `TEMPO_MCP_URL` (token set) it returns 1 with `"Missing TEMPO_MCP_URL"`.
  4. Given `[]`, `["call"]`, `["nope"]`, `["tools", "x"]` and `["call", "tasks_list", "{}", "x"]` / When each runs / Then each returns 2 with `err` = `USAGE` and no request.
  5. Given `["call", "tasks_list", "[1]"]` and `["call", "tasks_list", "{bad"]` / When each runs / Then each returns 2 with `"Arguments must be a JSON object"` and no request.
  6. - **SPEC:** Pure server helper, exact code:
  ```ts
  import { CONNECTIONS_KEY_VERSION, SecretCryptoError, decryptSecret, encryptSecret, secretAad } from "./connections/crypto";

  /** The field every BYOK ciphertext is bound to (additional authenticated data). */
  export const BYOK_KEY_FIELD = "byokKeys.keyCipher";

  /** `tempo-connections|<userId>|byokKeys.keyCipher`: a ciphertext copied to another person's row does not decrypt. */
  export function byokAad(userId: string): string {
    return secretAad(userId, BYOK_KEY_FIELD);
  }

  /** Encrypts one person's API key. The plaintext never leaves this call. */
  export async function encryptByokKey(cryptoKey: CryptoKey, userId: string, plaintext: string): Promise<{ keyCipher: string; keyVersion: number }> {
    return { keyCipher: await encryptSecret(cryptoKey, plaintext, byokAad(userId)), keyVersion: CONNECTIONS_KEY_VERSION };
  }

  /** The plaintext of `encryptByokKey`'s ciphertext for the same person and key version; `SecretCryptoError` otherwise. */
  export async function decryptByokKey(cryptoKey: CryptoKey, userId: string, keyCipher: string, keyVersion: number): Promise<string> {
    if (keyVersion !== CONNECTIONS_KEY_VERSION) throw new SecretCryptoError("decrypt");
    return decryptSecret(cryptoKey, keyCipher, byokAad(userId));
  }

  /** What the vault shows instead of the key: first 3 characters, "…", last 4. Callers pass keys of at least 16 characters (TFV2-0361b). */
  export function byokKeyHint(plaintext: string): string {
    return `${plaintext.slice(0, 3)}…${plaintext.slice(-4)}`;
  }
  ```
  Errors: `SecretCryptoError` with message `"secret could not be decrypted"` for a wrong person, a tampered ciphertext or a key version other than `1`; `"secret could not be encrypted"` if Web Crypto fails. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (`bun:test`, file `convex/lib/byokCrypto.test.ts`; `PLAIN = "sk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaawxyz"`, a synthetic value)
  1. Given `encryptByokKey(key, "users:1", PLAIN)` / When `decryptByokKey(key, "users:1", keyCipher, keyVersion)` runs / Then it returns `PLAIN` and `keyVersion` is `1`.
  2. Given the result of case 1 / Then `keyCipher` starts with `"v1."` and does not contain `PLAIN`.
  3. Given two `encryptByokKey(key, "users:1", PLAIN)` calls / Then the two `keyCipher` values differ and both decrypt to `PLAIN`.
  4. Given a ciphertext made for `"users:1"` / When `decryptByokKey(key, "users:2", keyCipher, 1)` runs / Then it rejects with `"secret could not be decrypted"`.
  5. Given a ciphertext whose last character is replaced (`A` becomes `B`, any other character becomes `A`) / When decrypted for `"users:1"` / Then it rejects with `"secret could not be decrypted"`. (`PLAIN` is 23 characters, so the sealed part is 23 + 16 = 39 bytes = 52 base64url characters with no padding bits: the last character always changes the tag.)
  6. Given a valid ciphertext / When `decryptByokKey(key, "users:1", keyCipher, 2)` runs / Then it rejects with `"secret could not be decrypted"`.
  7. Given `byokKeyHint("sk-aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaawxyz")` / Then `"sk-…wxyz"`; and `byokAad("users:1")` equals `"tempo-connections|users:1|byokKeys.keyCipher"`.
- **NUMBERS:** AES-256-GCM with a 96-bit IV, fresh per encryption (NIST SP 800-38D §5.2.1.1 and §8.2, https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/38/d/final; inherited from `encryptSecret`, `IV_BYTES = 12`) · 7 of 7 cases pass (exact) · latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline; not a gate).
