- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const PLUGIN_META_TYPE = "plugin-meta" as const;
  export const PLUGIN_META_OPENER = "```json tempo\n";
  export const PLUGIN_META_CLOSER = "\n```\n";
  /** UTF-8 bytes; equal to BLOCK_CODEC_LIMITS.maxBodyChars because a plugin body is a page body. */
  export const PLUGIN_FILE_MAX_BYTES = 1_048_576;
  export type PluginParseError = "not_a_plugin" | "plugin_too_large";
  export type ParsedPlugin =
    | { ok: true; manifest: Record<string, unknown>; body: string }
    | { ok: false; error: PluginParseError };

  export function packPlugin(manifest: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>, body: string): string;
  export function parsePlugin(text: string): ParsedPlugin;
  ```
  - `packPlugin` returns exactly `PLUGIN_META_OPENER + JSON.stringify({ type: PLUGIN_META_TYPE, v: 1, data: manifest }) + PLUGIN_META_CLOSER + body` (the envelope JSON on one line, then the body verbatim). It does not catch a `JSON.stringify` error.
  - `parsePlugin`, in order: (1) `new TextEncoder().encode(text).length > PLUGIN_FILE_MAX_BYTES` → `{ ok: false, error: "plugin_too_large" }`; (2) `!text.startsWith(PLUGIN_META_OPENER)` → `{ ok: false, error: "not_a_plugin" }` (so leading whitespace, a BOM or `\r\n` line endings are not a plugin); (3) `const end = text.indexOf(PLUGIN_META_CLOSER, PLUGIN_META_OPENER.length)`; `end === -1` → `not_a_plugin`; (4) `JSON.parse(text.slice(PLUGIN_META_OPENER.length, end))` inside `try`; a throw → `not_a_plugin`; (5) the parsed value must be a non-null, non-array object with `type === "plugin-meta"`, `v === 1` and `data` a non-null, non-array object, else `not_a_plugin`; (6) return `{ ok: true, manifest: data, body: text.slice(end + PLUGIN_META_CLOSER.length) }`.
  - Export block added to `packages/utils/src/index.ts` (exact text):
    ```ts
    export {
      type ParsedPlugin,
      PLUGIN_FILE_MAX_BYTES,
      PLUGIN_META_CLOSER,
      PLUGIN_META_OPENER,
      PLUGIN_META_TYPE,
      type PluginParseError,
      packPlugin,
      parsePlugin,
    } from "./plugin-pack";
    ```
  - Errors are returned codes, never thrown: `"plugin_too_large"` (case 8), `"not_a_plugin"` (cases 4–7). No user-facing copy. No I/O.
- **TESTS:** (`const M = { id: "focus-timer", name: "Focus timer" }; const B = "# Focus timer\n\nA calm card.\n";` and `const FENCE = "```json tempo\n";`)
  1. Given `M` and `B` / When `parsePlugin(packPlugin(M, B))` runs / Then it equals `{ ok: true, manifest: M, body: B }`.
  2. Given `packPlugin({ id: "a" }, "x")` / Then it equals `FENCE + '{"type":"plugin-meta","v":1,"data":{"id":"a"}}' + "\n```\n" + "x"`.
  3. Given `const t = packPlugin(M, B)` and `const p = parsePlugin(t)` / When `packPlugin(p.manifest, p.body)` runs / Then it is `===` to `t` (byte-identical re-pack).
  4. Given `FENCE + '{"type":"task","v":1,"data":{}}' + "\n```\n" + "body"` / Then `parsePlugin` returns `{ ok: false, error: "not_a_plugin" }`.
  5. Given `"# Just markdown\n"` and, separately, `""` / Then each returns `{ ok: false, error: "not_a_plugin" }`.
  6. Given `FENCE + '{"type":"plugin-meta","v":1,"data":{}}'` (no closer) and, separately, `FENCE + "{not json}" + "\n```\n"` / Then each returns `{ ok: false, error: "not_a_plugin" }`.
  7. Given a well-fenced envelope with `v: 2`, and separately one with `data: []` / Then each returns `{ ok: false, error: "not_a_plugin" }`.
  8. Given `const head = packPlugin(M, "")` and `const atCap = packPlugin(M, "a".repeat(1_048_576 - head.length))` (all ASCII, so exactly 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes) / Then `parsePlugin(atCap).ok` is `true`; Given `FENCE + "a".repeat(1_048_577)` / Then `{ ok: false, error: "plugin_too_large" }`; Given `"ש".repeat(524_289)` (524,289 characters, 1,048,578 UTF-8 bytes) / Then `{ ok: false, error: "plugin_too_large" }`.
  9. Given a body that itself starts a second `json tempo` fence after a heading (`"# T\n" + FENCE + "{}\n```\n"`) / Then `parsePlugin(packPlugin(M, body)).body === body`; Given body `""` / Then the parsed `body` is `""`.
- **NUMBERS:** 9 of 9 cases pass (exact). File cap 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes (`PLUGIN_FILE_MAX_BYTES`, source `BLOCK_CODEC_LIMITS.maxBodyChars` in `packages/utils/src/blocks.ts`; case 8 checks the cap at 1,048,576 bytes (accepted) and 1,048,577+ bytes (refused), with Hebrew text for UTF-8 bytes, CONVENTIONS §7 H). Round trip byte-exact (cases 1, 3). Latency: n/a (pure, O(n)).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.

  export const PLUGINS_PER_USER_MAX = 50;

  /** The caller's row for one plugin id, live or uninstalled; null when there is none. */
  async function pluginRow(ctx: QueryCtx | MutationCtx, userId: Id<"users">, pluginId: string): Promise<Doc<"plugins"> | null> {
    return ctx.db
      .query("plugins")
      .withIndex("by_userId_pluginId", (q) => q.eq("userId", userId).eq("pluginId", pluginId))
      .unique();
  }

  export const install = mutation({
    args: { manifestText: v.string() },
    returns: v.object({ pluginId: v.string(), created: v.boolean() }),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { manifestText: string }): Promise<{ pluginId: string; created: boolean }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Behaviour, in order:
  1. `const user = await requireUser(ctx);`
  2. `const parsed = parsePlugin(args.manifestText);` — `parsed.ok === false` with `error === "plugin_too_large"` → `throw new Error("Plugin file is too large")`; with `error === "not_a_plugin"` → `throw new Error("Not a plugin file")`.
  3. `const checked = validatePluginManifest(parsed.manifest);` — `checked.ok === false` → `throw new Error("Invalid plugin manifest")`.
  4. `const manifest = checked.manifest; const now = Date.now(); const existing = await pluginRow(ctx, user._id, manifest.id);`
  5. `existing` live (`deletedAt === undefined`) → `ctx.db.patch(existing._id, { manifest, version: manifest.version, updatedAt: now })` (keeps `enabled`, `source`, `listingId`, `createdAt` and any stored grants) and return `{ pluginId: manifest.id, created: false }`.
  6. Otherwise read `ctx.db.query("plugins").withIndex("by_userId_deletedAt", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).eq("deletedAt", undefined)).take(PLUGINS_PER_USER_MAX)`; when its length is `PLUGINS_PER_USER_MAX` → `throw new Error("Plugin limit reached")`.
  7. `const doc = { userId: user._id, pluginId: manifest.id, manifest, version: manifest.version, source: "file" as const, enabled: true, createdAt: now, updatedAt: now };` — an uninstalled `existing` row → `ctx.db.replace(existing._id, doc)` (a fresh install: old grants, `listingId` and `deletedAt` are dropped); no row → `ctx.db.insert("plugins", doc)`. Return `{ pluginId: manifest.id, created: true }`.
  - Auth: any signed-in, active person; acts only on their own rows (the index is keyed by `user._id`).
  - Errors (plain `Error`, exact messages, one TESTS case each): `"Not authenticated"` — no identity (case 1); `"Plugin file is too large"` — file over `PLUGIN_FILE_MAX_BYTES` UTF-8 bytes (case 2); `"Not a plugin file"` — no leading `plugin-meta` fence (case 3); `"Invalid plugin manifest"` — `validatePluginManifest` fails (case 4); `"Plugin limit reached"` — a new install when 50 live rows exist (case 9). (`requireUser`'s `"User not found"` / `"This account is not active"` are covered by `convex/lib/requireUser.test.ts`.)
  - Limits: one indexed `.unique()` read, at most one bounded `.take(50)` read, one write. No model call, no network, no user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (`convex/plugins.test.ts` shared fixtures, created here: `import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test"; import { packPlugin } from "@tempo/utils"; import * as plugins from "./plugins"; import { makeFakeCtx, makeSignedOutCtx, run } from "./lib/testFakeCtx";` · `const A = "users:a"; const B = "users:b";` · `const VALID = { id: "focus-timer", name: "Focus timer", version: "1.0.0", summary: "A calm timer card for your Today.", author: { name: "Dana Levi" }, permissions: ["read_pages"], components: ["TaskBlock"], actions: ["setTaskDone"], minTempoVersion: "0.1.0" };` · `const file = (over: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => packPlugin({ ...VALID, ...over }, "# Body\n");` · `async function addPlugin(ctx: any, over: Record<string, unknown> = {}) { return ctx.db.insert("plugins", { userId: A, pluginId: "focus-timer", manifest: VALID, version: "1.0.0", source: "file", enabled: true, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1, ...over }); }` · `const rows = (ctx: any) => ctx.db.query("plugins").collect();` · every context is `makeFakeCtx(A, [B])` unless a case says signed out)
  1. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / When `run(plugins.install, ctx, { manifestText: file() })` / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  2. Given `manifestText: "x".repeat(1_048_577)` / When A installs / Then it rejects with `"Plugin file is too large"` and `rows(ctx)` is empty.
  3. Given `manifestText: "# not a plugin\n"` / Then it rejects with `"Not a plugin file"` and `rows(ctx)` is empty.
  4. Given `file({ components: ["Calendar"] })` / Then it rejects with `"Invalid plugin manifest"` and `rows(ctx)` is empty.
  5. Given no rows / When A installs `file()` / Then it returns `{ pluginId: "focus-timer", created: true }` and the one row has `userId: A`, `pluginId: "focus-timer"`, `version: "1.0.0"`, `source: "file"`, `enabled: true`, `deletedAt: undefined`, `createdAt === updatedAt`, and `manifest` equal to `VALID`.
  6. Given `addPlugin(ctx, { enabled: false })` / When A installs `file({ version: "1.1.0" })` / Then it returns `{ pluginId: "focus-timer", created: false }`, `rows(ctx)` has length 1, and that row has `version: "1.1.0"`, `manifest.version === "1.1.0"`, `enabled: false`, `createdAt: 1`.
  7. Given `addPlugin(ctx, { deletedAt: 5, enabled: false, source: "marketplace", listingId: "marketplaceListings:1" })` / When A installs `file()` / Then it returns `created: true`, `rows(ctx)` has length 1, and the row has `deletedAt: undefined`, `enabled: true`, `source: "file"`, `listingId: undefined`.
  8. Given `addPlugin(ctx, { userId: B })` / When A installs `file()` / Then it returns `created: true`, `rows(ctx)` has length 2, and B's row still has `userId: B`, `updatedAt: 1`.
  9. Given 50 rows from `addPlugin(ctx, { pluginId: "p" + i })` for `i` 0–49 / When A installs `file()` / Then it rejects with `"Plugin limit reached"` and `rows(ctx)` still has length 50.
- **NUMBERS:** 9 of 9 cases pass (exact). `PLUGINS_PER_USER_MAX` = 50 live plugins per person (code constant; no external source; case 9 seeds the cap). File cap 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes and manifest cap 8,192 UTF-8 bytes come from TFV2-0399 / TFV2-0397 (cases 2, 4). Backend p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline measured in this repo; not a gate) — CONVENTIONS §20.

  ```ts
  export const pluginViewValidator = v.object({
    pluginId: v.string(),
    name: v.string(),
    summary: v.string(),
    version: v.string(),
    source: v.union(v.literal("marketplace"), v.literal("file")),
    enabled: v.boolean(),
    permissions: v.array(v.string()),
    components: v.array(v.string()),
    actions: v.array(v.string()),
    updatedAt: v.number(),
  });
  export type PluginView = {
    pluginId: string; name: string; summary: string; version: string; source: "marketplace" | "file";
    enabled: boolean; permissions: string[]; components: string[]; actions: string[]; updatedAt: number;
  };

  function toPluginView(row: Doc<"plugins">): PluginView {
    const m = row.manifest as PluginManifest;
    return { pluginId: row.pluginId, name: m.name, summary: m.summary, version: row.version, source: row.source, enabled: row.enabled,
      permissions: [...m.permissions], components: [...m.components], actions: [...m.actions], updatedAt: row.updatedAt };
  }

  export const list = query({
    args: {},
    returns: v.array(pluginViewValidator),
    handler: async (ctx: QueryCtx): Promise<PluginView[]> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Behaviour: `const user = await requireUser(ctx);` then `ctx.db.query("plugins").withIndex("by_userId_deletedAt", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).eq("deletedAt", undefined)).take(PLUGINS_PER_USER_MAX)`, map with `toPluginView`, sort: `enabled` rows first, then `name` ascending by plain code-unit comparison (`a.name < b.name ? -1 : a.name > b.name ? 1 : 0`), then `pluginId` the same way. The manifest was validated at install, so the cast is safe.

  export const setEnabled = mutation({

A per-user `plainMode` flag ignores all `origin: user` modules"; "Fallback … built-in layout"); REWRITE-PLAN-v2 §6 chunk 6; CONVENTIONS §6 (web lib test), §9. Code truth: `apps/web/components/blocks/registry.tsx` does NOT exist, and no json-render React registry exists anywhere (`grep -rn "defineRegistry" apps packages` finds nothing; the catalog's own comment says the registry "is a separate ticket (TEMPO-B06-03)"); today `apps/web/components/editor/ReadView.tsx` draws blocks by hand. So this ticket builds only the pure, renderer-independent piece: which installed, enabled plugins attach to which catalog component and action, with the built-in catalog never touched. Whatever renderer later draws blocks reads this overlay; an empty overlay means the built-in rendering. Plain mode is an argument, so this does not wait on CFG-011.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  import {
    BLOCK_ACTION_NAMES,
    BLOCK_COMPONENT_TYPES,
    type BlockActionName,
    type BlockComponentType,
  } from "@tempo/ui/blocks/catalog";
  import { PLUGIN_ACTION_NAMES, PLUGIN_COMPONENT_NAMES } from "@tempo/utils";

  /** What a screen passes in: one entry per installed plugin (the shape of a PluginView from plugins.list). */
  export type PluginOverlayInput = {
    pluginId: string;
    enabled: boolean;
    components: readonly string[];
    actions: readonly string[];
  };
  /** Plugin ids per catalog name, in input order, without repeats. A name with no plugin has no key. */
  export type PluginOverlay = {
    readonly components: Readonly<Partial<Record<BlockComponentType, readonly string[]>>>;
    readonly actions: Readonly<Partial<Record<BlockActionName, readonly string[]>>>;
  };
  export const EMPTY_PLUGIN_OVERLAY: PluginOverlay;
  export function buildPluginOverlay(plugins: readonly PluginOverlayInput[], options: { plainMode: boolean }): PluginOverlay;
  export function pluginsExtending(overlay: PluginOverlay, componentName: string): readonly string[];
  ```
  - `EMPTY_PLUGIN_OVERLAY = Object.freeze({ components: Object.freeze({}), actions: Object.freeze({}) })`.
  - `buildPluginOverlay`: `options.plainMode` → return `EMPTY_PLUGIN_OVERLAY`. Otherwise walk `plugins` in order, skip `enabled === false`; a component name is kept only when it is in both `BLOCK_COMPONENT_TYPES` and `PLUGIN_COMPONENT_NAMES`, an action name only when it is in both `BLOCK_ACTION_NAMES` and `PLUGIN_ACTION_NAMES`; append the `pluginId` to that name's list unless already present. When no name was kept, return `EMPTY_PLUGIN_OVERLAY`; else return a new object whose every list, both maps and the object itself are `Object.freeze`d. The input array and its objects are never mutated.
  - `pluginsExtending(overlay, name)` returns `overlay.components[name]` when `name` is one of `BLOCK_COMPONENT_TYPES` and that key exists, else a frozen empty array `[]`.
  - Errors: none (unknown names are ignored, never thrown). No user-facing copy (the fallback banner belongs to the future renderer).
- **TESTS:** (`const P = (pluginId: string, over: Partial<PluginOverlayInput> = {}): PluginOverlayInput => ({ pluginId, enabled: true, components: ["TaskBlock"], actions: ["setTaskDone"], ...over });`)
  1. Given `[P("focus-timer")]` and `{ plainMode: true }` / When `buildPluginOverlay` runs / Then the result is `EMPTY_PLUGIN_OVERLAY` (`toBe`).
  2. Given `[P("focus-timer")]` and `{ plainMode: false }` / Then `pluginsExtending(overlay, "TaskBlock")` equals `["focus-timer"]` and `overlay.actions.setTaskDone` equals `["focus-timer"]`.
  3. Given `[P("focus-timer", { enabled: false })]` / Then the result is `EMPTY_PLUGIN_OVERLAY` and `pluginsExtending(result, "TaskBlock")` equals `[]`.
  4. Given `[P("x", { components: ["Calendar", "PageMeta"], actions: ["navigate"] })]` (`PageMeta` is a catalog name but not a plugin name) / Then the result is `EMPTY_PLUGIN_OVERLAY` and `pluginsExtending(result, "Calendar")` equals `[]`.
  5. Given `[P("a"), P("b", { components: ["TaskBlock", "TemplateBlock"] }), P("a")]` / Then `pluginsExtending(overlay, "TaskBlock")` equals `["a", "b"]` and `pluginsExtending(overlay, "TemplateBlock")` equals `["b"]`.
  6. Given the two allowlists / Then every entry of `PLUGIN_COMPONENT_NAMES` is in `BLOCK_COMPONENT_TYPES` and every entry of `PLUGIN_ACTION_NAMES` is in `BLOCK_ACTION_NAMES` (drift guard between `@tempo/utils` and the catalog).
  7. Given an overlay built from `[P("a")]` / Then `Object.isFrozen(overlay)`, `Object.isFrozen(overlay.components)` and `Object.isFrozen(overlay.components.TaskBlock)` are all `true`, and `tempoBlockCatalog.componentNames` (imported from `@tempo/ui/blocks/catalog`) still equals `[...BLOCK_COMPONENT_TYPES]`.
  8. Given `const input = [P("a")]` and a `JSON.stringify(input)` snapshot / When `buildPluginOverlay(input, { plainMode: false })` runs / Then `JSON.stringify(input)` is unchanged; and `buildPluginOverlay([], { plainMode: false })` is `EMPTY_PLUGIN_OVERLAY`.
- **NUMBERS:** 8 of 8 cases pass (exact). Allowlist ⊆ catalog (exact invariant, case 6). Lookup is O(1) per name; build is O(plugins × names) over at most `PLUGINS_PER_USER_MAX` (50, TFV2-0401a) inputs. Latency: n/a (pure, in memory).
- **GATES:** n/a — OPEN (not buildable until Amit answers).

Old TFV2-0405 bundled `grantPermissions` and `assertPermission` in `convex/lib/plugin-permissions.ts`; a public mutation cannot live in `convex/lib`, so the mutation goes in `convex/plugins.ts` (this ticket) and the check becomes the lib helper `assertPluginPermission` (TFV2-0405b). The grant is stored in the new field `plugins.grantedPermissions` (CFG-046), not inside the stored manifest, so the manifest stays exactly what was validated. The call replaces the whole granted set, so granting fewer permissions revokes the rest and `[]` revokes all.

  ```ts
  import { PLUGIN_CONFIRM_EACH_USE, type PluginManifest, type PluginPermission } from "@tempo/utils";
  import type { Id } from "../_generated/dataModel";
  import type { MutationCtx, QueryCtx } from "../_generated/server";

  export type PluginPermissionCheck = { needsConfirmation: boolean };

  export async function assertPluginPermission(
    ctx: QueryCtx | MutationCtx,
    userId: Id<"users">,
    pluginId: string,
    permission: PluginPermission,
  ): Promise<PluginPermissionCheck>;
  ```
  Behaviour, in order: `const row = await ctx.db.query("plugins").withIndex("by_userId_pluginId", (q) => q.eq("userId", userId).eq("pluginId", pluginId)).unique();` — `row === null || row.deletedAt !== undefined` → `throw new Error("Plugin not found")`; `row.enabled === false` → `throw new Error("Plugin is turned off")`; `const declared = (row.manifest as PluginManifest).permissions; const granted = row.grantedPermissions ?? [];` — unless `declared.includes(permission) && granted.includes(permission)` → `throw new Error("Permission not granted")`; return `{ needsConfirmation: PLUGIN_CONFIRM_EACH_USE.includes(permission) }`.
  - Errors (plain `Error`, one TESTS case each): `"Plugin not found"` — no row (case 1), uninstalled row (case 2), only another person's row with that id (case 8); `"Plugin is turned off"` — `enabled: false` (case 3); `"Permission not granted"` — granted but no longer declared (case 4), declared but not granted (case 5).
  - Limits: one indexed `.unique()` read. No writes, no user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (`const A = "users:a"; const B = "users:b"; const VALID = { id: "focus-timer", name: "Focus timer", version: "1.0.0", summary: "A calm timer card for your Today.", author: { name: "Dana Levi" }, permissions: ["read_pages", "web_request"], components: ["TaskBlock"], actions: ["setTaskDone"], minTempoVersion: "0.1.0" };` · `async function addPlugin(ctx: any, over: Record<string, unknown> = {}) { return ctx.db.insert("plugins", { userId: A, pluginId: "focus-timer", manifest: VALID, version: "1.0.0", source: "file", enabled: true, grantedPermissions: ["read_pages", "web_request"], createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1, ...over }); }` · `const ctx = makeFakeCtx(A, [B]);` · `const check = (p: PluginPermission) => assertPluginPermission(ctx, A as Id<"users">, "focus-timer", p);`)
  1. Given no rows / When `check("read_pages")` / Then it rejects with `"Plugin not found"`.
  2. Given `addPlugin(ctx, { deletedAt: 5 })` / When `check("read_pages")` / Then it rejects with `"Plugin not found"`.
  3. Given `addPlugin(ctx, { enabled: false })` / When `check("read_pages")` / Then it rejects with `"Plugin is turned off"`.
  4. Given `addPlugin(ctx, { grantedPermissions: ["write_today"] })` (declared: `read_pages`, `web_request`) / When `check("write_today")` / Then it rejects with `"Permission not granted"`.
  5. Given `addPlugin(ctx, { grantedPermissions: undefined })` / When `check("read_pages")` / Then it rejects with `"Permission not granted"`.
  6. Given `addPlugin(ctx)` / When `check("read_pages")` / Then it resolves `{ needsConfirmation: false }`.
  7. Given `addPlugin(ctx)` / When `check("web_request")` / Then it resolves `{ needsConfirmation: true }`.
  8. Given `addPlugin(ctx, { userId: B })` only / When `check("read_pages")` for A / Then it rejects with `"Plugin not found"`.
- **NUMBERS:** 8 of 8 cases pass (exact). Effective permission = declared ∩ granted (exact invariant, cases 4–5). Every `PLUGIN_CONFIRM_EACH_USE` permission returns `needsConfirmation: true` (case 7). Latency: one indexed read; p95 UNKNOWN (no baseline; not a gate) — CONVENTIONS §20.

- **SPEC:** new file `convex/marketplace.ts`:
  ```ts
  import { parsePlugin, PLUGIN_ID_PATTERN, type PluginManifest, validatePluginManifest } from "@tempo/utils";
  import { type Infer, v } from "convex/values";
  import type { Doc } from "./_generated/dataModel";
  import { type MutationCtx, mutation, type QueryCtx } from "./_generated/server";
  import { requireUser } from "./lib/requireUser";

  export const MARKETPLACE_LIMITS = { listingsPerAuthorMax: 100, slugMaxChars: 64 } as const;

  export const listingCategoryValidator = v.union(
    v.literal("planning"), v.literal("coach"), v.literal("learning"),
    v.literal("habits"), v.literal("wellbeing"), v.literal("other"),
  );
  export type ListingCategory = Infer<typeof listingCategoryValidator>;

  /** The one listing that owns a slug, in any status, unpublished or not; null when the slug is free. */
  async function listingBySlug(ctx: QueryCtx | MutationCtx, slug: string): Promise<Doc<"marketplaceListings"> | null> {
    return ctx.db.query("marketplaceListings").withIndex("by_slug", (q) => q.eq("slug", slug)).unique();
  }

  export const publish = mutation({
    args: { manifestText: v.string(), category: listingCategoryValidator, slug: v.optional(v.string()) },
    returns: v.object({ slug: v.string(), created: v.boolean() }),
    handler: async (
      ctx: MutationCtx,
      args: { manifestText: string; category: ListingCategory; slug?: string },
    ): Promise<{ slug: string; created: boolean }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Behaviour, in order:
  1. `const user = await requireUser(ctx);`
  2. `parsePlugin(args.manifestText)`: `error === "plugin_too_large"` → `throw new Error("Plugin file is too large")`; `error === "not_a_plugin"` → `throw new Error("Not a plugin file")`.
  3. `validatePluginManifest(parsed.manifest)` fails → `throw new Error("Invalid plugin manifest")`. `const manifest = checked.manifest;`
  4. `const slug = args.slug ?? manifest.id;` — `slug.length > MARKETPLACE_LIMITS.slugMaxChars || !PLUGIN_ID_PATTERN.test(slug)` → `throw new Error("Invalid slug")`.
  5. `const existing = await listingBySlug(ctx, slug);` — `existing !== null && existing.authorId !== user._id` → `throw new Error("Slug is taken")` (also when that listing is unpublished).
  6. `const mine = await ctx.db.query("marketplaceListings").withIndex("by_authorId", (q) => q.eq("authorId", user._id)).take(MARKETPLACE_LIMITS.listingsPerAuthorMax);` — when some row in `mine` has `deletedAt === undefined`, `slug !== slug` and `(row.manifest as PluginManifest).id === manifest.id` → `throw new Error("Plugin is already listed under another slug")`.
  7. `existing === null && mine.length === MARKETPLACE_LIMITS.listingsPerAuthorMax` → `throw new Error("Listing limit reached")` (the cap counts every listing row the author has, unpublished ones included, because slugs stay owned).
  8. `const now = Date.now(); const fields = { manifest, currentVersion: manifest.version, status: "under_review" as const, category: args.category, updatedAt: now };`
  9. `existing` (the caller's) → `ctx.db.patch(existing._id, { ...fields, deletedAt: undefined })`, return `{ slug, created: false }`; else `ctx.db.insert("marketplaceListings", { authorId: user._id, slug, ...fields, installCount: 0, createdAt: now })`, return `{ slug, created: true }`.
  - Auth: any signed-in, active person, acting as author of their own listings only.
  - Errors (plain `Error`, exact messages, one TESTS case each): `"Not authenticated"` (case 1); `"Plugin file is too large"` (case 2); `"Not a plugin file"` (case 3); `"Invalid plugin manifest"` (case 4); `"Invalid slug"` (case 5); `"Slug is taken"` (case 7); `"Plugin is already listed under another slug"` (case 9); `"Listing limit reached"` (case 10).
  - Limits: one `.unique()` read, one bounded `.take(100)` read, one write. No model call, no network, no user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (`convex/marketplace.test.ts` shared fixtures, created here: `import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test"; import { packPlugin } from "@tempo/utils"; import * as marketplace from "./marketplace"; import { makeFakeCtx, makeSignedOutCtx, run } from "./lib/testFakeCtx";` · `const A = "users:a"; const B = "users:b";` · `const VALID = { id: "focus-timer", name: "Focus timer", version: "1.0.0", summary: "A calm timer card for your Today.", author: { name: "Dana Levi" }, permissions: ["read_pages"], components: ["TaskBlock"], actions: ["setTaskDone"], minTempoVersion: "0.1.0" };` · `const file = (over: Record<string, unknown> = {}) => packPlugin({ ...VALID, ...over }, "# Body\n");` · `async function addListing(ctx: any, over: Record<string, unknown> = {}) { return ctx.db.insert("marketplaceListings", { authorId: A, slug: "focus-timer", manifest: VALID, currentVersion: "1.0.0", status: "published", category: "planning", installCount: 0, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1, ...over }); }` · `const rows = (ctx: any) => ctx.db.query("marketplaceListings").collect();` · contexts `makeFakeCtx(A, [B])`)
  1. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / When `run(marketplace.publish, ctx, { manifestText: file(), category: "planning" })` / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  2. Given `manifestText: "x".repeat(1_048_577)` / Then it rejects with `"Plugin file is too large"` and `rows(ctx)` is empty.
  3. Given `manifestText: "# not a plugin\n"` / Then it rejects with `"Not a plugin file"` and `rows(ctx)` is empty.
  4. Given `file({ version: "1" })` / Then it rejects with `"Invalid plugin manifest"` and `rows(ctx)` is empty.
  5. Given `slug: "Bad Slug"`, and separately `slug: "a".repeat(65)` / Then each rejects with `"Invalid slug"` and `rows(ctx)` is empty.
  6. Given no rows / When A publishes `file()` with `category: "planning"` and no slug / Then it returns `{ slug: "focus-timer", created: true }` and the one row has `authorId: A`, `status: "under_review"`, `category: "planning"`, `currentVersion: "1.0.0"`, `installCount: 0`, `deletedAt: undefined`, `createdAt === updatedAt`, `manifest` equal to `VALID`.

  ```ts
  export const MARKETPLACE_LIST = { defaultLimit: 24, maxLimit: 100, scanMax: 500, queryMaxChars: 100 } as const;

  export const listingSummaryValidator = v.object({
    slug: v.string(),
    name: v.string(),
    summary: v.string(),
    authorName: v.string(),
    category: listingCategoryValidator,
    currentVersion: v.string(),
    installCount: v.number(),
    ratingAverage: v.union(v.number(), v.null()),
    ratingCount: v.number(),
    updatedAt: v.number(),
  });
  export type ListingSummary = Infer<typeof listingSummaryValidator>;

  export const list = query({
    args: {
      query: v.optional(v.string()),
      category: v.optional(listingCategoryValidator),
      sort: v.optional(v.union(v.literal("popular"), v.literal("recent"))),
      cursor: v.optional(v.string()),
      limit: v.optional(v.number()),
    },
    returns: v.object({ items: v.array(listingSummaryValidator), hasMore: v.boolean(), nextCursor: v.union(v.string(), v.null()) }),
    handler: async (
      ctx: QueryCtx,
      args: { query?: string; category?: ListingCategory; sort?: "popular" | "recent"; cursor?: string; limit?: number },
    ): Promise<{ items: ListingSummary[]; hasMore: boolean; nextCursor: string | null }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Behaviour, in order:
  1. `await requireUser(ctx);`
  2. `const limit = args.limit ?? MARKETPLACE_LIST.defaultLimit;` — `!Number.isInteger(limit) || limit < 1 || limit > MARKETPLACE_LIST.maxLimit` → `throw new Error("Invalid limit")`.
  3. `const offset = args.cursor === undefined ? 0 : Number(args.cursor)` after checking `/^(0|[1-9]\d{0,5})$/.test(args.cursor)`; a failing cursor → `throw new Error("Invalid cursor")`.
  4. `const needle = (args.query ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();` — `needle.length > MARKETPLACE_LIST.queryMaxChars` → `throw new Error("Search is too long")`.
  5. Read `ctx.db.query("marketplaceListings").withIndex("by_status_category", (q) => args.category === undefined ? q.eq("status", "published") : q.eq("status", "published").eq("category", args.category)).take(MARKETPLACE_LIST.scanMax)`.
  6. Keep rows with `deletedAt === undefined`; when `needle !== ""`, keep rows whose `manifest.name.toLowerCase()` or `manifest.summary.toLowerCase()` includes `needle`.
  7. Sort with plain comparisons (no `localeCompare`): `"popular"` (the default) = `installCount` descending, then `updatedAt` descending, then `slug` ascending; `"recent"` = `updatedAt` descending, then `slug` ascending.
  8. `const page = sorted.slice(offset, offset + limit); const hasMore = offset + limit < sorted.length;` return `{ items: page.map(toSummary), hasMore, nextCursor: hasMore ? String(offset + limit) : null }`, where `toSummary(row)` with `const m = row.manifest as PluginManifest;` is `{ slug: row.slug, name: m.name, summary: m.summary, authorName: m.author.name, category: row.category, currentVersion: row.currentVersion, installCount: row.installCount, ratingAverage: row.ratingAverage ?? null, ratingCount: row.ratingCount ?? 0, updatedAt: row.updatedAt }`.
  - Errors (plain `Error`, one TESTS case each): `"Not authenticated"` (case 1); `"Invalid limit"` (case 8); `"Invalid cursor"` (case 9); `"Search is too long"` (case 10).
  - Limits: one bounded read of at most `MARKETPLACE_LIST.scanMax` (500) rows (case 11); a page holds at most 100 items. No writes, no user-facing copy.

  3. Given `L("x", { manifest: { ...VALID, id: "x", name: "Focus timer" } })`, `L("y", { manifest: { ...VALID, id: "y", name: "Calm", summary: "Helps you focus on one thing." } })`, `L("z", { manifest: { ...VALID, id: "z", name: "Habits", summary: "Daily habits." } })` / When A lists `{ query: "  FOCUS " }` / Then the sorted item slugs are `["x", "y"]`.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const installListing = mutation({
    args: { slug: v.string() },
    returns: v.object({ pluginId: v.string(), created: v.boolean() }),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { slug: string }): Promise<{ pluginId: string; created: boolean }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Behaviour, in order:
  1. `const user = await requireUser(ctx);`
  2. `const listing = await listingBySlug(ctx, args.slug);` — `null`, `deletedAt !== undefined` or `status !== "published"` → `throw new Error("Listing not found")`.
  3. `const checked = validatePluginManifest(listing.manifest);` — fails → `throw new Error("Invalid plugin manifest")` (a stored manifest that no longer validates is never installed). `const manifest = checked.manifest; const now = Date.now();`
  4. `existing` = `ctx.db.query("plugins").withIndex("by_userId_pluginId", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).eq("pluginId", manifest.id)).unique()`.
  5. `existing` live → `ctx.db.patch(existing._id, { manifest, version: manifest.version, source: "marketplace", listingId: listing._id, updatedAt: now })` (keeps `enabled`, grants and `createdAt`); when `existing.listingId !== listing._id` also `ctx.db.patch(listing._id, { installCount: listing.installCount + 1 })`; return `{ pluginId: manifest.id, created: false }`.
  6. Otherwise count live rows: `ctx.db.query("plugins").withIndex("by_userId_deletedAt", (q) => q.eq("userId", user._id).eq("deletedAt", undefined)).take(PLUGINS_PER_USER_MAX)`; length `=== PLUGINS_PER_USER_MAX` → `throw new Error("Plugin limit reached")`.
  7. `doc = { userId: user._id, pluginId: manifest.id, manifest, version: manifest.version, source: "marketplace" as const, listingId: listing._id, enabled: true, createdAt: now, updatedAt: now }`; an uninstalled `existing` → `ctx.db.replace(existing._id, doc)`; none → `ctx.db.insert("plugins", doc)`; then `ctx.db.patch(listing._id, { installCount: listing.installCount + 1 })`; return `{ pluginId: manifest.id, created: true }`.
  Errors (exact → trigger, one TESTS case each): `"Not authenticated"`; `"Listing not found"` (no row, unpublished, or not `published`); `"Invalid plugin manifest"`; `"Plugin limit reached"` (a new install when 50 live plugins exist). Limits: two `.unique()` reads, one `.take(50)`, at most two writes. No model call, no network, no user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (TFV2-0407a fixtures; `makeFakeCtx(A, [B])`)
  1. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / Then `run(marketplace.installListing, ctx, { slug: "focus-timer" })` rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  2. Given no listing, and separately `addListing(ctx, { status: "under_review" })`, and `addListing(ctx, { deletedAt: 9 })` / When B installs `focus-timer` / Then each rejects with `"Listing not found"` and no `plugins` row exists.
  3. Given `addListing(ctx, { manifest: { ...VALID, version: "1" } })` / Then B's install rejects with `"Invalid plugin manifest"`.
  4. Given `addListing(ctx)` / When B installs / Then it returns `{ pluginId: "focus-timer", created: true }`, B's one `plugins` row has `source: "marketplace"`, `listingId` = the listing id, `enabled: true`, `version: "1.0.0"`, and the listing's `installCount` is 1.
  5. Given that install / When B installs again after the listing's `manifest` and `currentVersion` move to `1.1.0` / Then it returns `created: false`, the row has `version: "1.1.0"`, and `installCount` is still 1.
  6. Given B has a live `source: "file"` row for `focus-timer` with `enabled: false` / When B installs the listing / Then `created` is false, the row has `source: "marketplace"`, the listing id, `enabled: false`, and `installCount` is 1.
  7. Given B's row for `focus-timer` with `deletedAt: 5` / When B installs / Then `created` is true, the row has `deletedAt: undefined`, `enabled: true`, and `installCount` is 1.
  8. Given B has 50 live plugins with other ids / Then B's install rejects with `"Plugin limit reached"` and `installCount` stays 0.

  // apps/web/components/marketplace/InstallConfirm.tsx ("use client")
  import type React from "react";
  import type { Lang } from "@/lib/i18n";
  export type PluginPermissionName = "read_pages" | "write_today" | "schedule_job" | "web_request";
  export type PluginPartName = "TaskBlock" | "TemplateBlock" | "setTaskDone";
  export const PLUGIN_PERMISSION_COPY: Record<Lang, Record<PluginPermissionName, string>>; // table below
  export const PLUGIN_PART_COPY: Record<Lang, Record<PluginPartName, string>>;             // table below
  export type InstallConfirmProps = {
    pluginName: string;
    authorName: string;
    permissions: PluginPermissionName[];   // what the plugin declares, in manifest order
    state: "idle" | "installing" | "error";
    online: boolean;
    onApprove: (granted: PluginPermissionName[]) => void; // ticked permissions, in the order of `permissions`
    onCancel: () => void;                                  // Cancel, Close, Esc, scrim
  };
  export function InstallConfirm(props: InstallConfirmProps): React.JSX.Element;
  ```
  **Markup:** fragment of `<div className="tp-sheet-scrim" aria-hidden="true" onClick={onCancel} />` and `<section className="tp-sheet tp-glass" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby={titleId} data-component="MobileSheet" data-view="InstallConfirm" data-state={state} onKeyDown={trap}>`: grabber; head `<h2 className="tp-sheet__title" id={titleId}>{copy.title with {name} in <bdi dir="auto">}</h2>` + `<Button label={copy.close} variant="ghost" icon="x" iconOnly onClick={onCancel} />`; body: `{!online && <StateOffline text={copy.offline} />}`, `<p className="tp-small tp-muted">{copy.by with {name} = authorName in <bdi dir="auto">}</p>`, `<h3 className="tp-h3">{copy.mayDo}</h3>`, then `permissions.length === 0` → `<p className="tp-body">{copy.none}</p>`, else `<p className="tp-small tp-muted" id={hintId}>{copy.hint}</p>` and one `<Checkbox id={\`install-perm-${p}\`} label={PLUGIN_PERMISSION_COPY[lang][p]} checked={ticked.has(p)} onChange=… disabled={state === "installing"} />` per permission; `<p className="tp-small">{copy.sandbox}</p>`; `<p className="tp-small tp-muted">{copy.note}</p>`; `{state === "error" && <p className="tp-error-text" role="alert">{copy.error}</p>}`; `{state === "installing" && <p className="tp-sr-only" role="status">{copy.installing}</p>}`. Foot: `<Button variant="primary" label={copy.install} disabled={state === "installing" || !online} aria-busy={state === "installing" || undefined} onClick={() => onApprove(permissions.filter((p) => ticked.has(p)))} />` then `<Button variant="ghost" label={copy.cancel} onClick={onCancel} />`. `ticked` is local state, empty on mount. Focus moves to Cancel on mount; Tab wraps inside the section; Esc → `onCancel`; focus returns to the opener on unmount.
  **COPY** (component strings):

  | key | EN | HE |
  |---|---|---|
  | title | Install {name}? | להתקין את {name}? |
  | close | Close | סגירה |
  | by | by {name} | מאת {name} |
  | mayDo | What it may do | מה התוסף יכול לעשות |
  | hint | Tick what you allow. You can change this later. | אפשר לסמן מה מותר. אפשר לשנות את זה אחר כך. |
  | none | It asks for no permissions. | התוסף לא מבקש הרשאות. |
  | sandbox | Plugins use only Tempo's own building blocks. They never see your keys or anyone else's data. | תוספים משתמשים רק באבני הבניין של Tempo. הם אף פעם לא רואים את המפתחות שלך או מידע של אחרים. |
  | note | Nothing runs until you install. You can turn it off or remove it any time. | שום דבר לא רץ לפני ההתקנה. אפשר לכבות או להסיר אותו מתי שרוצים. |
  | install | Install | התקנה |
  | cancel | Cancel | ביטול |
  | installing | Installing… | בהתקנה… |
  | error | That didn't install. Nothing changed. | זה לא הותקן. שום דבר לא השתנה. |
  | offline | You're offline. Installing needs a connection. | אין חיבור כרגע. כדי להתקין צריך חיבור. |

  **PLUGIN_PERMISSION_COPY:** `read_pages` EN "Read your pages" / HE "קריאת הדפים שלך" · `write_today` EN "Add items to Today" / HE "הוספת פריטים להיום" · `schedule_job` EN "Set up scheduled jobs" / HE "הגדרת פעולות מתוזמנות" · `web_request` EN "Reach websites (asks you each time)" / HE "פנייה לאתרים (עם אישור בכל פעם)".

  **RTL:** tempo.css logical sheet; names in `<bdi dir="auto">`; Close at the inline end. **Keyboard / screen reader:** dialog named by its heading; each permission is a native checkbox with its plain-words label; errors `role="alert"`; installing announced by `role="status"`. **Breakpoints:** bottom sheet at 390; centred panel from 768. **Motion:** tempo.css `tp-rise` 240 ms / `tp-fade` 180 ms; none under reduced motion.

  ```ts
  // apps/web/components/marketplace/PluginDetailView.tsx ("use client")
  import type React from "react";
  import { InstallConfirm, PLUGIN_PART_COPY, PLUGIN_PERMISSION_COPY, type PluginPartName, type PluginPermissionName } from "./InstallConfirm";
  export type PluginDetail = {
    slug: string; name: string; summary: string; description: string | null; authorName: string;
    category: "planning" | "coach" | "learning" | "habits" | "wellbeing" | "other";
    status: "draft" | "under_review" | "published" | "rejected";
    currentVersion: string; installCount: number; ratingAverage: number | null; ratingCount: number;
    permissions: PluginPermissionName[]; components: PluginPartName[]; actions: PluginPartName[]; isAuthor: boolean;
  };
  export type PluginDetailViewProps = {
    state: "ready" | "loading" | "error" | "not-found";
    detail: PluginDetail | null;                       // non-null only when state === "ready"
    installed: { version: string; enabled: boolean } | null;
    confirming: boolean;                               // the install sheet is open
    installState: "idle" | "installing" | "error";
    justInstalled: boolean;                            // show the "Installed." notice with Undo
    online: boolean;
    onInstallClick: () => void;
    onApprove: (granted: PluginPermissionName[]) => void;
    onCancelInstall: () => void;
    onUndoInstall: () => void;
    onRetry: () => void;
  };
  export function PluginDetailView(props: PluginDetailViewProps): React.JSX.Element;
  ```
  **Layout:** root `<div className="tp-page" data-component="PageLayout" data-view="PluginDetailView">`; first child always `<Link className="tp-btn tp-btn--ghost" href="/marketplace">` (`next/link`) with `<TpIcon name="chevron" size="sm" className="tp-icon--back" />` + `<span>{copy.back}</span>`. Then `{!online && <StateOffline />}` (from `@/components/states/StateOffline`). By state: `loading` → `<StateLoading label={copy.loading} rows={4} />`; `error` → `<StateError what={copy.error} onRetry={onRetry} />`; `not-found` → `<StateEmpty title={copy.notFound} body={copy.notFoundBody} />`; `ready` →
  1. `<PageHeader title={detail.name} subtitle={copy.by with {name}} actions={installed ? <Button variant="secondary" label={copy.installed} disabled /> : <Button variant="primary" label={copy.install} disabled={!online || detail.status !== "published"} onClick={onInstallClick} />} />`.
  2. `detail.isAuthor && detail.status !== "published"` → `<Notice tone="caution" title={copy.review} live="status" />`.
  3. `justInstalled` → `<Notice tone="done" title={copy.justInstalled} live="status" action={<Button variant="ghost" size="sm" label={copy.undo} onClick={onUndoInstall} />} />`.
  4. Facts line `<p className="tp-small tp-muted">`: `<Badge label={copy[category]} />`, `{copy.version with {v} in .tp-num}`, installs (`installOne` / `installMany`), rating (`noRatings` / `ratingOne` / `ratingMany`), the same rules and copy keys as TFV2-0409a.
  5. `<p className="tp-body" dir="auto">{summary}</p>`; then `description` split on `/\n{2,}/`, each part `<p className="tp-body" dir="auto">`.
  6. `<Section id="plugin-parts" title={copy.changes}>`: a `<ul>` of `PLUGIN_PART_COPY[lang][name]` for each of `components` then `actions`, or `<p>{copy.changesNone}</p>` when both are empty.
  7. `<Section id="plugin-perms" title={copy.mayDo}>`: a `<ul>` of `PLUGIN_PERMISSION_COPY[lang][p]`, or `<p>{copy.permsNone}</p>`.
  8. `<p className="tp-small tp-muted">{copy.share}</p>`.
  9. `confirming` → `<InstallConfirm pluginName={detail.name} authorName={detail.authorName} permissions={detail.permissions} state={installState} online={online} onApprove={onApprove} onCancel={onCancelInstall} />`.

  | permsNone | It asks for no permissions. | התוסף לא מבקש הרשאות. |
  | share | Authors keep 100% of what they earn. | 100% מההכנסות נשארים אצל היוצרים. |

  | noRatings / ratingOne / ratingMany | No ratings yet / {avg} of 5 (1 rating) / {avg} of 5 ({count} ratings) | עדיין אין דירוגים / {avg} מתוך 5 (דירוג אחד) / {avg} מתוך 5 ({count} דירוגים) |

- **DO NOT:** append a second review for the same person and listing; accept stars outside 1–5 or a non-integer; let an author rate their own listing; store HTML or trim inner whitespace beyond the SPEC; edit `convex/schema.ts`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0412a / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: convex/marketplace.ts, convex/marketplace.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 with evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const REVIEW_TEXT_MAX = 1_000;        // characters
  export const REVIEWS_AGGREGATE_MAX = 5_000;  // reviews read to recompute the average
  export const rate = mutation({
    args: { slug: v.string(), stars: v.number(), text: v.optional(v.string()) },
    returns: v.object({ ratingAverage: v.number(), ratingCount: v.number() }),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { slug: string; stars: number; text?: string }): Promise<{ ratingAverage: number; ratingCount: number }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Behaviour, in order: 1) `user = await requireUser(ctx)`. 2) `listing = listingBySlug(ctx, args.slug)`; missing, `deletedAt` set or not `published` → `throw new Error("Listing not found")`. 3) `listing.authorId === user._id` → `throw new Error("Authors cannot rate their own listing")`. 4) `!Number.isInteger(args.stars) || args.stars < 1 || args.stars > 5` → `throw new Error("Stars must be 1 to 5")`. 5) `text = args.text?.trim()`; `text !== undefined && text.length > REVIEW_TEXT_MAX` → `throw new Error("Review is too long")`; `""` becomes `undefined`. 6) the caller's `plugins` row for the listing's manifest id must be live with `listingId === listing._id`, else `throw new Error("Install the plugin before rating it")`. 7) `existing` = `marketplaceReviews` by `by_listingId_userId` (`.unique()`); live → `patch(existing._id, { stars, text, updatedAt: now })`; soft-deleted → `patch(existing._id, { stars, text, updatedAt: now, deletedAt: undefined })`; none → insert `{ userId, listingId, stars, ...(text ? { text } : {}), createdAt: now, updatedAt: now }`. 8) Recompute: `all = query("marketplaceReviews").withIndex("by_listingId_createdAt", (q) => q.eq("listingId", listing._id)).take(REVIEWS_AGGREGATE_MAX)` without `deletedAt`; `ratingCount = all.length`; `ratingAverage = Math.round((sum / count) * 10) / 10`; `patch(listing._id, { ratingAverage, ratingCount })`; return both.
  Errors (exact → trigger, one TESTS case each): `"Not authenticated"`; `"Listing not found"`; `"Authors cannot rate their own listing"`; `"Stars must be 1 to 5"`; `"Review is too long"`; `"Install the plugin before rating it"`.
- **TESTS:** (TFV2-0407a fixtures; B installs `focus-timer` through `installListing` first unless stated)
  1. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / Then `rate({ slug: "focus-timer", stars: 4 })` rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  2. Given an `under_review` listing / Then B's rate rejects with `"Listing not found"`.
  3. Given A (the author) / Then A's rate rejects with `"Authors cannot rate their own listing"`.
  4. Given `stars: 0`, `stars: 6` and `stars: 4.5` / Then each rejects with `"Stars must be 1 to 5"`.
  5. Given `text: "x".repeat(1_001)` / Then it rejects with `"Review is too long"`.
  6. Given B never installed the listing / Then it rejects with `"Install the plugin before rating it"`.
  7. Given B rates `4` with text `"  Calm and useful  "` / Then it returns `{ ratingAverage: 4, ratingCount: 1 }`, the review row has `text: "Calm and useful"`, and the listing has `ratingAverage: 4`, `ratingCount: 1`.
  8. Given B rated 4 / When B rates 2 / Then there is still one review row for B (stars 2) and it returns `{ ratingAverage: 2, ratingCount: 1 }`; and given a third person's live review of 5 seeded directly / When B rates 2 again / Then `{ ratingAverage: 3.5, ratingCount: 2 }`.
- **NUMBERS:** Stars integer 1–5 · review ≤ 1,000 characters (old TFV2-0412; CFG-023 note) · ≤ 5,000 reviews read per recompute (`REVIEWS_AGGREGATE_MAX`, product bound; CONVENTIONS §16). Review spam limits: UNKNOWN (Amit). p95 latency: UNKNOWN (not a gate). 8 of 8 cases pass.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const update = mutation({
    args: { pluginId: v.string(), acceptNewPermissions: v.boolean() },
    returns: v.object({ version: v.string(), granted: v.array(v.string()) }),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { pluginId: string; acceptNewPermissions: boolean }): Promise<{ version: string; granted: string[] }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Behaviour, in order: 1) `user = await requireUser(ctx)`. 2) `row = pluginRow(ctx, user._id, args.pluginId)`; missing or soft-deleted → `throw new Error("Plugin not found")`. 3) `row.source !== "marketplace"` or no `listingId`, or `listing = await ctx.db.get(row.listingId)` is missing, soft-deleted, not `published`, or `compareVersions(listing.currentVersion, row.version) !== 1` → `throw new Error("No update available")`. 4) `checked = validatePluginManifest(listing.manifest)`; fails → `throw new Error("Invalid plugin manifest")`. 5) `added` = new `permissions` not in the old manifest's `permissions`; `added.length > 0 && !args.acceptNewPermissions` → `throw new Error("Update needs new permissions")`. 6) `granted = (row.grantedPermissions ?? []).filter((p) => checked.manifest.permissions.includes(p))`; `patch(row._id, { manifest: checked.manifest, version: checked.manifest.version, grantedPermissions: granted, updatedAt: now })`; return `{ version, granted }`.
  Errors (exact → trigger, one TESTS case each): `"Not authenticated"`; `"Plugin not found"`; `"No update available"`; `"Invalid plugin manifest"`; `"Update needs new permissions"`.
- **TESTS:** (TFV2-0401a fixtures; A's marketplace plugin `focus-timer` at `1.0.0` with `grantedPermissions: ["read_pages"]`, linked to a published listing)
  1. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / Then `update({ pluginId: "focus-timer", acceptNewPermissions: false })` rejects with `"Not authenticated"`.
  2. Given no row for A, and separately only B's row / Then each rejects with `"Plugin not found"`.
  3. Given the listing still at `1.0.0`, and separately A's plugin with `source: "file"` / Then each rejects with `"No update available"`.
  4. Given the listing at `1.1.0` with a stored manifest whose `version` is `"1"` / Then it rejects with `"Invalid plugin manifest"`.
  5. Given the listing at `1.1.0` adding `"web_request"` and `acceptNewPermissions: false` / Then it rejects with `"Update needs new permissions"` and the row is unchanged.
  6. Given the same with `acceptNewPermissions: true` / Then it returns `{ version: "1.1.0", granted: ["read_pages"] }` and the row's `version` is `"1.1.0"`, `enabled` unchanged, `grantedPermissions` `["read_pages"]`.
  7. Given the listing at `1.1.0` whose manifest drops `"read_pages"` / Then it returns `granted: []` and the row's `grantedPermissions` is `[]`.
- **NUMBERS:** No new permission is granted by an update (exact; case 6). Only newer versions apply (exact; case 3). p95 latency: UNKNOWN (not a gate). 7 of 7 cases pass.

  ```rust
  // apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/nav.rs
  use tauri::Url;
  /// The one web origin the desktop shows (CFG-048 OPEN: live origin proposed).
  pub const WEB_ORIGIN: &str = "https://www.tempoflow.dev";
  pub const WEB_HOST: &str = "www.tempoflow.dev";
  pub const START_PATH: &str = "/today";
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub enum NavDecision { Allow, OpenExternal, Block }
  /// Allow: https on WEB_HOST with no explicit port; tauri://localhost (macOS/Linux bundled pages);
  /// http://tauri.localhost (Windows bundled pages); about:blank.
  /// OpenExternal: any other http, https or mailto URL. Block: everything else.
  pub fn decide(url: &Url) -> NavDecision {
      match (url.scheme(), url.host_str()) {
          ("https", Some(WEB_HOST)) if url.port().is_none() => NavDecision::Allow,
          ("tauri", Some("localhost")) => NavDecision::Allow,
          ("http", Some("tauri.localhost")) => NavDecision::Allow,
          ("about", _) if url.path() == "blank" => NavDecision::Allow,
          ("https", _) | ("http", _) | ("mailto", _) => NavDecision::OpenExternal,
          _ => NavDecision::Block,
      }
  }
  /// Some(WEB_ORIGIN + path) when path starts with "/" but not "//" and the result keeps WEB_HOST; else None.
  pub fn web_url(path: &str) -> Option<Url> {
      if !path.starts_with('/') || path.starts_with("//") { return None; }
      let url = Url::parse(&format!("{WEB_ORIGIN}{path}")).ok()?;
      (url.host_str() == Some(WEB_HOST)).then_some(url)
  }
  ```
  ```rust
  // apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/window.rs
  use crate::nav::{self, NavDecision};
  use tauri::{App, Url, WebviewUrl, WebviewWindow, WebviewWindowBuilder};
  use tauri_plugin_opener::OpenerExt;
  pub const MAIN_LABEL: &str = "main";
  pub const MAIN_TITLE: &str = "Tempo Flow";
  pub const MAIN_SIZE: (f64, f64) = (1200.0, 800.0);
  pub const MAIN_MIN_SIZE: (f64, f64) = (800.0, 600.0);
  /// initial = Some(url) whose decide() is Allow → that URL; otherwise the bundled boot page "index.html".
  pub fn create_main(app: &App, initial: Option<Url>) -> tauri::Result<WebviewWindow> {
      let url = match initial {
          Some(u) if nav::decide(&u) == NavDecision::Allow => WebviewUrl::External(u),
          _ => WebviewUrl::App("index.html".into()),
      };
      let handle = app.handle().clone();
      WebviewWindowBuilder::new(app, MAIN_LABEL, url)
          .title(MAIN_TITLE)
          .inner_size(MAIN_SIZE.0, MAIN_SIZE.1)
          .min_inner_size(MAIN_MIN_SIZE.0, MAIN_MIN_SIZE.1)
          .on_navigation(move |u| match nav::decide(u) {
              NavDecision::Allow => true,
              NavDecision::OpenExternal => { let _ = handle.opener().open_url(u.as_str(), None::<&str>); false }
              NavDecision::Block => false,
          })
          .build()
  }
  ```
  No user-facing copy (the window title "Tempo Flow" is the product name, Latin in both languages per CONVENTIONS §12). No errors of its own: `create_main` returns Tauri's `tauri::Result`, and `setup` propagates it with `?`.

  1. Given `https://www.tempoflow.dev/today?code=x` / When `decide` / Then `NavDecision::Allow`.
  2. Given `tauri://localhost/index.html` and `http://tauri.localhost/index.html` / Then both `Allow`.
  3. Given `https://www.tempoflow.dev:8443/today` / Then `OpenExternal` (explicit port is not the origin).
  4. Given `https://example.com/a` and `http://www.tempoflow.dev/today` and `mailto:a@b.c` / Then each `OpenExternal`.
  5. Given `file:///etc/passwd`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `data:text/html,hi` / Then each `Block`.
  6. Given `about:blank` / Then `Allow`.
  7. Given `web_url("/today")` / Then `Some(url)` with `url.as_str() == "https://www.tempoflow.dev/today"`.
  8. Given `web_url("//evil.example")`, `web_url("today")`, `web_url("")` / Then each `None`.
  9. Given the window constants / Then `MAIN_LABEL == "main"`, `MAIN_TITLE == "Tempo Flow"`, `MAIN_SIZE == (1200.0, 800.0)`, `MAIN_MIN_SIZE == (800.0, 600.0)`.

  ```ts
  export type DesktopLang = "en" | "he";
  export type DesktopSettings = { lang: DesktopLang; launchAtLogin: boolean; autoUpdate: boolean; closeToTray: boolean; onboarded: boolean };
  export type DesktopSettingsPatch = Partial<DesktopSettings>;
  export type DesktopUpdateStatus =
    | { state: "idle" } | { state: "checking" } | { state: "upToDate" } | { state: "ready"; version: string } | { state: "failed" };
  export type DesktopCachedPageInput = { id: string; title: string; body: string; updatedAt: number };
  export type TauriInvoke = (cmd: string, args?: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<unknown>;
  export const DESKTOP_HANDOFF_PATH = "/desktop/handoff";
  export const DESKTOP_DEEP_LINK_SCHEME = "tempo-flow"; // CFG-048 OPEN: scheme name
  export const AUTH_CODE_PATTERN = /^[0-9A-Za-z]{32}$/; // Convex Auth magic-link code: 32 chars of 0-9A-Za-z (@convex-dev/auth 0.0.91 signIn.js generateRandomString(32, alphabet))
  /** win.__TAURI__.core.invoke when it is a function, else null. Default win = globalThis.window (undefined on the server). */
  export function getTauriInvoke(win?: unknown): TauriInvoke | null;
  export function isDesktopShell(win?: unknown): boolean; // getTauriInvoke(win) !== null
  /** Throws "Desktop settings are invalid" unless raw has exactly the 5 keys with the right types and lang is "en" | "he". */
  export function parseDesktopSettings(raw: unknown): DesktopSettings;
  /** Throws "Desktop update status is invalid" unless raw matches one DesktopUpdateStatus variant ("ready" needs a non-empty string version). */
  export function parseUpdateStatus(raw: unknown): DesktopUpdateStatus;
  export function getDesktopSettings(invoke?: TauriInvoke | null): Promise<DesktopSettings>;            // invoke("desktop_settings_get")
  export function setDesktopSettings(patch: DesktopSettingsPatch, invoke?: TauriInvoke | null): Promise<DesktopSettings>; // invoke("desktop_settings_set", { patch })
  export function cachePage(page: DesktopCachedPageInput, invoke?: TauriInvoke | null): Promise<void>; // invoke("desktop_page_cache_put", { page })
  export function clearPageCache(invoke?: TauriInvoke | null): Promise<void>;                          // invoke("desktop_page_cache_clear")
  export function getUpdateStatus(invoke?: TauriInvoke | null): Promise<DesktopUpdateStatus>;          // invoke("desktop_update_status")
  export function restartToUpdate(invoke?: TauriInvoke | null): Promise<void>;                         // invoke("desktop_update_restart")
  /** "tempo-flow://auth?code=<code>" when AUTH_CODE_PATTERN matches, else null. */
  export function handoffDeepLink(code: string | null): string | null;
  ```
  Each async function's `invoke` parameter defaults to `getTauriInvoke()`; when it is `null` the function rejects with `new Error("Not running in the desktop app")` before anything else. A rejection from `invoke` itself propagates unchanged (the Rust command's `Err(String)` arrives as that string). Errors (exact → trigger): `"Not running in the desktop app"` → no invoke; `"Desktop settings are invalid"` → bad settings shape; `"Desktop update status is invalid"` → bad status shape. No user-facing copy (callers map errors to their own copy).
- **TESTS:** (`bun:test`)
  1. Given `getTauriInvoke(undefined)`, `getTauriInvoke({})`, `getTauriInvoke({ __TAURI__: { core: { invoke: "x" } } })` / Then each `null`; given `{ __TAURI__: { core: { invoke: fn } } }` / Then it returns `fn`.
  2. Given those same objects / When `isDesktopShell` / Then `false, false, false, true`.
  3. Given a fake invoke resolving `{ lang: "he", launchAtLogin: false, autoUpdate: true, closeToTray: true, onboarded: true }` / When `getDesktopSettings(fake)` / Then it resolves that object and the fake recorded `["desktop_settings_get", undefined]`.
  4. Given a fake resolving `{ lang: "fr", launchAtLogin: false, autoUpdate: true, closeToTray: true, onboarded: true }` / Then `getDesktopSettings(fake)` rejects `"Desktop settings are invalid"`; and a raw missing `onboarded` rejects the same.
  5. Given `setDesktopSettings({ launchAtLogin: true }, fake)` / Then the fake recorded `["desktop_settings_set", { patch: { launchAtLogin: true } }]` and the parsed reply is returned.
  6. Given `cachePage({ id: "n1", title: "T", body: "B", updatedAt: 5 }, fake)` and `clearPageCache(fake)` / Then the records are `["desktop_page_cache_put", { page: { id: "n1", title: "T", body: "B", updatedAt: 5 } }]` and `["desktop_page_cache_clear", undefined]`.
  7. Given a fake resolving `{ state: "ready", version: "1.2.0" }` / Then `getUpdateStatus(fake)` resolves it; resolving `{ state: "ready" }` or `{ state: "weird" }` rejects `"Desktop update status is invalid"`.
  8. Given `restartToUpdate(fake)` / Then the record is `["desktop_update_restart", undefined]`.
  9. Given `getDesktopSettings(null)` / Then it rejects `"Not running in the desktop app"`.
  10. Given `handoffDeepLink("A1".repeat(16))` / Then `"tempo-flow://auth?code=A1A1A1A1A1A1A1A1A1A1A1A1A1A1A1A1"`; and `handoffDeepLink("abc")`, `handoffDeepLink("a".repeat(31) + "!")`, `handoffDeepLink(null)` are each `null`.

  use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  pub const STORE_FILE: &str = "settings.json";
  pub const STORE_KEY: &str = "desktop";
  pub const SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT: &str = "desktop-settings-changed";
  pub const READ_ERROR: &str = "Settings could not be read";
  pub const SAVE_ERROR: &str = "Settings could not be saved";
  pub const AUTOSTART_ERROR: &str = "Start at login could not be changed";
  #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
  pub enum Lang { En, He }
  #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase", default)]
  pub struct DesktopSettings { pub lang: Lang, pub launch_at_login: bool, pub auto_update: bool, pub close_to_tray: bool, pub onboarded: bool }
  impl Default for DesktopSettings { /* lang En, launch_at_login false, auto_update true, close_to_tray true, onboarded false */ }
  #[derive(Deserialize, Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
  #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
  pub struct DesktopSettingsPatch { pub lang: Option<Lang>, pub launch_at_login: Option<bool>, pub auto_update: Option<bool>, pub close_to_tray: Option<bool>, pub onboarded: Option<bool> }
  pub trait SettingsBackend {
      fn read(&self) -> Result<Option<serde_json::Value>, String>;
      fn write(&mut self, settings: &DesktopSettings) -> Result<(), String>;
      fn set_autostart(&mut self, enabled: bool) -> Result<(), String>;
  }
  /// None → default; a value that does not deserialize (wrong type, unknown lang) → default; missing fields → their defaults.
  pub fn parse_stored(value: Option<serde_json::Value>) -> DesktopSettings;
  pub fn merge(current: &DesktopSettings, patch: &DesktopSettingsPatch) -> DesktopSettings; // each Some field replaces, None keeps
  /// read() Err → Err(READ_ERROR); else Ok(parse_stored(value)).
  pub fn load(backend: &impl SettingsBackend) -> Result<DesktopSettings, String>;
  /// load → merge → if launch_at_login changed: set_autostart(next) (Err → Err(AUTOSTART_ERROR), nothing written) → write (Err → Err(SAVE_ERROR)) → Ok(next).
  pub fn apply_patch(backend: &mut impl SettingsBackend, patch: &DesktopSettingsPatch) -> Result<DesktopSettings, String>;
  /// Real backend: tauri_plugin_store::StoreExt (app.store(STORE_FILE), get/set STORE_KEY, save) and tauri_plugin_autostart::ManagerExt (app.autolaunch().enable()/disable()); every underlying error string is replaced by READ_ERROR / SAVE_ERROR / AUTOSTART_ERROR by load/apply_patch.
  pub struct AppBackend { pub app: tauri::AppHandle }
  impl SettingsBackend for AppBackend { /* as above */ }
  #[tauri::command]
  pub fn desktop_settings_get(app: tauri::AppHandle) -> Result<DesktopSettings, String>; // load(&AppBackend { app })
  #[tauri::command]
  pub fn desktop_settings_set(app: tauri::AppHandle, patch: DesktopSettingsPatch) -> Result<DesktopSettings, String>;
  // apply_patch(&mut AppBackend { app: app.clone() }, &patch); on Ok(next): tauri::Emitter::emit(&app, SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT, &next) (an emit error is ignored), return Ok(next)
  ```

  ```rust
  // apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/updater.rs
  use serde::Serialize;
  use std::sync::Mutex;
  pub const NOT_READY_ERROR: &str = "No update is ready";
  pub const INSTALL_ERROR: &str = "The update could not be installed";
  #[derive(Serialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
  #[serde(tag = "state", rename_all = "camelCase")]
  pub enum UpdateStatus { Idle, Checking, UpToDate, Ready { version: String }, Failed }
  pub struct UpdateSlot<P> { pub status: UpdateStatus, pub pending: Option<P> }
  impl<P> Default for UpdateSlot<P> { /* status Idle, pending None */ }
  /// The managed state: the ready package is (tauri_plugin_updater::Update, downloaded bytes).
  #[derive(Default)]
  pub struct UpdaterState(pub Mutex<UpdateSlot<(tauri_plugin_updater::Update, Vec<u8>)>>);
  pub fn should_check(settings: &crate::settings::DesktopSettings, debug_build: bool) -> bool; // settings.auto_update && !debug_build
  /// Ok(Some(v)) → Ready { version: v }; Ok(None) → UpToDate; Err(_) → Failed.
  pub fn status_from_check(result: Result<Option<String>, ()>) -> UpdateStatus;
  /// pending None → Err(NOT_READY_ERROR), slot unchanged; Some(p) → Ok(p), slot.status = Idle, slot.pending = None.
  pub fn take_ready<P>(slot: &mut UpdateSlot<P>) -> Result<P, String>;
  pub fn map_install_error<E>(result: Result<(), E>) -> Result<(), String>; // Err(_) → Err(INSTALL_ERROR)
  /// Spawns (tauri::async_runtime::spawn): settings::load(&AppBackend) (Err → return); unless should_check(&s, cfg!(debug_assertions)) return;
  /// status Checking; app.updater()?.check().await: Ok(Some(u)) → u.download(|_, _| {}, || {}).await → Ok(bytes) → pending = Some((u, bytes)), status Ready { version: u.version.clone() }, download Err → Failed;
  /// Ok(None) → UpToDate; Err → Failed. Never installs.
  pub fn spawn_check(app: tauri::AppHandle);
  #[tauri::command]
  pub fn desktop_update_status(state: tauri::State<'_, UpdaterState>) -> UpdateStatus; // clone of slot.status
  #[tauri::command]
  pub fn desktop_update_restart(app: tauri::AppHandle, state: tauri::State<'_, UpdaterState>) -> Result<(), String>;
  // take_ready → map_install_error(update.install(bytes)) → app.restart()
  /// Used by Tempo's Quit (menu, tray, close with keep-in-tray off): if a package is ready, install it (errors ignored), then app.exit(0).
  pub fn quit(app: &tauri::AppHandle);
  ```
  Wire format: `{"state":"idle"}`, `{"state":"checking"}`, `{"state":"upToDate"}`, `{"state":"ready","version":"1.2.0"}`, `{"state":"failed"}`. Errors (exact → trigger): `"No update is ready"` → restart requested with no ready package; `"The update could not be installed"` → `Update::install` failed. A quit through the operating system (Dock "Quit", task manager) skips `quit`; the ready package is then downloaded again on the next launch. No user-facing copy here (TFV2-0423b shows the status).
- **TESTS:** (`tests/updater.rs`)
  1. Given each `UpdateStatus` variant / When `serde_json::to_value` / Then exactly the five wire objects above.
  2. Given settings with `auto_update: true` / Then `should_check(&s, false) == true`, `should_check(&s, true) == false`; with `auto_update: false` / Then `should_check(&s, false) == false`.
  3. Given `status_from_check(Ok(Some("1.2.0".into())))`, `Ok(None)`, `Err(())` / Then `Ready { version: "1.2.0" }`, `UpToDate`, `Failed`.
  4. Given `UpdateSlot::<u8>::default()` / When `take_ready` / Then `Err("No update is ready")` and `status == Idle`, `pending == None`.
  5. Given `UpdateSlot { status: Ready { version: "1.2.0".into() }, pending: Some(7u8) }` / When `take_ready` / Then `Ok(7)`, status `Idle`, pending `None`.
  6. Given `map_install_error::<&str>(Err("disk"))` / Then `Err("The update could not be installed")`; and `map_install_error::<&str>(Ok(()))` / Then `Ok(())`.
- **NUMBERS:** downloads only over HTTPS and only with a valid signature (exact; enforced by `tauri-plugin-updater` and the CFG-048 `https://` endpoint). 0 installs without a Quit or Restart (exact; tests 4–5 and DO NOT). 6 of 6 tests pass.   // apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/menu.rs
  use crate::settings::Lang;
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub enum ItemKind { Custom, Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, SelectAll, Fullscreen, Minimize, CloseWindow, About, Separator }
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct ItemSpec { pub id: &'static str, pub label: &'static str, pub accelerator: Option<&'static str>, pub kind: ItemKind }
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub struct SectionSpec { pub id: &'static str, pub label: &'static str, pub items: Vec<ItemSpec> }
  pub fn menu_spec(lang: Lang) -> Vec<SectionSpec>;
  pub fn tray_spec(lang: Lang) -> Vec<ItemSpec>;
  /// Builds a tauri::menu::Menu from menu_spec(settings::load(&AppBackend).map(|s| s.lang).unwrap_or(Lang::En)):
  /// Custom → MenuItem::with_id(id, label, true, accelerator); Undo…CloseWindow → the matching PredefinedMenuItem with Some(label);
  /// About → PredefinedMenuItem::about(Some(label), Some(AboutMetadata { name: Some("Tempo Flow".into()), version: Some(app.package_info().version.to_string()), ..Default::default() }));
  /// Separator → PredefinedMenuItem::separator. Then app.set_menu(menu), app.on_menu_event(|app, e| handle_menu_id(app, e.id().as_ref())),
  /// and app.listen_any(SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT, …) which parses the payload as DesktopSettings and rebuilds the menu in its lang (bad payload → ignored).
  pub fn install(app: &tauri::App) -> tauri::Result<()>;
  /// "settings" → main window: navigate(nav::web_url("/desktop/settings")), show, set_focus; "reload" → main window eval("window.location.reload()");
  /// "quit" → updater::quit(app); "open" → main window show, unminimize, set_focus; any other id → nothing.
  pub fn handle_menu_id(app: &tauri::AppHandle, id: &str);
  ```
  ```rust
  // apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/tray.rs
  #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
  pub enum CloseAction { Hide, Quit }
  pub fn on_close_action(settings: &crate::settings::DesktopSettings) -> CloseAction; // close_to_tray → Hide, else Quit
  /// TrayIconBuilder::with_id("main").icon(app.default_window_icon().cloned()).tooltip("Tempo Flow").menu(from tray_spec).show_menu_on_left_click(false)
  /// .on_menu_event(|app, e| menu::handle_menu_id(app, e.id().as_ref())); left-click (MouseButtonState::Up) → handle_menu_id(app, "open").
  /// Main window on_window_event: CloseRequested { api } → match on_close_action(&settings::load(&AppBackend).unwrap_or_default())
  /// { Hide → api.prevent_close(); window.hide() ; Quit → api.prevent_close(); updater::quit(app) }.
  /// Listens to SETTINGS_CHANGED_EVENT and calls tray.set_menu with tray_spec(new lang).
  pub fn install(app: &tauri::App) -> tauri::Result<()>;
  ```

Code truth (`@convex-dev/auth` 0.0.91 in `bun.lock`): a magic-link code is 32 characters of `0-9A-Za-z`, carries no verifier, and is deleted on the first verify attempt (`verifyCodeAndSignIn.js`), so the code must reach the desktop window unused. The email link opens `/desktop/handoff` in the browser (TFV2-0417b), which opens `tempo-flow://auth?code=…`; this ticket receives that link and loads `https://www.tempoflow.dev/today?code=…` in the main window, where the existing Next.js auth middleware (`apps/web/proxy.ts`, `convexAuthNextjsMiddleware`) exchanges the code and sets the session cookies inside the desktop webview. No token is handled by Rust.

  // apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/deeplink.rs
  use tauri::Url;
  pub const DEEP_LINK_SCHEME: &str = "tempo-flow"; // CFG-048 OPEN: scheme name
  pub const AUTH_HOST: &str = "auth";
  pub const AUTH_CODE_LEN: usize = 32;
  /// Some(nav::web_url("/today?code=<code>")) only when: the link parses as a URL; scheme == DEEP_LINK_SCHEME;
  /// host == AUTH_HOST; path is "" or "/"; the query has exactly one pair, its key is "code", and its value
  /// is AUTH_CODE_LEN ASCII alphanumerics. Otherwise None.
  pub fn auth_redirect(link: &str) -> Option<Url>;
  /// tauri_plugin_deep_link::DeepLinkExt: app.deep_link().get_current() → the first URL whose auth_redirect is Some (errors → None).
  pub fn cold_start_url(app: &tauri::App) -> Option<Url>;

  /// app.deep_link().on_open_url(|event| for each url: if let Some(target) = auth_redirect(url.as_str()) → main window navigate(target), unminimize, show, set_focus).
  pub fn install(app: &tauri::App) -> tauri::Result<()>;
  ```
  Cold start: the redirect URL becomes the window's first URL (`window::create_main(app, initial)`, TFV2-0418a), so the boot page never races it. No user-facing copy; no errors returned (an invalid link is ignored).

  ```tsx
  // apps/web/app/desktop/handoff/page.tsx (server component)
  import type { Metadata } from "next";
  import { DesktopHandoff } from "@/components/desktop/DesktopHandoff";
  import { handoffDeepLink } from "@/lib/desktop/bridge";
  export const metadata: Metadata = { referrer: "no-referrer", robots: { index: false, follow: false } };
  export default async function Page({ searchParams }: { searchParams: Promise<{ code?: string | string[] }> }) {
    const { code } = await searchParams;
    return <DesktopHandoff link={handoffDeepLink(typeof code === "string" ? code : null)} />;
  }
  // apps/web/components/desktop/DesktopHandoff.tsx ("use client")
  import type React from "react";
  export type DesktopHandoffProps = { link: string | null };
  export function DesktopHandoff(props: DesktopHandoffProps): React.JSX.Element;
  ```
  **Markup:** `<main className="tp-page" id="main">` → `<div className="tp-state" data-component="DesktopHandoff" data-state={link ? "opening" : "invalid"}>`. `opening`: `<h1 className="tp-state__title">{openingTitle}</h1>`, `<p className="tp-state__body">{openingBody}</p>`, `<div className="tp-state__actions"><a className="tp-btn tp-btn--primary" href={link} data-testid="desktop-handoff-open">{openButton}</a></div>`, `<p className="tp-state__body tp-small">{closeHint}</p>`; one `useEffect(() => { if (link) window.location.assign(link); }, [link])` guarded by a `useRef` so it runs once. `invalid`: `<h1 className="tp-state__title">{invalidTitle}</h1>`, `<p className="tp-state__body">{invalidBody}</p>`, no link. "Tempo Flow" stays Latin (CONVENTIONS §12).
  **COPY** (`type CopyKey = "openingTitle" | "openingBody" | "openButton" | "closeHint" | "invalidTitle" | "invalidBody"`; `const { lang } = useLocale()`):
  | key | EN | HE |
  |---|---|---|
  | openingTitle | Opening Tempo Flow on this computer… | Tempo Flow נפתח במחשב הזה… |
  | openingBody | If the app doesn't open, use the button. | אם האפליקציה לא נפתחת, אפשר להשתמש בכפתור. |
  | openButton | Open the desktop app | פתיחת האפליקציה במחשב |
  | closeHint | After the app opens, you can close this tab. | אחרי שהאפליקציה נפתחת, אפשר לסגור את הלשונית הזאת. |
  | invalidTitle | This sign-in link doesn't work here. | קישור ההתחברות הזה לא עובד כאן. |
  | invalidBody | Open Tempo Flow on your computer and ask for a new sign-in link. | אפשר לפתוח את Tempo Flow במחשב ולבקש קישור התחברות חדש. |

  ```rust
  // apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/page_cache.rs
  use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
  pub const PAGE_CACHE_MAX_PAGES: usize = 200;
  pub const PAGE_CACHE_BODY_MAX_BYTES: usize = 262_144;
  pub const PAGE_ID_MAX_BYTES: usize = 128;
  pub const STORE_FILE: &str = "pages.json";
  pub const STORE_KEY: &str = "pages";
  pub const READ_ERROR: &str = "Offline pages could not be read";
  pub const SAVE_ERROR: &str = "Offline pages could not be saved";
  pub const ID_ERROR: &str = "Page id is invalid";
  pub const SIZE_ERROR: &str = "Page is too large to keep offline";
  #[derive(Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
  pub struct CachedPageInput { pub id: String, pub title: String, pub body: String, pub updated_at: f64 }
  #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
  pub struct CachedPage { pub id: String, pub title: String, pub body: String, pub updated_at: f64, pub cached_at: f64 }
  #[derive(Serialize, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
  pub struct CachedPageSummary { pub id: String, pub title: String, pub updated_at: f64, pub cached_at: f64 }
  pub trait PageStoreBackend {
      fn read(&self) -> Result<Option<serde_json::Value>, String>;
      fn write(&mut self, pages: &[CachedPage]) -> Result<(), String>;
  }
  /// None or a value that is not an array of CachedPage → empty Vec.
  pub fn parse_stored(value: Option<serde_json::Value>) -> Vec<CachedPage>;
  /// id empty or > PAGE_ID_MAX_BYTES UTF-8 bytes → Err(ID_ERROR); body > PAGE_CACHE_BODY_MAX_BYTES bytes → Err(SIZE_ERROR);
  /// else remove any entry with the same id, put the new one first with cached_at = now_ms, truncate to PAGE_CACHE_MAX_PAGES.
  pub fn insert(pages: Vec<CachedPage>, input: CachedPageInput, now_ms: f64) -> Result<Vec<CachedPage>, String>;
  pub fn summaries(pages: &[CachedPage]) -> Vec<CachedPageSummary>; // same order, body dropped
  pub fn put(backend: &mut impl PageStoreBackend, input: CachedPageInput, now_ms: f64) -> Result<(), String>; // read Err → READ_ERROR; insert; write Err → SAVE_ERROR
  pub fn list(backend: &impl PageStoreBackend) -> Result<Vec<CachedPageSummary>, String>; // read Err → READ_ERROR
  pub fn get(backend: &impl PageStoreBackend, id: &str) -> Result<Option<CachedPage>, String>;
  pub fn clear(backend: &mut impl PageStoreBackend) -> Result<(), String>; // write(&[]) Err → SAVE_ERROR
  pub struct AppPageStore { pub app: tauri::AppHandle } // tauri_plugin_store: app.store(STORE_FILE), get/set STORE_KEY, save
  impl PageStoreBackend for AppPageStore { /* … */ }
  #[tauri::command] pub fn desktop_page_cache_put(app: tauri::AppHandle, page: CachedPageInput) -> Result<(), String>; // now_ms from SystemTime::now() since UNIX_EPOCH
  #[tauri::command] pub fn desktop_page_cache_list(app: tauri::AppHandle) -> Result<Vec<CachedPageSummary>, String>;
  #[tauri::command] pub fn desktop_page_cache_get(app: tauri::AppHandle, id: String) -> Result<Option<CachedPage>, String>;
  #[tauri::command] pub fn desktop_page_cache_clear(app: tauri::AppHandle) -> Result<(), String>;
  ```
  Errors (exact → trigger): `"Offline pages could not be read"` → store read fails; `"Offline pages could not be saved"` → store write fails; `"Page id is invalid"` → empty id or id over 128 bytes; `"Page is too large to keep offline"` → body over 262,144 UTF-8 bytes. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (`tests/page_cache.rs`)
  1. Given `parse_stored(None)` and `parse_stored(Some(json!({"x":1})))` / Then both empty.
  2. Given an empty list / When `insert(input "n1", now 10.0)` / Then one page with `cached_at == 10.0`.
  3. Given pages `[n1, n2]` / When `insert(n2 with title "New", now 20.0)` / Then the list is `[n2 (title "New"), n1]` (no duplicate).
  4. Given 200 pages / When one new page is inserted / Then length is 200, the new page is first and the oldest (last) is gone.
  5. Given a body of exactly 262,144 ASCII bytes / Then `Ok`; given 262,145 bytes, or 87,382 copies of "א" (2 bytes each = 174,764 bytes, under the cap) / Then `Err("Page is too large to keep offline")` for the first and `Ok` for the second.
  6. Given id `""` or a 129-byte id / Then `Err("Page id is invalid")`.
  7. Given a store with `[n1]` / When `list` / Then one summary with no body field (`serde_json::to_value` has keys `cachedAt, id, title, updatedAt` only).
  8. Given a store whose `read` fails / Then `put`, `list` and `get` each return `Err("Offline pages could not be read")`.
  9. Given a store whose `write` fails / Then `put` and `clear` each return `Err("Offline pages could not be saved")`.
  10. Given a store with `[n1, n2]` / When `get("n2")` and `get("zz")` / Then `Some(n2)` and `None`; When `clear` / Then the store holds `[]`.
- **NUMBERS:** cap 200 pages (product value carried from the old TFV2-0421; test 4) · body ≤ 262,144 UTF-8 bytes (= 256 KiB; product bound; test 5; "bytes" per CONVENTIONS §7 H) · worst-case cache size ≈ 200 × 256 KiB = 50 MiB (derived). 10 of 10 tests pass. Latency: n/a (local file).
