  ```ts
  export const APP_SCHEME = "tempo-rhythm";
  export type DeepLink = { kind: "route"; path: string } | { kind: "fallback" } | { kind: "foreign" };
  export function resolveDeepLink(raw: string, hosts: readonly string[]): DeepLink;
  /** A push payload { url } → an in-app path; anything else → "/today". */
  export function routeForPushData(data: unknown): string;
  ```
  `resolveDeepLink` rules: (1) Find the path: `raw` starting with `"/"` → `path = raw` and `source = "path"`; starting with `"tempo-rhythm://"` → `path = "/" + raw.slice(15).replace(/^\/+/, "")`, `source = "scheme"`; starting with `"https://"` → parse with `new URL(raw)` (a throw → `foreign`); `url.hostname.toLowerCase()` in `hosts` (compared lower-case) → `path = url.pathname`, `source = "web"`, else `foreign`; anything else → `foreign`. (2) Cut `path` at the first `?` or `#`; drop one trailing `/` unless the path is `/`. (3) Map: `/today`, `/coach`, `/capture`, `/notifications`, `/enable-push`, `/scan` → `{ kind: "route", path }`; `/notes/<id>` or `/page/<id>` with `id` matching `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/` → `{ kind: "route", path: "/page/<id>" }`. (4) Not mapped: `source === "path"` → `foreign` (Expo Router handles its own paths, so a real route such as `/settings` passes through unchanged); `source` `scheme` or `web` → `fallback`.
  `routeForPushData(data)`: `data` is an object with a string `url` and `resolveDeepLink(url, [])` is a `route` → that path; otherwise `"/today"`. No errors, no copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `"tempo-rhythm://today"` and `"tempo-rhythm:///coach"` with `hosts = []` / Then `{ kind: "route", path: "/today" }` and `{ kind: "route", path: "/coach" }`.
  2. Given `"tempo-rhythm://page/abc_12"` and `"https://www.tempoflow.dev/notes/abc_12?x=1#top"` with `hosts = ["www.tempoflow.dev"]` / Then both `{ kind: "route", path: "/page/abc_12" }`.
  3. Given `"https://evil.test/today"` with `hosts = ["www.tempoflow.dev"]` / Then `{ kind: "foreign" }`; and `"https://WWW.TEMPOFLOW.DEV/today"` / Then `{ kind: "route", path: "/today" }`.
  4. Id length at n and n + 1 (64): given `"tempo-rhythm://page/" + "a".repeat(64)` / Then `{ kind: "route", path: "/page/" + "a".repeat(64) }`; given `"tempo-rhythm://page/" + "a".repeat(65)` and `"tempo-rhythm://notes/../../x"` / Then both `{ kind: "fallback" }`.
  5. Given `"tempo-rhythm://"` and `"https://www.tempoflow.dev/"` (hosts as in 2) / Then both `{ kind: "fallback" }`.
  6. Given `"/settings"` / Then `{ kind: "foreign" }`; and `"/today/"` / Then `{ kind: "route", path: "/today" }`.
  7. Given `"exp+tempi://expo-development-client/?url=http%3A%2F%2F10.0.0.2%3A8081"` and `"not a url"` / Then both `{ kind: "foreign" }`.
  8. Given `routeForPushData({ url: "tempo-rhythm://page/n1" })` / Then `"/page/n1"`; `routeForPushData({ url: "https://x.test/today" })`, `routeForPushData(null)` and `routeForPushData({ url: 5 })` / Then each `"/today"`.
- **NUMBERS:** 8 of 8 cases pass (exact). Note id ≤ 64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]` (case 4 at 64 and 65; Convex ids are 32 lower-case alphanumerics; bound leaves room). Latency: n/a (pure).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // apps/mobile/lib/push-tap.ts
  import * as Notifications from "expo-notifications";
  import { router } from "expo-router";
  import { useEffect } from "react";
  import { routeForPushData } from "./deep-link";
  import { configurePushHandler } from "./push-native";
  /** Renders nothing. Mounted once in the root layout, never on web. */
  export function PushTapRouter(): null {
    const response = Notifications.useLastNotificationResponse();
    useEffect(() => {
      configurePushHandler();
    }, []);
    useEffect(() => {
      if (!response || response.actionIdentifier !== Notifications.DEFAULT_ACTION_IDENTIFIER) return;
      router.push(routeForPushData(response.notification.request.content.data));
    }, [response]);
    return null;
  }
  ```

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // apps/web/app/.well-known/apple-app-site-association/route.ts
  export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
  export function GET(): Response {
    const team = process.env.APPLE_TEAM_ID?.trim();
    if (!team) return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });
    const body = { applinks: { details: [{ appIDs: [`${team}.com.temporhythm.app`], components: [{ "/": "/today" }, { "/": "/coach" }, { "/": "/notes/*" }] }] } };
    return Response.json(body, { headers: { "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=3600" } });
  }
  // apps/web/app/.well-known/assetlinks.json/route.ts
  export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";
  export function GET(): Response {
    const fingerprints = (process.env.ANDROID_CERT_SHA256 ?? "").split(",").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
    if (fingerprints.length === 0) return new Response("Not found", { status: 404 });
    const body = [{ relation: ["delegate_permission/common.handle_all_urls"], target: { namespace: "android_app", package_name: "com.temporhythm.app", sha256_cert_fingerprints: fingerprints } }];
    return Response.json(body, { headers: { "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=3600" } });
  }
  ```
  Env names used (names only): `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `ANDROID_CERT_SHA256` (comma-separated, upload key and Play signing key). No copy, no errors thrown.
- **TESTS:**
  1.   3. Run DONE.

### TFV2-0438a — Calendar file import: `parseIcs` (`convex/lib/ics.ts`)
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent

CONVENTIONS §9 (pure helper file set), §7 E (Convex file names: letters, digits, `_`, `.`), §16 (exact error messages). Today no `.ics` code exists (`grep -rn "VCALENDAR" convex apps packages` prints nothing). Split from old TFV2-0438 (parse and serialize are two exported functions → two tickets).
- **GOAL:** `parseIcs(text, fallbackTimeZone)` turns the text of an `.ics` file into a bounded list of plain events (uid, title, start, end, all-day flag, raw repeat rule, description) without touching the database or the network.
- **SCOPE:** `convex/lib/ics.ts` · test: `convex/lib/ics.test.ts`.

- **STEPS:**

  2. Create `convex/lib/ics.ts` with exactly the SPEC exports (no imports from `convex/server`, `./_generated/*` or any package; only built-ins `TextEncoder` and `Intl`).
  3. Implement the parse algorithm in SPEC "Algorithm", including the private helpers `unfoldLines`, `parseContentLine`, `unescapeText`, `parseIcsDate`, `wallTimeToUtcMs` (not exported).
  4. Create `convex/lib/ics.test.ts` (`bun:test`) with the 10 TESTS cases, inline `.ics` strings only (no fixture files).
  5. Run DONE, then `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint`.

- **EVIDENCE:** the `bun test` summary lines and the typecheck and lint exit codes, pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** expand `RRULE` into occurrences (it is kept as the raw string); write rows or call `ctx`; call `fetch`; add a dependency (no ical library: `package.json` is config lane); throw for a single bad event (it is skipped and counted); name the file with a hyphen; touch `convex/schema.ts`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0438a / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: convex/lib/ics.ts, convex/lib/ics.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–5 with evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // convex/lib/ics.ts
  export const ICS_MAX_BYTES = 1_048_576;   // 1 MiB of UTF-8, product bound
  export const ICS_MAX_EVENTS = 5_000;      // product bound
  export type IcsEvent = {
    uid: string;              // UID, trimmed, non-empty
    title: string;            // SUMMARY unescaped and trimmed; "" when absent
    startsAtMs: number;       // UTC ms
    endsAtMs: number | null;  // DTEND as UTC ms; null when absent
    allDay: boolean;          // true when DTSTART is a DATE (no time part)
    rrule: string | null;     // RRULE value exactly as written; null when absent
    description: string | null; // DESCRIPTION unescaped; null when absent
  };
  export type IcsParseResult = { events: IcsEvent[]; skipped: number; truncated: boolean };
  export function parseIcs(text: string, fallbackTimeZone: string): IcsParseResult;
  ```
  Errors (exact message → trigger), thrown with `new Error(…)` before any event is read:
  - `"iCalendar file is too large"` → `new TextEncoder().encode(text).length > ICS_MAX_BYTES`.
  - `"Unknown time zone"` → `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone: fallbackTimeZone })` throws.
  - `"Not an iCalendar file"` → after unfolding, no line whose name is `BEGIN` (case-insensitive) has the value `VCALENDAR` (case-insensitive).
  **Algorithm:**
  1. `unfoldLines`: split on `/\r\n|\n|\r/`; a line that starts with one space or one tab is joined to the previous line with that first character removed (RFC 5545 §3.1); empty lines are dropped.
  2. `parseContentLine(line)`: name = text before the first `;` or `:` that is outside double quotes, upper-cased; params = `;`-separated `KEY=VALUE` pairs before that first unquoted `:` (keys upper-cased, surrounding double quotes removed from values); value = everything after it. A line with no unquoted `:` is ignored.
  3. Walk the lines. `BEGIN:VEVENT` opens an event; `END:VEVENT` closes it; lines between `BEGIN:VALARM` and `END:VALARM` are ignored; properties outside a VEVENT are ignored. Inside a VEVENT the first occurrence of `UID`, `SUMMARY`, `DESCRIPTION`, `DTSTART`, `DTEND`, `RRULE` is kept; later duplicates are ignored. Other properties are ignored.
  4. `unescapeText(v)` for `SUMMARY`, `DESCRIPTION`, `UID`: `\n` or `\N` → newline, `\,` → `,`, `\;` → `;`, `\\` → `\`, in one left-to-right pass.
  5. `parseIcsDate(value, params, fallbackTimeZone)` → `{ ms: number; allDay: boolean } | null`:
     - `/^\d{8}$/` (or `params.VALUE === "DATE"` with that form) → `{ ms: Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d), allDay: true }`;
     - `/^\d{8}T\d{6}Z$/` → `{ ms: Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d, hh, mm, ss), allDay: false }`;
     - `/^\d{8}T\d{6}$/` → wall time in `params.TZID` when `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone: params.TZID })` does not throw, else in `fallbackTimeZone`, converted by `wallTimeToUtcMs`; `allDay: false`;
     - anything else, or a calendar-invalid date (month 13, day 32, `Date.UTC` round-trip mismatch) → `null`.
  6. `wallTimeToUtcMs(parts, timeZone)`: `guess = Date.UTC(parts)`; `offset(t)` = the difference between `Date.UTC` of `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone, hourCycle: "h23", year: "numeric", month: "2-digit", day: "2-digit", hour: "2-digit", minute: "2-digit", second: "2-digit" }).formatToParts(t)` and `t`; `r = guess - offset(guess)`; if `offset(r) !== offset(guess)` then `r = guess - offset(r)`; return `r`.
  7. On `END:VEVENT`: the event is **skipped** (`skipped += 1`) when `UID` is missing or empty after trim, `DTSTART` is missing or `parseIcsDate` returns `null`, or `DTEND` is present and `parseIcsDate` returns `null` or a value smaller than `startsAtMs`. Otherwise push `{ uid, title, startsAtMs, endsAtMs, allDay, rrule, description }`.
  8. When `events.length === ICS_MAX_EVENTS` and another `BEGIN:VEVENT` starts, stop reading, set `truncated: true` and return (later events are not counted in `skipped`).
  No user-facing copy (the caller maps errors to UI text).
- **TESTS:** (`convex/lib/ics.test.ts`, `bun:test`; every case asserts returned values). Text builders, declared at the top of the test file exactly as here (origin: this ticket, §16 d); "a VEVENT with X, Y" means `cal(vevent(X, Y))`:
  ```ts
  const cal = (...lines: string[]) => ["BEGIN:VCALENDAR", "VERSION:2.0", ...lines, "END:VCALENDAR", ""].join("\r\n");
  const vevent = (...props: string[]) => ["BEGIN:VEVENT", ...props, "END:VEVENT"].join("\r\n");
  const nEvents = (n: number) => cal(...Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => vevent("UID:e" + i, "DTSTART:20261012T080000Z")));
  const HEAD = "BEGIN:VCALENDAR\r\nX-PAD:";
  const TAIL = "\r\nEND:VCALENDAR\r\n";
  const padded = (bytes: number) => HEAD + "a".repeat(bytes - HEAD.length - TAIL.length) + TAIL; // ASCII: length === UTF-8 bytes
  ```
  1. Given one VEVENT with `UID:a1`, `SUMMARY:Dentist`, `DTSTART:20261012T080000Z`, `DTEND:20261012T090000Z` / When `parseIcs(text, "UTC")` / Then `events` equals `[{ uid: "a1", title: "Dentist", startsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12, 8), endsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12, 9), allDay: false, rrule: null, description: null }]`, `skipped` 0, `truncated` false.
  2. Given `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20261012` and `DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20261013` / Then `allDay` true, `startsAtMs` `Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12)`, `endsAtMs` `Date.UTC(2026, 9, 13)`.
  3. Given `DTSTART;TZID=Asia/Jerusalem:20261012T100000` / Then `startsAtMs` equals `Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12, 7)` (UTC+3 in October 2026); and the same line without `TZID` parsed with `fallbackTimeZone` `"Asia/Jerusalem"` gives the same value.
  4. Given `SUMMARY:Lunch\, then walk\nwith Dana` folded over two lines (`SUMMARY:Lunch\, then wa` + CRLF + ` lk\nwith Dana`) / Then `title` is `"Lunch, then walk\nwith Dana"`.
  5. Given `RRULE:FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO` / Then `rrule` is `"FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO"` and exactly one event is returned.
  6. Given three VEVENTs: one without `UID`, one with `DTSTART:2026-10-12`, one valid / Then `events.length` 1 and `skipped` 2.
  7. Given a VEVENT whose `DTEND` is earlier than its `DTSTART` / Then `events` is `[]` and `skipped` 1.
  8. Given a VEVENT containing a `BEGIN:VALARM` … `SUMMARY:Alarm` … `END:VALARM` block before its own `SUMMARY:Meeting` / Then `title` is `"Meeting"`.
  9. Event cap at n and n + 1 (`ICS_MAX_EVENTS` = 5,000): given `nEvents(ICS_MAX_EVENTS)` / Then `events.length` is 5000 and `truncated` is false; given `nEvents(ICS_MAX_EVENTS + 1)` / Then `events.length` is 5000 and `truncated` is true.
  10. Errors: Given `"hello"` / Then `parseIcs` throws `"Not an iCalendar file"`; Given a valid file and `fallbackTimeZone` `"Mars/Base"` / Then it throws `"Unknown time zone"`; size at n and n + 1 (`ICS_MAX_BYTES` = 1,048,576): given `padded(ICS_MAX_BYTES)` / Then it returns `{ events: [], skipped: 0, truncated: false }`; given `padded(ICS_MAX_BYTES + 1)` / Then it throws `"iCalendar file is too large"`.
- **NUMBERS:** File ≤ 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes (`ICS_MAX_BYTES`, product bound; RFC 5545 sets no limit) · events ≤ 5,000 (`ICS_MAX_EVENTS`, product bound) · checked by cases 9–10, each at n and n + 1. Line folding and escaping exact per RFC 5545 §3.1/§3.3.11 (cases 4). Parse latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline; pure CPU, not a gate). 10 of 10 cases pass.
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export type IcsExportEvent = { uid: string; title: string; startsAtMs: number; endsAtMs: number | null; allDay: boolean; description: string | null };
  export function serializeIcs(events: readonly IcsExportEvent[], nowMs: number): string;
  ```
  Error (exact → trigger): `"Too many events"` → `events.length > ICS_MAX_EVENTS` (thrown before any output).
  Output: content lines joined with `"\r\n"` and ending with `"\r\n"`, in this order: `BEGIN:VCALENDAR`, `VERSION:2.0`, `PRODID:-//Tempo Flow//Tempo//EN`, `CALSCALE:GREGORIAN`; then per event, in input order: `BEGIN:VEVENT`, `UID:<escapeText(uid)>`, `DTSTAMP:<formatUtc(nowMs)>`, start line, end line (only when `endsAtMs !== null`), `SUMMARY:<escapeText(title)>`, `DESCRIPTION:<escapeText(description)>` (only when `description !== null`), `END:VEVENT`; then `END:VCALENDAR`.
  - Start/end lines: `allDay` → `DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:<formatDate(ms)>` / `DTEND;VALUE=DATE:<formatDate(ms)>`; else `DTSTART:<formatUtc(ms)>` / `DTEND:<formatUtc(ms)>`.
  - `formatUtc(ms)` → `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` from the UTC fields of `new Date(ms)`; `formatDate(ms)` → `YYYYMMDD` from the UTC fields.
  - `escapeText(s)` → `\` → `\\`, `;` → `\;`, `,` → `\,`, `\r\n` / `\n` / `\r` → `\n` (backslash then letter n), in that order.
  - `foldLine(line)`: when the UTF-8 length of a line exceeds 75 bytes, cut it into pieces so the first piece is ≤ 75 bytes and each continuation piece, written as one space plus its text, is ≤ 75 bytes; never cut inside a multi-byte character; pieces are joined with `"\r\n "`.
  No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (added to `convex/lib/ics.test.ts`)
  11. Given one event `{ uid: "t1", title: "Dentist", startsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12, 8), endsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12, 9), allDay: false, description: null }` and `nowMs` `Date.UTC(2026, 9, 1)` / When `serializeIcs` / Then the output equals exactly `"BEGIN:VCALENDAR\r\nVERSION:2.0\r\nPRODID:-//Tempo Flow//Tempo//EN\r\nCALSCALE:GREGORIAN\r\nBEGIN:VEVENT\r\nUID:t1\r\nDTSTAMP:20261001T000000Z\r\nDTSTART:20261012T080000Z\r\nDTEND:20261012T090000Z\r\nSUMMARY:Dentist\r\nEND:VEVENT\r\nEND:VCALENDAR\r\n"`.
  12. Given `{ uid: "t2", title: "Holiday", startsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12), endsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 13), allDay: true, description: null }` / Then the output contains `"DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20261012\r\n"` and `"DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20261013\r\n"`.
  13. Given the case 11 event with `title` `"Lunch, then walk; bring\nnotes"` / Then the output contains `"SUMMARY:Lunch\\, then walk\\; bring\\nnotes\r\n"`.
  14. Given the case 11 event with `title` `"א".repeat(100)` (100 Hebrew letters, 200 UTF-8 bytes) / Then every line of the output is ≤ 75 UTF-8 bytes, continuation lines start with one space, and `parseIcs(output, "UTC").events[0].title` equals the original title.
  15. Round trip: Given `[{ uid: "r1", title: "Dentist", startsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12, 8), endsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 12, 9), allDay: false, description: null }, { uid: "r2", title: "Holiday", startsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 14), endsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 15), allDay: true, description: null }, { uid: "r3", title: "Review", startsAtMs: Date.UTC(2026, 9, 16, 13, 30), endsAtMs: null, allDay: false, description: "Bring notes, 2 pages; ask Dana\nabout dates" }]` and `nowMs` `Date.UTC(2026, 9, 1)` / When `parseIcs(serializeIcs(events, nowMs), "UTC")` / Then each returned event equals its input plus `rrule: null`, and `skipped` is 0.
  16. ### TFV2-0439 — Calendar sync: pure merge `mergeEvents` (`convex/lib/calendarMerge.ts`)
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent
- **Stage:** F · **Pass:** 1 · **Depends:** none · **Folds-in:** none
- **FOR:** Tempo Flow (`Levidavidspublic/tempo-rhythm`); area `backend` (pure helper); lane per `factory/SLOTS.md`.
- **WHEN:** first.
- **WHY:** PRD §4.12 (two-way calendar sync must not duplicate or silently drop events); PRD F-131 (no silent data loss; confirmation before any external write); CONVENTIONS §7 E (the old name `calendar-merge.ts` has a hyphen, which Convex file names forbid, so the file is `calendarMerge.ts`), §9 (pure helper). The old ticket depended on TFV2-0437; the merge takes plain inputs, so it depends on nothing and is buildable now.
- **GOAL:** `mergeEvents(existing, incoming)` decides, deterministically and without side effects, which incoming calendar events are inserts, updates, deletions or conflicts, so sync never overwrites or duplicates a Tempo-made event and never deletes on absence.
- **SCOPE:** `convex/lib/calendarMerge.ts` · test: `convex/lib/calendarMerge.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `convex/lib/calendarMerge.ts` (new) · `convex/lib/calendarMerge.test.ts` (new). No table, env or route.
- **STEPS:**
  1. Code-map check: `test -e convex/lib/calendarMerge.ts` fails; `grep -rn "mergeEvents" convex` prints nothing.
  2. Create `convex/lib/calendarMerge.ts` with exactly the SPEC exports and rules (no imports).
  3. Create `convex/lib/calendarMerge.test.ts` (`bun:test`) with the 9 TESTS cases.
  4. Run DONE, then `bun run typecheck` and `bun run lint`.
- **DONE:** `bun test convex/lib/calendarMerge.test.ts` → `9 pass`, `0 fail`; `bun run typecheck` → exit 0.
- **EVIDENCE:** the `bun test` summary and the typecheck and lint exit codes, pasted into the PR.
- **DO NOT:** resolve a conflict automatically; delete an existing row because it is missing from `incoming`; read the database or the clock; mutate the input arrays; touch `convex/schema.ts`, `.github/**`, `.env*`.
- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0439 / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: convex/lib/calendarMerge.ts, convex/lib/calendarMerge.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–4 with evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // convex/lib/calendarMerge.ts
  export type MergeExisting = { id: string; externalId: string | null; title: string; startsAtMs: number; endsAtMs: number | null };
  export type MergeIncoming = { externalId: string; title: string; startsAtMs: number; endsAtMs: number | null; deleted: boolean };
  export type MergeConflict = { existingId: string; incoming: MergeIncoming; reason: "same-start-and-title" };
  export type MergeResult = {
    toInsert: MergeIncoming[];
    toUpdate: { id: string; incoming: MergeIncoming }[];
    toDelete: string[];          // existing ids
    conflicts: MergeConflict[];
    duplicates: number;          // incoming items skipped because an earlier item had the same externalId
  };
  export function normalizeTitle(title: string): string; // trim, collapse runs of whitespace to one space, toLocaleLowerCase("en")
  export function mergeEvents(existing: readonly MergeExisting[], incoming: readonly MergeIncoming[]): MergeResult;
  ```
  Rules, applied to each incoming item `i` in input order (all output arrays keep that order):
  1. If an earlier incoming item had the same `externalId` → `duplicates += 1`; skip `i`.
  2. `e` = the first existing row with `e.externalId === i.externalId`. If found: `i.deleted` → push `e.id` to `toDelete`; else if `e.title !== i.title || e.startsAtMs !== i.startsAtMs || e.endsAtMs !== i.endsAtMs` → push `{ id: e.id, incoming: i }` to `toUpdate`; else nothing.
  3. If not found: `i.deleted` → nothing. Else `c` = the first existing row with `c.externalId === null`, `c.startsAtMs === i.startsAtMs`, `normalizeTitle(c.title) === normalizeTitle(i.title)` and `c.id` not already used by an earlier conflict → push `{ existingId: c.id, incoming: i, reason: "same-start-and-title" }` to `conflicts`; else push `i` to `toInsert`.
  Existing rows that no incoming item matches are left alone. No errors are thrown. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (`convex/lib/calendarMerge.test.ts`; each asserts the whole `MergeResult` with `toEqual`). Builders, declared at the top of the test file exactly as here (origin: this ticket, §16 d); `EMPTY` is the result with no work:
  ```ts
  import { type MergeExisting, type MergeIncoming, mergeEvents } from "./calendarMerge";
  const E1: MergeExisting = { id: "e1", externalId: "g1", title: "Gym", startsAtMs: 1000, endsAtMs: 2000 };
  const T1: MergeExisting = { id: "t1", externalId: null, title: "Coffee  with Dana", startsAtMs: 5000, endsAtMs: null };
  const inc = (externalId: string, over: Partial<MergeIncoming> = {}): MergeIncoming => ({ externalId, title: "Gym", startsAtMs: 1000, endsAtMs: 2000, deleted: false, ...over });
  const EMPTY = { toInsert: [], toUpdate: [], toDelete: [], conflicts: [], duplicates: 0 };
  ```
  1. Given existing `[E1]` and incoming `[inc("g1")]` / Then the result equals `EMPTY`.
  2. Given existing `[E1]` and incoming `[inc("g1", { startsAtMs: 1500 })]` / Then the result equals `{ ...EMPTY, toUpdate: [{ id: "e1", incoming: inc("g1", { startsAtMs: 1500 }) }] }`.
  3. Given existing `[]` and incoming `[inc("g2")]` / Then `{ ...EMPTY, toInsert: [inc("g2")] }`.
  4. Given existing `[E1]` and incoming `[inc("g1", { deleted: true })]` / Then `{ ...EMPTY, toDelete: ["e1"] }`.
  5. Given existing `[E1]` and incoming `[inc("g3", { deleted: true })]` / Then `EMPTY`.
  6. Given existing `[T1]` and incoming `[g4]` with `g4 = inc("g4", { title: "coffee with dana", startsAtMs: 5000, endsAtMs: null })` / Then `{ ...EMPTY, conflicts: [{ existingId: "t1", incoming: g4, reason: "same-start-and-title" }] }`.
  7. Given existing `[T1]` and incoming `[g4, g5]` with that `g4` and `g5 = inc("g5", { title: "coffee with dana", startsAtMs: 5000, endsAtMs: null })` / Then `{ ...EMPTY, conflicts: [{ existingId: "t1", incoming: g4, reason: "same-start-and-title" }], toInsert: [g5] }`.
  8. Given existing `[]` and incoming `[inc("g6"), inc("g6", { title: "Swim" })]` / Then `{ ...EMPTY, toInsert: [inc("g6")], duplicates: 1 }`.
  9. Given existing `[E1, T1]` and incoming `[inc("g7")]`, with `structuredClone` copies of both arrays taken before the call / Then the result is `{ ...EMPTY, toInsert: [inc("g7")] }` (`toDelete` empty: no delete on absence) and both input arrays `toEqual` their copies.
- **NUMBERS:** Deterministic and idempotent: running `mergeEvents` on its own no-change output (case 1) yields no work (exact). Never deletes on absence (case 9, exact). 9 of 9 cases pass. Latency: UNKNOWN (pure CPU, not a gate).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.
- **OPEN:** none.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // convex/calendarSync.ts
  import { v } from "convex/values";
  import type { Id } from "./_generated/dataModel";
  import { internalMutation, type MutationCtx } from "./_generated/server";
  import { mergeEvents, type MergeExisting, type MergeIncoming } from "./lib/calendarMerge";

  export const CALENDAR_IMPORT_MAX = 100;        // incoming events per call
  export const CALENDAR_IMPORT_SCAN_MAX = 500;   // Tempo-made rows read for conflict matching
  export const incomingEventValidator = v.object({
    externalId: v.string(),
    title: v.string(),
    startsAtMs: v.number(),
    endsAtMs: v.union(v.number(), v.null()),
    deleted: v.boolean(),
  });
  export type ImportCounts = { inserted: number; updated: number; deleted: number; conflicts: number; duplicates: number };

  export const applyImport = internalMutation({
    args: { userId: v.id("users"), source: v.literal("google"), events: v.array(incomingEventValidator) },
    returns: v.object({ inserted: v.number(), updated: v.number(), deleted: v.number(), conflicts: v.number(), duplicates: v.number() }),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { userId: Id<"users">; source: "google"; events: MergeIncoming[] }): Promise<ImportCounts> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Handler, in order:
  1. `args.events.length > CALENDAR_IMPORT_MAX` → `throw new Error("Too many events in one import")`.
  2. `user = await ctx.db.get(args.userId)`; missing, or `user.deletedAt !== undefined` → `throw new Error("User not found")`.
  3. Existing rows with an outside id: for each distinct `externalId` in `args.events`, `await ctx.db.query("calendarEvents").withIndex("by_userId_externalId", (q) => q.eq("userId", args.userId).eq("externalId", externalId)).first()`; keep it when `deletedAt === undefined`.
  4. Tempo-made rows for conflict matching: when `args.events` is not empty, `minStart` / `maxStart` = min / max `startsAtMs` of the not-deleted incoming events; read `ctx.db.query("calendarEvents").withIndex("by_userId_deletedAt_startsAtMs", (q) => q.eq("userId", args.userId).eq("deletedAt", undefined).gte("startsAtMs", minStart).lt("startsAtMs", maxStart + 1)).take(CALENDAR_IMPORT_SCAN_MAX)` (`lt(max + 1)`, not `lte`, so the test fake from `convex/lib/testFakeCtx.ts`, which supports `eq` / `gte` / `lt`, runs it) and keep rows whose `externalId === undefined`.
  `mergeEvents` (created by TFV2-0439, in `Depends`; `convex/lib/calendarMerge.ts`) has the signature `export function mergeEvents(existing: readonly MergeExisting[], incoming: readonly MergeIncoming[]): MergeResult;` and its full return type, quoted from TFV2-0439:
  ```ts
  export type MergeExisting = { id: string; externalId: string | null; title: string; startsAtMs: number; endsAtMs: number | null };
  export type MergeIncoming = { externalId: string; title: string; startsAtMs: number; endsAtMs: number | null; deleted: boolean };
  export type MergeConflict = { existingId: string; incoming: MergeIncoming; reason: "same-start-and-title" };
  export type MergeResult = {
    toInsert: MergeIncoming[];
    toUpdate: { id: string; incoming: MergeIncoming }[];
    toDelete: string[];          // existing ids
    conflicts: MergeConflict[];
    duplicates: number;          // incoming items skipped because an earlier item had the same externalId
  };
  ```
  The handler destructures `const { toInsert, toUpdate, toDelete, conflicts, duplicates } = mergeEvents(existing, args.events);` and casts each `id` / `existingId` to `Id<"calendarEvents">` before `ctx.db.patch`.
  5. Map rows to `MergeExisting` (`{ id: row._id, externalId: row.externalId ?? null, title: row.title, startsAtMs: row.startsAtMs, endsAtMs: row.endsAtMs ?? null }`) and call `mergeEvents(existing, args.events)`.
  6. `now = Date.now()`. Each `toInsert` item → `ctx.db.insert("calendarEvents", { userId: args.userId, title: item.title.trim(), startsAtMs: item.startsAtMs, ...(item.endsAtMs !== null && item.endsAtMs > item.startsAtMs ? { endsAtMs: item.endsAtMs } : {}), externalId: item.externalId, externalSource: args.source, createdAt: now, updatedAt: now })`. Each `toUpdate` → `ctx.db.patch(id, { title: incoming.title.trim(), startsAtMs: incoming.startsAtMs, endsAtMs: incoming.endsAtMs !== null && incoming.endsAtMs > incoming.startsAtMs ? incoming.endsAtMs : undefined, updatedAt: now })`. Each `toDelete` id → `ctx.db.patch(id, { deletedAt: now, updatedAt: now })`. Conflicts are not written.
  7. Return `{ inserted: toInsert.length, updated: toUpdate.length, deleted: toDelete.length, conflicts: conflicts.length, duplicates }`.
  Errors (exact → trigger): `"Too many events in one import"` → more than 100 events; `"User not found"` → `userId` has no row or the row is soft-deleted. Auth: internal only (no `requireUser`; the caller TFV2-0437b authenticates). Limits: 100 incoming, ≤ 100 index lookups, ≤ 500 Tempo rows scanned.
- **TESTS:** (`convex/calendarSync.test.ts`; `makeFakeCtx("users:1", ["users:2"])`; assert stored rows and the returned counts)
  1. Given no calendar rows / When `run(applyImport, ctx, { userId: "users:1", source: "google", events: [{ externalId: "g1", title: " Gym ", startsAtMs: 1000, endsAtMs: 2000, deleted: false }] })` / Then it returns `{ inserted: 1, updated: 0, deleted: 0, conflicts: 0, duplicates: 0 }` and one `calendarEvents` row has `title: "Gym"`, `endsAtMs: 2000`, `externalId: "g1"`, `externalSource: "google"`.
  2. Given a stored row `{ userId: "users:1", externalId: "g1", externalSource: "google", title: "Gym", startsAtMs: 1000, endsAtMs: 2000, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1 }` / When the import sends `g1` with `startsAtMs: 1500` / Then `updated` is 1 and the row's `startsAtMs` is 1500.
  3. Given that stored row / When the import sends `g1` with `deleted: true` / Then `deleted` is 1, the row has a numeric `deletedAt`, and the row still exists.
  4. Given a stored Tempo row `{ userId: "users:1", title: "Coffee with Dana", startsAtMs: 5000, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1 }` (no `externalId`) / When the import sends `{ externalId: "g4", title: "coffee with dana", startsAtMs: 5000, endsAtMs: null, deleted: false }` / Then `conflicts` is 1, `inserted` is 0, and the Tempo row is unchanged.
  5. Given a stored row `{ userId: "users:2", externalId: "g1", externalSource: "google", title: "Gym", startsAtMs: 1000, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1 }` / When `users:1` imports `{ externalId: "g1", title: "Gym", startsAtMs: 1000, endsAtMs: 2000, deleted: false }` / Then `inserted` is 1 and the `users:2` row is unchanged.
  6. Given no rows and the incoming event `{ externalId: "g6", title: "Call", startsAtMs: 3000, endsAtMs: 3000, deleted: false }` (`endsAtMs` equal to `startsAtMs`) / Then the inserted row has no `endsAtMs` field.
  7. Limit at n and n + 1 (`CALENDAR_IMPORT_MAX` = 100): given 100 incoming events `g0`…`g99` (`{ externalId: "g<i>", title: "E<i>", startsAtMs: 10_000 + i, endsAtMs: null, deleted: false }` for i = 0…99) / Then it returns `inserted: 100`; given the same shape with 101 events (i = 0…100) / Then it rejects with `"Too many events in one import"` and no row was written.
  8. Given `userId` `"users:999"` (no row) / Then it rejects with `"User not found"`.
  9. Scan limit at n and n + 1 (`CALENDAR_IMPORT_SCAN_MAX` = 500; the fake returns index rows in ascending `startsAtMs`): given 500 Tempo rows `{ userId: "users:1", title: "T<i>", startsAtMs: i, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1 }` for i = 1…500 (no `externalId`) / When the import sends `{ externalId: "ga", title: "T1", startsAtMs: 1, endsAtMs: null, deleted: false }` and `{ externalId: "gb", title: "T500", startsAtMs: 500, endsAtMs: null, deleted: false }` / Then it returns `conflicts: 2, inserted: 0`; given 501 such rows (i = 1…501) and the import sends `ga` (`T1` at 1) and `{ externalId: "gb", title: "T501", startsAtMs: 501, endsAtMs: null, deleted: false }` / Then it returns `conflicts: 1, inserted: 1` (row 501 is beyond the 500 read, so it is not matched).
- **NUMBERS:** Incoming events per call ≤ 100 (`CALENDAR_IMPORT_MAX`, product bound; case 7 at 100 and 101). Tempo rows scanned ≤ 500 (`CALENDAR_IMPORT_SCAN_MAX`, product bound; CONVENTIONS §16 bounded reads; case 9 at 500 and 501). p95 latency: UNKNOWN (no measured baseline; CONVENTIONS §20, not a gate). 9 of 9 cases pass.
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // convex/lib/calendarProvider.ts
  import type { MergeIncoming } from "./calendarMerge";
  export const CALENDAR_IMPORT_WINDOW_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000; // next 30 days
  export type CalendarListResult = { status: "ok"; events: MergeIncoming[] } | { status: "unavailable" } | { status: "error" };
  export type CalendarProviderDeps = { now: () => number; listGoogleEvents: (userId: Id<"users">, fromMs: number, toMs: number) => Promise<CalendarListResult> };
  export function defaultCalendarProviderDeps(ctx: ActionCtx): CalendarProviderDeps; // wraps listGoogleEventsViaExecutor
  export async function listGoogleEventsViaExecutor(ctx: ActionCtx, userId: Id<"users">, fromMs: number, toMs: number): Promise<CalendarListResult>;
  // convex/calendarSync.ts
  export async function importGoogleFlow(ctx: ActionCtx, deps: CalendarProviderDeps): Promise<ImportCounts>;
  export const importGoogle = action({
    args: {},
    returns: v.object({ inserted: v.number(), updated: v.number(), deleted: v.number(), conflicts: v.number(), duplicates: v.number() }),
    handler: async (ctx: ActionCtx): Promise<ImportCounts> => importGoogleFlow(ctx, defaultCalendarProviderDeps(ctx)),
  });
  ```
  `currentUserId` (added in this file): `export const currentUserId = internalQuery({ args: {}, returns: v.id("users"), handler: async (ctx: QueryCtx): Promise<Id<"users">> => (await requireUser(ctx))._id })` — the action's identity reaches it through `ctx.runQuery` (the same way `convex/lib/aiGate.ts` runs `approval.assertApprovedForAi`), and `requireUser` throws `"Not authenticated"` / `"User not found"` / `"This account is not active"`.
  `importGoogleFlow`: 1) `userId = await ctx.runQuery(internal.calendarSync.currentUserId, {})` (signed out → `"Not authenticated"` propagates). 2) `from = deps.now()`, `to = from + CALENDAR_IMPORT_WINDOW_MS`; `result = await deps.listGoogleEvents(userId, from, to)`. 3) `status "unavailable"` → `throw new Error("Calendar sync is unavailable")`; `status "error"` → `throw new Error("Calendar sync failed")`. 4) `events = result.events.slice(0, CALENDAR_IMPORT_MAX)`; return `ctx.runMutation(internal.calendarSync.applyImport, { userId, source: "google", events })`.
  `listGoogleEventsViaExecutor`: loads the person's connection material with `internal.connections.secretsForCall` (status other than `"ok"` → `{ status: "unavailable" }`), reserves one call with `internal.connections.reserveCall`, calls the Executor tool fixed by Amit's answer with a 15-second deadline, maps each returned event to `MergeIncoming` (cancelled events → `deleted: true`), records the call with `internal.connections.recordCall`, and returns `{ status: "error" }` on any network, parse or 4xx/5xx failure. It never returns or logs a token.
  Errors (exact → trigger): `"Not authenticated"` → no identity; `"Calendar sync is unavailable"` → no live Executor connection or feature off; `"Calendar sync failed"` → the provider returned an error. No user-facing copy here (a later settings ticket maps these to text).
- **TESTS:** (added to `convex/calendarSync.test.ts`; stub deps)
  9. Given an action ctx over `makeSignedOutCtx()` / When `importGoogleFlow(ctx, stub)` / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"` and the stub's `listGoogleEvents` was not called.
  10. Given a signed-in ctx and a stub returning `{ status: "ok", events: [g1] }` / Then it returns `inserted: 1` and the stub was called with `fromMs = now()` and `toMs = now() + CALENDAR_IMPORT_WINDOW_MS`.
  11. Given a stub returning `{ status: "unavailable" }` / Then it rejects with `"Calendar sync is unavailable"` and no row is written.
  12. Given a stub returning `{ status: "error" }` / Then it rejects with `"Calendar sync failed"`.
  13. Given a stub returning 150 events / Then exactly 100 rows are inserted (`CALENDAR_IMPORT_MAX`).
- **NUMBERS:** Import window 30 days (`CALENDAR_IMPORT_WINDOW_MS`, proposed; Amit to confirm) · one Executor call per import, 15-second deadline (copies `searchExecutorFor`) · ≤ 100 events per import (TFV2-0437a). Executor rate limit `CALLS_PER_HOUR = 30` (code, `convex/connections.ts`). p95 latency: UNKNOWN (outside service; no baseline). 13 of 13 cases pass.
- **GATES:** n/a — OPEN (not buildable until Amit answers).
- **OPEN:** new: Which Executor tool lists Google Calendar events (its name, input arguments and result fields), may that read-only listing run without a per-call approval card even though `convex/lib/connections/policy.ts` today allows only `search` and `describe`, and is a 30-day, manual "Import now" window right (or a scheduled sync, at what interval)? — Amit.

### TFV2-0441a — WhatsApp bridge: export parser `parseWhatsAppExport` (`convex/lib/whatsappExport.ts`)
- **STATUS:** approved-unsent

Precedent: `parseMemoryExport` in `convex/lib/memoryImport.ts` is a pure parser that the web screen imports (`apps/web/lib/you/memory.ts`), so the raw text is parsed in the browser and never reaches Convex. A WhatsApp export has no time zone and its date order (day-first or month-first) depends on the phone's region, so the caller passes the order; the parser never guesses it.
- **GOAL:** A pure function `parseWhatsAppExport(text, dateOrder)` turns an exported WhatsApp chat (Android or iOS text format) into an in-memory list of `{ timestampMs, sender, text }` messages, bounded by exported limits, writing nothing anywhere.
- **SCOPE:** `convex/lib/whatsappExport.ts` · test: `convex/lib/whatsappExport.test.ts`.
- **MUTATES:** `convex/lib/whatsappExport.ts` (new) · `convex/lib/whatsappExport.test.ts` (new). No table, file or network write.
- **STEPS:**

  2. Create `convex/lib/whatsappExport.ts`. First line: `// RAM-ONLY: parses an exported WhatsApp chat in memory; nothing here writes to disk, Convex or the network (HARD_RULES §6.4).` Then `import { utf8ByteLength } from "./memoryImport";` and the exports exactly as SPEC.
  3. Implement `parseWhatsAppExport` with the algorithm in SPEC, in that order.
  4. Create `convex/lib/whatsappExport.test.ts` (`import { describe, expect, test } from "bun:test";`) with exactly the 10 TESTS cases inside `describe("TFV2-0441a parseWhatsAppExport", …)`.

- **REPORT:** `status / ticket: TFV2-0441a / evidence: <DONE output> / changed: convex/lib/whatsappExport.ts, convex/lib/whatsappExport.test.ts / unknowns / notes for ticket sync`; list STEPS 1–5 with evidence.
- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  // RAM-ONLY: parses an exported WhatsApp chat in memory; nothing here writes to disk, Convex or the network (HARD_RULES §6.4).
  import { utf8ByteLength } from "./memoryImport";

  /** Same bound as MAX_HISTORY_IMPORT_BYTES in packages/utils/src/historyImport.ts. */
  export const WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES = 10 * 1024 * 1024;
  /** Same bound as MAX_HISTORY_MESSAGES in packages/utils/src/historyImport.ts. */
  export const WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_MESSAGES = 20_000;
  export type WhatsAppDateOrder = "day-first" | "month-first";
  /** timestampMs is the printed wall-clock time encoded with Date.UTC (no zone conversion). */
  export type WhatsAppMessage = { timestampMs: number; sender: string; text: string };
  export type WhatsAppParseResult = { messages: WhatsAppMessage[]; skippedLines: number; truncated: boolean };
  /** Android: "<a>/<b>/<yy|yyyy>, <h>:<mm>[ am|pm] - <rest>" */
  export const ANDROID_HEADER =
    /^(\d{1,2})\/(\d{1,2})\/(\d{2}|\d{4}), (\d{1,2}):(\d{2})(?:[ \u00A0\u202F]([AaPp])\.?[Mm]\.?)? - (.*)$/;
  /** iOS: "[<a>/<b>/<yy|yyyy>, <h>:<mm>:<ss>[ AM|PM]] <rest>" */
  export const IOS_HEADER =
    /^\[(\d{1,2})\/(\d{1,2})\/(\d{2}|\d{4}), (\d{1,2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})(?:[ \u00A0\u202F]([AaPp])\.?[Mm]\.?)?\] (.*)$/;
  export function parseWhatsAppExport(text: string, dateOrder: WhatsAppDateOrder): WhatsAppParseResult;
  ```
  Algorithm (exact order):
  1. `utf8ByteLength(text) > WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES` → `throw new Error("WhatsApp export is too large")`.
  2. `messages = []`, `skippedLines = 0`, `truncated = false`, `current: WhatsAppMessage | null = null`. Split `text` on `/\r?\n/`. For each raw line, `line = raw.replace(/^[\u200E\u200F\uFEFF]+/, "")` (iOS left-to-right marks and the file's byte-order mark).
  3. Header: `ANDROID_HEADER.exec(line)` (groups a, b, year, hour, minute, am/pm letter, rest; seconds = 0) else `IOS_HEADER.exec(line)` (groups a, b, year, hour, minute, second, am/pm letter, rest).
  4. On a header: `day, month` = `a, b` for `"day-first"` and `b, a` for `"month-first"`; a 2-digit year is `2000 + yy`; with an am/pm letter the hour must be 1–12 and becomes `hour % 12 + (letter is p/P ? 12 : 0)`, without one it must be 0–23; minute and second 0–59; month 1–12; `ms = Date.UTC(year, month - 1, day, hour24, minute, second)` is valid only when `new Date(ms).getUTCDate() === day` and `getUTCMonth() === month - 1`. Invalid → `skippedLines++`, `current = null`, next line. Then `i = rest.indexOf(": ")`; `i <= 0` or `rest.slice(0, i).trim() === ""` (a system line such as a group-created notice) → `skippedLines++`, `current = null`, next line. Otherwise, if `messages.length === WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_MESSAGES` → `truncated = true` and stop reading lines; else push `current = { timestampMs: ms, sender: rest.slice(0, i).trim(), text: rest.slice(i + 2) }`.
  5. Not a header: `current` set → `current.text += "\n" + line` (a multi-line message); `current` null and `line.trim() !== ""` → `skippedLines++`; `current` null and blank → ignored.
  6. After the loop every `message.text = message.text.trim()`. Return `{ messages, skippedLines, truncated }`.
  Errors (exact → trigger): `"WhatsApp export is too large"` → UTF-8 size over 10,485,760 bytes. Nothing else throws. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `"12/03/24, 9:05 am - Dana: Can you call the bank?\n12/03/24, 9:06 pm - Me: I'll call the bank tomorrow"` and `"day-first"` / When parsed / Then `messages` equals `[{ timestampMs: Date.UTC(2024, 2, 12, 9, 5, 0), sender: "Dana", text: "Can you call the bank?" }, { timestampMs: Date.UTC(2024, 2, 12, 21, 6, 0), sender: "Me", text: "I'll call the bank tomorrow" }]`, `skippedLines: 0`, `truncated: false`.
  2. Given the same text and `"month-first"` / Then `messages[0].timestampMs` equals `Date.UTC(2024, 11, 3, 9, 5, 0)` and `messages[1].timestampMs` equals `Date.UTC(2024, 11, 3, 21, 6, 0)`.
  3. Given `"01/01/2024, 00:15 - Dana: a\n1/1/24, 12:30 am - Dana: b\n1/1/24, 12:30 pm - Dana: c"` and `"day-first"` / Then the timestamps are `Date.UTC(2024, 0, 1, 0, 15)`, `Date.UTC(2024, 0, 1, 0, 30)`, `Date.UTC(2024, 0, 1, 12, 30)`.
  4. Given `"\uFEFF\u200E[03/12/2024, 21:06:09] Dana: Buy milk\n[3/12/24, 9:06:09\u202FPM] Dana: Hi"` and `"month-first"` / Then both messages have `timestampMs: Date.UTC(2024, 2, 12, 21, 6, 9)`, `sender: "Dana"`, and texts `"Buy milk"` and `"Hi"`.
  5. Given `"12/03/24, 10:00 - Dana: first\nsecond line\n\nthird line"` and `"day-first"` / Then one message with `text: "first\nsecond line\n\nthird line"`.
  6. Given `"Messages and calls are end-to-end encrypted.\n12/03/24, 09:00 - Dana created group \"Family\"\n12/03/24, 09:01 - Dana: hello"` and `"day-first"` / Then `messages` has one entry (`text: "hello"`) and `skippedLines: 2`.
  7. Given `"31/02/24, 10:00 - Dana: x\nmore"` and `"day-first"` / Then `messages` is `[]` and `skippedLines: 2`; and given `"12/03/24, 13:00 pm - Dana: x"` / Then `messages` is `[]` and `skippedLines: 1`.
  8. Given `"a".repeat(WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES + 1)` / Then it throws `"WhatsApp export is too large"`; given `"א".repeat(WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES / 2 + 1)` (2 bytes each) / Then it throws the same; given `"a".repeat(WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES)` / Then it returns `{ messages: [], skippedLines: 1, truncated: false }`.
  9. Message cap at n and n + 1 (`WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_MESSAGES` = 20,000), lines `"1/1/24, 10:00 - Dana: m" + i` joined with `"\n"`: given `i` 0…19999 (20,000 lines) / Then `messages.length` is `20000` and `truncated` is `false`; given `i` 0…20000 (20,001 lines) / Then `messages.length` is `20000`, `messages[19999].text` is `"m19999"` and `truncated` is `true`.
  10. Given `""` and `"\n\n"` / Then each returns `{ messages: [], skippedLines: 0, truncated: false }`.
- **NUMBERS:** export ≤ 10,485,760 UTF-8 bytes and ≤ 20,000 messages (`WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_BYTES`, `WHATSAPP_EXPORT_MAX_MESSAGES`; source: the existing chat-history bounds in `packages/utils/src/historyImport.ts`; cases 8 and 9 test each at n and n + 1); raw text persisted = 0 bytes (HARD_RULES §6.4; one import only); 10 of 10 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure; no baseline).

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  /** Same value as QUICK_TITLE_MAX in convex/tasks.ts. */
  export const MESSAGE_CANDIDATE_MAX_CHARS = 280;
  export const COMMITMENT_CUES_EN: readonly string[] = [
    "remind me to", "don't forget to", "dont forget to", "i'm going to", "im going to",
    "i need to", "i have to", "i will", "i'll", "need to", "have to",
  ];
  export const COMMITMENT_CUES_HE: readonly string[] = [
    "תזכיר לי", "תזכירי לי", "לא לשכוח", "אני צריך", "אני צריכה", "צריך", "צריכה",
  ];
  export function candidateFromText(text: string): string | null;
  ```
  Algorithm (exact order):
  1. `isCrisisText(text)` → `null`.
  2. `norm = text.replace(/[‘’]/g, "'").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim()`.
  3. For every cue in `[...COMMITMENT_CUES_EN, ...COMMITMENT_CUES_HE]`, build `new RegExp("(^|[\\s,.;:!?\"(])(" + escaped + ")(?=[\\s,.;:!?]|$)", "iu")` (`escaped = cue.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&")`) and run it on `norm`. Of all matches keep the one whose cue starts earliest (`m.index + m[1].length`); on a tie keep the longer cue. No match → `null`.
  4. `rest = norm.slice(start + cue.length).split(/[.!?]/)[0].replace(/[,;:\s]+$/, "").trim()`.
  5. `rest.length < 3` or `!/\p{L}/u.test(rest)` → `null`.
  6. `rest.length > MESSAGE_CANDIDATE_MAX_CHARS` → `rest = rest.slice(0, MESSAGE_CANDIDATE_MAX_CHARS - 1).trimEnd() + "…"`.
  7. Return `rest.charAt(0).toLocaleUpperCase() + rest.slice(1)`.
  Pure; throws nothing; no user-facing copy (the returned sentence is the person's own words).
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `"I'll call the bank tomorrow."` / Then `"Call the bank tomorrow"`.
  2. Given `"ok so I need to renew my passport! lol"` / Then `"Renew my passport"`.
  3. Given `"Can you send the file?"` and `"Thanks!"` / Then each is `null`.
  4. Given `"אני צריכה לקנות חלב מחר"` / Then `"לקנות חלב מחר"`.
  5. Given `"I’ll book the dentist"` (U+2019) / Then `"Book the dentist"`.
  6. Given `"Need to call mom. I'll do it later"` / Then `"Call mom"` (the earliest cue wins; the sentence ends at the full stop).
  7. Given `"I need to end my life"` / Then `null` (crisis text).
  8. Given `"Kneed to stretch"` / Then `null` (a cue inside a word does not match).
  9. Given `"I'll go"` / Then `null` (fewer than 3 characters left).
  10. Given `"I need to " + "a".repeat(400)` / Then the result has length 280, starts with `"Aaa"` and ends with `"…"`.
- **NUMBERS:** candidate ≤ 280 characters (`MESSAGE_CANDIDATE_MAX_CHARS`; source: `QUICK_TITLE_MAX` in `convex/tasks.ts`; tested with 400); crisis text → 0 candidates (PRD §6, fixed list); 10 of 10 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure). Precision/recall of the cue list: UNKNOWN (no labelled set; Amit).

  ```ts
  /** Telegram Bot API: message text is 1–4096 characters. */
  export const TELEGRAM_TEXT_MAX_CHARS = 4096;
  /** A link code is randomBase64Url(16): 22 base64url characters (TFV2-0442c). */
  export const TELEGRAM_LINK_CODE_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}$/;
  export type TelegramIntent =
    | { kind: "crisis" }
    | { kind: "start"; code: string | null }
    | { kind: "add"; title: string }
    | { kind: "suggest"; candidate: string }
    | { kind: "help" };
  export function telegramIntent(text: string): TelegramIntent;
  ```
  Order: `t = text.slice(0, TELEGRAM_TEXT_MAX_CHARS).trim()` → `isCrisisText(t)` → `{ kind: "crisis" }` → `/^\/start(?:@\w+)?(?:\s+(\S+))?$/` matches → `{ kind: "start", code }` where `code` is group 1 when it matches `TELEGRAM_LINK_CODE_PATTERN`, else `null` → `/^\/add(?:@\w+)?(?:\s+([\s\S]*))?$/` matches → `{ kind: "add", title: (group 1 ?? "").replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim() }` (may be `""`) → `t.startsWith("/")` → `{ kind: "help" }` → `c = candidateFromText(t)`; `c !== null` → `{ kind: "suggest", candidate: c }` → `{ kind: "help" }`. Pure; throws nothing; no copy.
- **TESTS:**
  1. Given `"I want to kill myself"` and `"/add I want to kill myself"` / Then each is `{ kind: "crisis" }`.
  2. Given `"/start abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv"` and `"/start@TempoBot abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv"` / Then each is `{ kind: "start", code: "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv" }`.
  3. Given `"/start"`, `"/start bad!"` and `"/start abc"` / Then each is `{ kind: "start", code: null }`.
  4. Given `"/add   Call  the bank "` / Then `{ kind: "add", title: "Call the bank" }`; `"/add@TempoBot Buy milk"` / Then title `"Buy milk"`; `"/add"` / Then title `""`.
  5. Given `"I'll call the bank tomorrow"` / Then `{ kind: "suggest", candidate: "Call the bank tomorrow" }`.
  6. Given `"hello"`, `"/settings"` and `"/addition x"` / Then each is `{ kind: "help" }`.
  7. Given `"a".repeat(4096) + " I'll call mom"` / Then `{ kind: "help" }` (text past 4,096 characters is not read).
- **NUMBERS:** text read ≤ 4,096 characters (Telegram Bot API message limit, https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#sendmessage; tested at 4,096 + suffix); link code 22 characters (16 random bytes, base64url); 7 of 7 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure).

  ```ts
  export const TELEGRAM_LINK_CODE_TTL_MS = 10 * 60_000;
  /** Bound on telegramLinks rows read per person or per chat. */
  export const TELEGRAM_LINK_ROWS_MAX = 10;
  export const createLinkCode = mutation({
    args: {},
    returns: v.object({ code: v.string(), expiresAt: v.number() }),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, _args: Record<string, never>): Promise<{ code: string; expiresAt: number }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Order: `user = await requireUser(ctx)` → `now = Date.now()` → read `telegramLinks` `by_userId_deletedAt` (`userId = user._id`, `deletedAt = undefined`) `.take(TELEGRAM_LINK_ROWS_MAX)`; each row with `chatId === undefined` → `patch(row._id, { codeHash: undefined, codeExpiresAt: undefined, deletedAt: now, updatedAt: now })` → `code = randomBase64Url(16)` → insert `{ userId: user._id, codeHash: await sha256Hex(code), codeExpiresAt: now + TELEGRAM_LINK_CODE_TTL_MS, createdAt: now, updatedAt: now }` → return `{ code, expiresAt: now + TELEGRAM_LINK_CODE_TTL_MS }`.
  Errors (exact → trigger): `"Not authenticated"` → signed out (also `"User not found"` / `"This account is not active"` from `requireUser`, unchanged). No user-facing copy (the settings screen shows the code).
- **TESTS:**

Given user `"users:a"` and no rows / When `createLinkCode({})` runs / Then `code` matches `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{22}$/`, `expiresAt` is `1_600_000`, and the one `telegramLinks` row has `userId: "users:a"`, `codeHash === await sha256Hex(code)`, `codeExpiresAt: 1_600_000`, no `chatId`, and none of its values equals `code`.
  2. Given a first call / When `createLinkCode({})` runs again / Then the first row has `deletedAt: 1_000_000` and `codeHash` undefined, and exactly one live row (no `deletedAt`) remains, holding the new code's hash.
  3. Given a live linked row `{ userId: "users:a", chatId: "42", linkedAt: 1, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1 }` / When `createLinkCode({})` runs / Then that row is unchanged.
  4. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"` and `telegramLinks` is empty.
  5. Given `makeFakeCtx("users:a", ["users:b"])` and a pending row of `"users:b"` / When A calls `createLinkCode({})` / Then B's row is unchanged (other-user case).
- **NUMBERS:** code lifetime 600,000 ms (`TELEGRAM_LINK_CODE_TTL_MS`; same as `CONFIRM_TTL_MS` in `convex/connections.ts`); 16 random bytes = 128 bits per code; ≤ 10 rows read (`TELEGRAM_LINK_ROWS_MAX`); 5 of 5 cases pass. Latency: UNKNOWN (no baseline).

  ```ts
    returns: v.object({ reply: v.string() }),
    handler: async (ctx: MutationCtx, args: { chatId: string; text: string; languageCode?: string }): Promise<{ reply: string }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Order:
  1. `intent = telegramIntent(args.text)`; `now = Date.now()`.
  2. `link` = first `telegramLinks` row on `by_chatId_deletedAt` (`chatId = args.chatId`, `deletedAt = undefined`); `owner = link ? await ctx.db.get(link.userId) : null`; `active = owner !== null && !isInactiveAccount(owner)`.
  3. `lang: TelegramLang` = `active ? (await preferencesFor(ctx, owner._id)).locale : (args.languageCode?.toLowerCase().startsWith("he") ? "he" : "en")`.
  4. Outcome: `crisis` → `{ kind: "crisis" }` (no write). `start`: `code === null` → `link-invalid`; else `row` = first `telegramLinks` on `by_codeHash` (`codeHash = await sha256Hex(code)`); valid only when `row` exists, `row.deletedAt === undefined`, `row.chatId === undefined`, `(row.codeExpiresAt ?? 0) > now`, and `row.userId`'s user exists and is not inactive. Valid → patch `deletedAt: now, updatedAt: now` on every other live row with this `chatId` (`by_chatId_deletedAt`, `.take(TELEGRAM_LINK_ROWS_MAX)`) and on every live row of `row.userId` that has a `chatId` (`by_userId_deletedAt`, `.take(TELEGRAM_LINK_ROWS_MAX)`); then patch `row` with `{ chatId: args.chatId, linkedAt: now, codeHash: undefined, codeExpiresAt: undefined, updatedAt: now }`; outcome `linked` with `lang` = the new owner's `preferencesFor(...).locale`. Invalid → `link-invalid`. `add`: `!active` → `not-linked`; `title === ""` → `add-empty`; `title.length > TELEGRAM_TITLE_MAX` → `too-long`; else `await createTaskForUser(ctx, owner._id, { title })` → `{ kind: "added", title }`. `suggest`: `!active` → `not-linked`; else `{ kind: "suggest", candidate }`. `help`: `!active` → `not-linked`; else `help`.
  5. Return `{ reply: telegramReplyText(outcome, lang) }`.
  Errors: none thrown (every path returns a reply). Known limit: a Telegram retry of an already-applied `/add` adds the task again (no update-id store).

Telegram calls a webhook with each update and sends the header `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` set by `setWebhook` (Bot API, https://core.telegram.org/bots/api#setwebhook). The reply is returned in the webhook response as a `sendMessage` method call (Bot API "Making requests when getting updates"), so Convex never holds the bot token. Pattern: `convex/connectionsHttp.ts` (a one-line `httpAction` over a testable handler). `convex/_generated/api.d.ts` lists modules explicitly and is regenerated only by `convex codegen`, which build lanes may not run, so the handler references the internal mutation with `makeFunctionReference` from `convex/server` (at runtime `internal` is `anyApi`, `convex/_generated/api.js`, so both resolve the same path `telegram:applyUpdate`). Route line per CONVENTIONS §17.
- **GOAL:** `POST /telegram/webhook` accepts only requests carrying the webhook secret, passes private text messages to `telegram.applyUpdate`, and answers with the reply as a `sendMessage` call.

  ```ts
  export const TELEGRAM_SECRET_HEADER = "X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token";
  export type TelegramWebhookDeps = { webhookSecret: string | undefined };
  export function defaultTelegramWebhookDeps(): TelegramWebhookDeps {
    return { webhookSecret: process.env.TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET };
  }
  const applyUpdateRef = makeFunctionReference<
    "mutation",
    { chatId: string; text: string; languageCode?: string },
    { reply: string }
  >("telegram:applyUpdate");
  export async function handleTelegramWebhook(
    ctx: Pick<ActionCtx, "runMutation">,
    request: Request,
    deps: TelegramWebhookDeps,
  ): Promise<Response>;
  export const telegramWebhook = httpAction(async (ctx, request) =>
    handleTelegramWebhook(ctx, request, defaultTelegramWebhookDeps()),
  );
  ```
  `handleTelegramWebhook` order: no `deps.webhookSecret` → `new Response("Telegram is not set up", { status: 503 })` → `request.headers.get(TELEGRAM_SECRET_HEADER) !== deps.webhookSecret` → `new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 })` → `body = await request.json().catch(() => null)`; `message = body?.message`; when `typeof message?.text !== "string"`, `message.chat?.type !== "private"`, or `message.chat.id` is not a number → `new Response("", { status: 200 })` without calling the mutation → `{ reply } = await ctx.runMutation(applyUpdateRef, { chatId: String(message.chat.id), text: message.text.slice(0, TELEGRAM_TEXT_MAX_CHARS), ...(typeof message.from?.language_code === "string" ? { languageCode: message.from.language_code } : {}) })` → `new Response(JSON.stringify({ method: "sendMessage", chat_id: message.chat.id, text: reply }), { status: 200, headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } })`.

  5. Given header `"s"` and body `"not json"`, and separately `{ update_id: 2, edited_message: { text: "x", chat: { id: 42, type: "private" } } }` / Then each is status `200`, body `""`, `calls` empty.

Mirrors `memoryImport.saveReviewed` in `convex/memoryImport.ts`: the browser parses the export (TFV2-0441a) and picks candidates (TFV2-0441c), the person keeps or edits them, and pressing Save sends only the kept sentences here. The ids come back so the screen's Undo can remove exactly this batch with `tasks.remove`. This function takes plain strings, so it does not import the bridge helpers and is buildable now.

  ```ts
  export const MESSAGE_IMPORT_MAX_ITEMS = 200;
  /** Same value as QUICK_TITLE_MAX in convex/tasks.ts. */
  export const MESSAGE_IMPORT_TITLE_MAX = 280;
  export const commitImport = mutation({
    args: { items: v.array(v.string()) },
    returns: v.object({ created: v.number(), skipped: v.number(), taskIds: v.array(v.id("tasks")) }),
    handler: async (
      ctx: MutationCtx,
      args: { items: string[] },
    ): Promise<{ created: number; skipped: number; taskIds: Id<"tasks">[] }> => { … },
  });
  ```
  Order: `user = await requireUser(ctx)` → `args.items.length > MESSAGE_IMPORT_MAX_ITEMS` → throw → `titles = args.items.map((item) => item.replace(/\s+/g, " ").trim())` → any `title.length > MESSAGE_IMPORT_TITLE_MAX` → throw (before any insert, so a batch is all or nothing) → for each title in order: `""` → `skipped++`; `title.toLocaleLowerCase()` already seen in this batch → `skipped++`; else `taskIds.push(await createTaskForUser(ctx, user._id, { title }))` → return `{ created: taskIds.length, skipped, taskIds }`.
  Errors (exact → trigger): `"Not authenticated"` → signed out (`"User not found"` / `"This account is not active"` from `requireUser`, unchanged); `"Save up to 200 tasks at a time."` → more than 200 items; `"Each task can be up to 280 characters."` → any cleaned item over 280 characters. No user-facing copy (the review screen maps these messages).

Given `makeFakeCtx("users:a")` / When `commitImport({ items: ["Call the bank", "Renew passport"] })` / Then `{ created: 2, skipped: 0 }`, `taskIds` has 2 ids, and the two `tasks` rows have `userId: "users:a"`, titles `"Call the bank"` and `"Renew passport"`, `status: "todo"`, `priority: "medium"`, `energy: "medium"`, and `row.dueAt` is `undefined` (`createTaskForUser`, `convex/tasks.ts` line 214, writes `dueAt: args.dueAt`).
  2. Given `items: ["  Call   the bank ", "", "   ", "call the BANK"]` / Then `{ created: 1, skipped: 3 }` and the one row's title is `"Call the bank"`.
  3. Given 201 items `"Task " + i` (i = 0…200) / Then it rejects with `"Save up to 200 tasks at a time."` and `tasks` is empty; given exactly 200 / Then `created: 200`.
  4. Given `["Call the bank", "a".repeat(281)]` / Then it rejects with `"Each task can be up to 280 characters."` and `tasks` is empty; given `["a".repeat(280)]` / Then `created: 1`.
  5. Given `makeSignedOutCtx()` / Then it rejects with `"Not authenticated"` and `tasks` is empty.
  6. Given `makeFakeCtx("users:a", ["users:b"])` and a `"users:b"` task `"Call the bank"` / When A commits `["Call the bank"]` / Then `created: 1`, the new row has `userId: "users:a"`, and B's row is unchanged (other-user case: nothing of B's is read or changed).
  7. Given `items: []` / Then `{ created: 0, skipped: 0, taskIds: [] }`.

  ```ts
  export const COURSE_DEADLINES_MAX = 500;
  /** Same value as QUICK_TITLE_MAX in convex/tasks.ts. */
  export const COURSE_TASK_TITLE_MAX = 280;
  export type CourseDeadline = { externalId: string; courseName: string; title: string; dueAtMs: number; taskTitle: string };
  export function courseDeadlineItems(raw: unknown, nowMs: number): { items: CourseDeadline[]; dropped: number; truncated: boolean };
  ```
  Rules: `!Array.isArray(raw)` → `throw new Error("Course data is not a list")`. Each element must be a non-null object with string `externalId` (trimmed length 1–128), `courseName` (trimmed 1–120), `title` (trimmed 1–200) and `dueAt` (string with `Number.isFinite(Date.parse(dueAt))` and matching `/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}T/`); otherwise `dropped++`. `dueAtMs < nowMs` → `dropped++`. A repeated `externalId` (after trim) → `dropped++` (first kept). `taskTitle = `${courseName}: ${title}``, cut to `COURSE_TASK_TITLE_MAX - 1` characters plus `"…"` when longer than 280. Sort by `dueAtMs` ascending (ties by `externalId`); keep the first 500 and set `truncated` when more remained. Errors (exact → trigger): `"Course data is not a list"` → `raw` not an array. No user-facing copy.

  2. Given one past item (`"2026-10-01T09:00:00Z"`), one with `dueAt: "next week"`, one missing `title`, and one valid item / Then one item and `dropped: 3`.
  3. Given two valid items with `externalId: "x"` / Then one item (the first) and `dropped: 1`.
  4. Given `{ items: [] }` and `null` / Then each throws `"Course data is not a list"`.
  5. Given 501 valid future items / Then 500 items and `truncated: true`.
  6. Given `courseName: "C"` and `title: "t".repeat(200)` plus a 120-character course name item / Then each `taskTitle` is at most 280 characters and the over-long one ends with `"…"`.
- **NUMBERS:** ≤ 500 deadlines per fetch (`COURSE_DEADLINES_MAX`; proposed bound, UNKNOWN real LMS volumes; tested at 501); task title ≤ 280 characters; 6 of 6 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure).

  ```ts
  export const DISPATCH_B_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
  export const DISPATCH_B_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000;
  export type DispatchBAdapter = { run(payload: string, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<{ result: string }> };

  ```
  Order: `timeoutMs` (default `DISPATCH_B_TIMEOUT_MS`) not an integer in `[1, DISPATCH_B_TIMEOUT_MS]` → `throw new Error("Invalid timeout")` → `payload.trim() === ""` → `"Dispatch B payload is empty"` → `new TextEncoder().encode(payload).length > DISPATCH_B_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES` → `"Dispatch B payload is too large"` → create an `AbortController`; race `adapter.run(payload, controller.signal)` against a `setTimeout(timeoutMs)` that calls `controller.abort()` and rejects `"Dispatch B timed out"`; clear the timer when either settles → an adapter rejection, or a resolved value whose `result` is not a string → `"Dispatch B failed"` → return `{ result }`.
  Errors (exact → trigger): `"Invalid timeout"`, `"Dispatch B payload is empty"`, `"Dispatch B payload is too large"`, `"Dispatch B timed out"`, `"Dispatch B failed"` as above. No user-facing copy.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export const LOCAL_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES = 32 * 1024;
  export const LOCAL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS = 8_000;
  export const LOCAL_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS = 120_000;
  export type LocalInferOptions = { maxOutputChars: number; timeoutMs: number };
  export type LocalInferResult = { text: string; truncated: boolean };
  export interface LocalModelRunner {
    /** The loaded model id, or null when nothing is loaded. */
    readonly loadedModelId: string | null;
    load(modelId: string): Promise<void>;
    /** Must stop work when signal aborts. */
    infer(prompt: string, opts: { maxOutputChars: number; signal: AbortSignal }): Promise<string>;
    unload(): Promise<void>;
  }
  export async function inferWithBudget(runner: LocalModelRunner, prompt: string, opts: LocalInferOptions): Promise<LocalInferResult>;
  ```
  Order: `maxOutputChars` not an integer in `[1, LOCAL_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS]` or `timeoutMs` not an integer in `[1, LOCAL_TIMEOUT_MAX_MS]` → `throw new Error("Invalid local model options")` → `runner.loadedModelId === null` → `"Local model not loaded"` → `prompt.trim() === ""` → `"Prompt is empty"` → `new TextEncoder().encode(prompt).length > LOCAL_PROMPT_MAX_BYTES` → `"Prompt too large"` → race `runner.infer(prompt, { maxOutputChars, signal })` against a timer that calls `controller.abort()` and rejects `"Local model timed out"`; clear the timer when either settles; a rejection from `infer` propagates unchanged → `text.length > maxOutputChars` → `{ text: text.slice(0, maxOutputChars), truncated: true }`, else `{ text, truncated: false }`.
  Errors (exact → trigger): the five messages above. No user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (helper declared at the top of the test file exactly as here (origin: this ticket, §16 d); "a loaded fake whose `infer` resolves X" is `fakeRunner(async () => X)`):
  ```ts
  function fakeRunner(infer: LocalModelRunner["infer"], loadedModelId: string | null = "m1") {
    const calls: { prompt: string; opts: { maxOutputChars: number; signal: AbortSignal } }[] = [];
    const runner: LocalModelRunner = {
      loadedModelId,
      load: async () => {},
      unload: async () => {},
      infer: (prompt, opts) => {
        calls.push({ prompt, opts });
        return infer(prompt, opts);
      },
    };
    return { runner, calls };
  }
  ```
  1. Given a loaded fake whose `infer` resolves `"hello"` / When `inferWithBudget(runner, "hi", { maxOutputChars: 100, timeoutMs: 1000 })` / Then `{ text: "hello", truncated: false }` and `calls[0].opts.maxOutputChars` is `100`.
  2. Given `infer` resolving `"abcdefghij"` and `maxOutputChars: 4` / Then `{ text: "abcd", truncated: true }`.
  3. Given `fakeRunner(async () => "x", null)` / Then it rejects with `"Local model not loaded"` and `calls` is empty.
  4. Given prompt `"   "` / Then `"Prompt is empty"`.
  5. Given `"a".repeat(32_769)` and `"א".repeat(16_385)` / Then each rejects with `"Prompt too large"`; `"a".repeat(32_768)` reaches `infer`.
  6. Given `fakeRunner(() => new Promise<string>(() => {}))` (never resolves) and `timeoutMs: 20` / Then it rejects with `"Local model timed out"` and `calls[0].opts.signal.aborted` is `true`.
  7. Option bounds at both ends: given a loaded fake resolving `"ok"` and `{ maxOutputChars: 8_000, timeoutMs: 120_000 }`, and separately `{ maxOutputChars: 1, timeoutMs: 1_000 }` / Then the first resolves `{ text: "ok", truncated: false }` and the second `{ text: "o", truncated: true }`; given `maxOutputChars` `0`, `8_001` or `1.5`, or `timeoutMs` `0` or `120_001` / Then each rejects with `"Invalid local model options"`.
  8. Given `infer` rejecting `new Error("engine crashed")` / Then it rejects with `"engine crashed"`.
- **NUMBERS:** prompt ≤ 32,768 UTF-8 bytes, output ≤ 8,000 characters, deadline ≤ 120,000 ms (proposed engineering bounds; the real limits depend on the unchosen engine and model — UNKNOWN; each tested at n and n + 1, cases 5 and 7); 8 of 8 cases pass. On-device latency: UNKNOWN (device-dependent).

- **SCOPE:** `packages/utils/src/local-model-state.ts` · test: `packages/utils/src/local-model-state.test.ts`.

- **SPEC:**
  ```ts
  export type LocalModelFailure = "network" | "checksum" | "storage";
  export type LocalModelState =
    | { status: "none" }
    | { status: "downloading"; modelId: string; version: string; receivedBytes: number; totalBytes: number }
    | { status: "ready"; modelId: string; version: string }
    | { status: "failed"; modelId: string; version: string; reason: LocalModelFailure };
  export type LocalModelEvent =
    | { type: "start"; modelId: string; version: string; totalBytes: number }
    | { type: "progress"; receivedBytes: number }
    | { type: "verified" }
    | { type: "fail"; reason: LocalModelFailure }
    | { type: "remove" };
  export const LOCAL_MODEL_INITIAL_STATE: LocalModelState = { status: "none" };
  export function nextLocalModelState(state: LocalModelState, event: LocalModelEvent): LocalModelState;
  ```
  Transitions (anything not listed returns the same `state` object):
  - `start` from `none`, `ready` or `failed`, with `totalBytes` a positive integer and non-empty `modelId`/`version` → `{ status: "downloading", modelId, version, receivedBytes: 0, totalBytes }`.
  - `progress` from `downloading` → same with `receivedBytes = Math.min(totalBytes, Math.max(state.receivedBytes, Math.floor(event.receivedBytes)))` (never goes back).
  - `verified` from `downloading` with `receivedBytes === totalBytes` → `{ status: "ready", modelId, version }`.
  - `fail` from `downloading` → `{ status: "failed", modelId, version, reason }`.
  - `remove` from any state → `{ status: "none" }`.
  Pure; throws nothing; no user-facing copy.
- **TESTS:** (states and events are written in the test file exactly as here (origin: this ticket, §16 d); "downloading r of 1000" is `dl(r)`, `READY` is `{ status: "ready", modelId: "m1", version: "1" }`; `start (a, b, n)` is `{ type: "start", modelId: a, version: b, totalBytes: n }`; `progress n` is `{ type: "progress", receivedBytes: n }`):
  `const dl = (receivedBytes: number): LocalModelState => ({ status: "downloading", modelId: "m1", version: "1", receivedBytes, totalBytes: 1000 });`
  1. Given `LOCAL_MODEL_INITIAL_STATE` and `start` (`"m1"`, `"1"`, `1000`) / Then `{ status: "downloading", modelId: "m1", version: "1", receivedBytes: 0, totalBytes: 1000 }`.
  2. Given downloading at 0 of 1000 / When `progress` 100, then 50, then 2000 / Then `receivedBytes` is 100, then 100, then 1000.
  3. Given downloading 1000 of 1000 / When `verified` / Then `{ status: "ready", modelId: "m1", version: "1" }`; given 500 of 1000 / Then the same object is returned (`toBe`).
  4. Given downloading / When `fail` `"checksum"` / Then `{ status: "failed", modelId: "m1", version: "1", reason: "checksum" }`; given `none` and `fail` / Then the same object.
  5. Given `ready` and given `downloading` / When `remove` / Then each is `{ status: "none" }`.
  6. Given `ready` (`"m1"`, `"1"`) / When `start` (`"m1"`, `"2"`, 500) / Then downloading version `"2"` at 0 of 500; given `downloading` / When `start` / Then the same object.
  7. Given `none` / When `start` with `totalBytes` `0` or `1.5`, or `modelId: ""` / Then the same object each time.
  8. Given `none` / When `progress` 10 / Then the same object.
- **NUMBERS:** 4 states, 5 events; `receivedBytes` never decreases and never exceeds `totalBytes` (tested); 8 of 8 cases pass. Latency: n/a (pure).
- **GATES:** 1 Build/typecheck/lint · 2 own TESTS green · 3 NUMBERS in range · 4 Google style formatting/naming · 5 secret + forbidden-tech scan · 6 scope guard · 7 config guard · 8 never weaken/skip/lower/delete a check · 9 Jev judge (~typesafe/jev-latest): instruction-following, formatting, naming, clean code each >= 0.85; a massive violation fails · 10 Process check: REPORT lists every STEP and DONE item with evidence; a missing item fails.

  ```ts
  /** Label the UI shows beside a local answer. */
  export const OFFLINE_REPLY_LABEL = { en: "Offline answer (on your device).", he: "תשובה לא מקוונת (במכשיר שלך)." } as const;
  export type OfflineCoachReply =
    | { kind: "crisis" }
    | { kind: "local"; text: string; truncated: boolean; modelId: string }
    | { kind: "unavailable"; reason: "no-model" | "timed-out" | "failed" };
  export type OfflineCoachDeps = {
    runner: LocalModelRunner;
    localModel: LocalModelState;
    isCrisis: (text: string) => boolean;
    dial: number;
    timeoutMs?: number;
  };
  export async function offlineCoachReply(message: string, deps: OfflineCoachDeps): Promise<OfflineCoachReply>;
  ```

Match tone accordingly.\n\nPerson: ${message.trim()}`` → `inferWithBudget(runner, prompt, { maxOutputChars: OFFLINE_COACH_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS, timeoutMs: deps.timeoutMs ?? OFFLINE_COACH_TIMEOUT_MS })` → success `{ kind: "local", text, truncated, modelId: localModel.modelId }`; error message `"Local model timed out"` → `{ kind: "unavailable", reason: "timed-out" }`; any other error → `{ kind: "unavailable", reason: "failed" }`. Never throws.
  Copy: `OFFLINE_REPLY_LABEL` — EN: "Offline answer (on your device)." / HE: "תשובה לא מקוונת (במכשיר שלך)." (the UI renders it; the prompt text is model-facing and English only).

  2. Given `localModel: { status: "downloading", … }` / Then `{ kind: "unavailable", reason: "no-model" }` and `infer` was not called.
  3. Given a ready state for `"m1"` and an unloaded stub, `dial: 5` / When `offlineCoachReply("  I feel stuck  ", deps)` / Then `load` was called once with `"m1"` and the result is `{ kind: "local", modelId: "m1", truncated: false }` with `text` starting `"[stub:m1] You are Tempo's coach"` and containing `"Current accountability dial: 5 / 10."` and ending `"Person: I feel stuck"`.
  4. Given `createStubRunner({ delayMs: 1000 })` and `timeoutMs: 20` / Then `{ kind: "unavailable", reason: "timed-out" }`.
  5. Given `createStubRunner({ failLoadFor: ["m1"] })` / Then `{ kind: "unavailable", reason: "failed" }` and `infer` was not called.
  6. Given a message of 2,000 characters / Then `kind: "local"`, `truncated: true` and `text.length` is `1200`.
  7. Given `dial: 14` and `dial: -3` / Then the texts contain `"Current accountability dial: 10 / 10."` and `"Current accountability dial: 0 / 10."`.
